Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.
n4bece2b3c98a: Nanoplastics are emerging stressors that perturb host physiology across the gut–immune–brain continuum, yet scalable interventions remain limited. Here, we engineer ZG@EcN@HA, a biohybrid living system created by vacuum-assisted intracellular loading of zinc gluconate into Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) followed by an outer hyaluronic acid (HA) shell. This architecture preserves probiotic culturability under gastric challenge and supports sustained zinc availability in intestinal conditions. In zebrafish chronically exposed to polystyrene nanoplastics, we observe reproducible neurobehavioral impairment coupled with inflammatory activation, redox imbalance, barrier stress, neurotransmitter dysregulation, and multiorgan histopathology. ZG@EcN@HA yields the most coherent rescue compared with single-component controls, restoring behavioral outputs and realigning immune–redox–neurochemical readouts. ASV-based profiling shows recovery of microbial diversity and a shift toward a control-like community structure, including reduced dominance of inflammation-linked taxa. Intestinal transcriptomics and integrative correlation analyses further support normalization of barrier/metabolic programs and attenuation of innate inflammatory signaling. Together, the data identify a materials-enabled strategy for microbiota–gut–brain protection against chronic nanoplastic stress.
n8d4aa5700958: Lead halide perovskite solar cells have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation photovoltaics; nevertheless, fabrication of the perovskite photoactive layer remains highly intricate with film formation strongly modulated by various processing and environmental factors. Here, we report an environment-controlled, robot-assisted platform for automated thin-film fabrication designed to quantify and visualize perovskite crystallization in situ. Beyond precise control of each processing step, the system captures dynamic phenomena spanning subsecond color evolution and millisecond antisolvent droplet behavior while simultaneously recording slower environmental parameters (temperature, humidity/moisture, and concentrations of oxygen and volatile organic compounds). For optoelectronic assessment, we implemented time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) measurements together with photoluminescence intensity quantification by using a complementary automated evaluation system. By combining machine-learning regression with SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) analysis, we identify the environmental parameters that most impact film properties and propose a feedback strategy to refine data and extract precise effects of process factors. A comparative study of a two-cation perovskite, (FAPbI3)0.87(MAPbBr3)0.13, and a three-cation perovskite, FA0.85MA0.10Cs0.05PbI3, further reveals markedly different sensitivities to environmental factors (FA, formamidinium; MA, methylammonium), in particular, temperature and resultant phase transition kinetics during thermal annealing. Based on the ML analysis and feedback, we tuned the antisolvent droplet velocity and obtained the maximized power conversion efficiency of 24.4%. Notably, this manual device fabrication was consistent with the results obtained by the automated system. This work establishes a practical route to stable, quantitative, and mechanistically informed investigation of solution-processed photovoltaic films.
nb60e8c4b14d9: Despite substantial progress in optoelectronic applications, lead–halide perovskites remain underperforming in field-effect transistors (FETs) due to multiphase instability, ion migration, and grain boundary scattering. Here, a dual-ion co-incorporation strategy was applied to CsxFA1–xPbI3–yBry single crystals. By systematically mapping a phase stability diagram, we pinpoint an optimal stoichiometry of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.7Br0.3 that integrates phase stability engineering with atomic-level ion confinement. Structural analysis reveals that 10% Cs+/Br– co-incorporation induces strain-relaxed lattice contraction (−1.23% along the a-axis relative to FAPbI3) and reinforces Pb–I bonds via octahedral distortion. This yields superior crystallinity (FWHM = 0.04°) and reduced I– migration, thereby enabling the investigation of FET and gated Hall effect carrier mobilities as functions of temperature. Consequently, champion two-terminal FET devices exhibit an electron mobility of 25.1 cm2 V–1 s–1 at room temperature, which increases to 126 cm2 V–1 s–1 at 120 K. Furthermore, high-resolution four-terminal measurements on a single crystal quantify and correct for contact-resistance effects, validating the relationship: Hall mobility (μHall) > linear regime mobility (μlin) > saturation regime mobility (μsat) with values of 89, 79.2, and 71.6 cm2 V–1 s–1, respectively. These findings collectively elucidate intrinsic band-like electron transport behavior in lead–halide perovskite single crystals, distinguishing it from hopping transport in organic semiconductors. By achieving a defect-minimized lattice, this compositional engineering paradigm overcomes the mobility bottleneck in perovskite FETs, facilitating the transition from photoelectronic applications to FET integration.
ne59a629dde2f: Piezocatalysis has emerged as a promising tumor therapeutic strategy because it enables oxygen-independent generation of multiple reactive oxygen species (ROS) with deep tissue penetration. However, the piezocatalytic efficiency of piezoelectric nanomaterials remains constrained by limited lattice distortion, low carrier separation efficiency, and insufficient catalytic active sites. Herein, we report the centrosymmetry breaking of cobalt–vanadium-layered double hydroxide (CoV-LDH) nanosheets via nitrogen doping for efficient ultrasound (US)-mediated piezocatalytic tumor therapy. Owing to the nitrogen doping-induced disruption of the centrosymmetric structure and lattice distortion in CoV-LDH, nitrogen-doped CoV-LDH (N-CoV-LDH) achieves an ultrahigh piezoelectric coefficient of 89.4 pm·V–1, which is superior to that of previously reported piezocatalytic nanomaterials. Moreover, nitrogen doping introduces an unsaturated coordination environment, significantly promoting the adsorption and activation of O2 (Eads = −2.63 eV) and H2O (Eads = −2.37 eV), thereby enhancing piezocatalytic redox reaction kinetics (k > 1.1 × 103 min–1·g–1). Consequently, under low-power US stimulation (0.15 W·cm–2), N-CoV-LDH nanosheets exhibit markedly enhanced ROS generation efficiency, including that of hydroxyl radicals (·OH), superoxide anions (·O2–), and singlet oxygen (1O2). This robust piezocatalytic ROS generation induces tumor cell apoptosis and immunogenic cell death, thereby activating an antitumor immune response characterized by dendritic cell maturation, M1 macrophage polarization, and T cell activation. Ultimately, N-CoV-LDH-mediated piezocatalytic therapy achieves suppression rates of 97.78% for primary tumors and 87.67% for metastatic tumors, establishing an efficient therapeutic paradigm for suppressing tumor metastasis and recurrence.
n1a48d6591244: On-surface Ullmann-type coupling has been widely employed for constructing atomically precise carbon-based nanostructures, yet its implementation remains largely restricted to metal substrates, where strong molecule–substrate interactions perturb intrinsic electronic properties and hinder further device integration. Extending on-surface reaction to chemically inert surfaces such as highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG) is fundamentally challenged by the competition between reaction activation and molecule desorption under ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) conditions. Here, we demonstrate classical Ullmann coupling on HOPG catalyzed by exogenous copper (Cu) atoms. Two brominated precursors, 2,4,6-tris(4-bromophenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (pTBPT) and 5,10,15,20-tetra(4-bromophenyl) porphine (TBrPP), are employed to investigate how exogenous Cu regulates the critical competition between molecular desorption and reaction activation. For pTBPT, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the formation of uniform and well-ordered oligomeric structures at 350 °C, whereas in the absence of Cu, molecules desorb without reaction. Synchrotron radiation X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (SR-XPS) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further indicate that Cu atoms simultaneously promote molecular anchoring and reduce the activation barrier for dehalogenative coupling. As a complementary system, STM and XPS analysis of TBrPP reveals a critical competition between molecular desorption and dehalogenative coupling. While HR-XPS reveals in situ metalation at room temperature, STM imaging confirms that complete molecular desorption occurs at 200 °C, preventing subsequent dehalogenative coupling. These findings provide mechanistic insights into how transition metal mediates the interplay between surface reaction and desorption, while offering a strategy for the fabrication of structurally defined covalent nanostructures on electronically decoupled platforms.
nc9cfd8d91eab: Unraveling the spatial distribution and energy dissipation of high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) is essential for advancing nanoacoustic architectures and probing low-dimensional wave–matter interactions. However, visualizing these dynamics at the subwavelength scale remains challenging due to the optical diffraction limit and severe topographic artifacts, such as surface defects and roughness, in scanning probe measurements. Here, we establish scanning thermal microscopy (SThM) as a robust metrological paradigm to map nanoscale energy dissipation and resolve complex acoustic wavefields through their localized thermal signatures. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate how microgeometries sculpt the acoustic energy landscape and enable quantitative extraction of wave scattering parameters. Furthermore, by interrogating the h-BN/LiNbO3 van der Waals (vdW) interface, we capture localized temperature signatures of interfacial energy exchange. We observe anomalous nonlinear thermal scaling at the 2D heterointerface, consistent with the intrinsic nonlinear damping of the 2D heterostructure. This work highlights the capability of SThM to probe acoustic energy dissipation, establishing a diagnostic framework for subwavelength acoustic wavefields and heterogeneously integrated devices.
n7170a773355c: Y-doped Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 demonstrated feasible field-induced ferroelectric properties for capacitor dielectrics in dynamic random access memory (DRAM) by stepwise cycling, which enabled low-voltage charge boosting. However, practical implementation remains limited by high cycling stress and leakage current density (J) degradation. This study reported a Y-doped ZrO2/HfO2/ZrO2 nanolaminate with middle-inserted and top-inserted Y2O3 layers, enabling low-voltage charge boosting with substantially decreased stepwise cycling stress. This effect arose from a more uniform distribution of oxygen-vacancy-dopant complexes, thereby decreasing the energy barrier for the tetragonal-to-polar orthorhombic phase transition. The middle-inserted Y2O3 layer underwent substitutional diffusion, stabilized the tetragonal phase and suppressed J by acceptor doping. In contrast, the top-inserted Y2O3 layer displayed limited bulk diffusion, resulting in minimal lattice strain and phase change, but further suppressed J. Consequently, a 5.2 nm-thick film achieved an ultralow equivalent oxide thickness of ∼0.26 nm while satisfying the DRAM J criterion (J < 10–7 A cm–2 at ±0.8 V), outperforming all previously reported DRAM dielectrics.
n15c2dfe8cc87: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are highly promising for grid-scale energy storage, yet their practical viability is severely plagued by the polyiodides shuttle effect and sluggish liquid–solid conversion kinetics, which fundamentally arise from the contradictory energetic demands between soluble intermediate confinement and solid-product desorption. Herein, we rationally construct a dual-facet spinel cobalt oxide to precisely decouple these competing interfacial behaviors. By regulating the proportional exposure of strongly coordinating (100) and weakly coordinating (111) facets, a tailored surface microenvironment is constructed that effectively circumvents the inherent thermodynamic trade-off, breaking the single adsorption limitation intrinsic to uniform catalysts. In situ iodine L3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and three-dimensional synchrotron-based nanocomputed tomography reveal that this specific facet modulation substantially reduces the activation barrier for rate-determining polyiodides oxidation, facilitating spatially uniform solid-iodine deposition. Driven by these structural advantages, the assembled Zn–I2 batteries with c/o-Co3O4 deliver a high specific capacity of 161.1 mAh g–1 at 16 A g–1 and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.00055% per cycle after 50,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Furthermore, the batteries also exhibit a broad operational temperature ranging from −30 to 60 °C, highlighting the strong potential for practical applications. This work provides a perspective on facet engineering for achieving wide-temperature-tolerant aqueous iodine storage.
naac5557f2b69: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and cost-effective platform for electrochemical energy storage, yet their practical operation remains limited by water-driven parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous Zn deposition. Here, we report a molecule-crowding strategy that programs zinc/sodium trifluoroacetate (Zn(TFA)2/NaTFA) aqueous electrolytes into an anion-rich nanoclustered solvation environment. The balanced affinity of TFA– toward Zn2+ and H2O promotes Zn2+–TFA– association and drives the evolution from water-rich local coordination toward abundant contact ion pairs, ion aggregates, and interconnected multi-ion nanoclusters. Spectroscopic characterization, X-ray scattering, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal reconstructed Zn2+ coordination, extended ion-associated correlations, and reorganization of the water hydrogen-bonding environment, accompanied by reduced water activity. The nanocluster electrolyte suppresses hydrogen evolution and Zn corrosion and promotes more uniform Zn deposition. The optimized nanocluster electrolyte sustains Zn||Zn cycling for over 2100 h, enables Zn||Cu cells to operate for more than 3000 h with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.4%, and affords Zn||Na2V6O16·3H2O full cells with 82.4% capacity retention after 30,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. These results show that balanced anion interactions and molecular crowding regulate ion association and the water hydrogen-bonding environment, contributing to improved Zn reversibility and cycling stability.
n6ba7d00e077a: Despite extensive studies on cycloalkane and cycloalkene dehydrogenation for liquid organic hydrogen carrier applications, the mechanisms governing selective H2 release under mild conditions remain poorly understood. Here, subnanometer CuxPdy pentamer clusters supported on ZrO2 represent a highly active and selective class of low-temperature dehydrogenation catalysts. Pd5 exhibits the highest benzene and molecular H2 formation rates from dehydrogenation of cyclohexene, followed by Cu2Pd3 and Cu3Pd2, whereas Cu5 is inactive. All active catalysts favored H2 over H2O as the hydrogen-containing product and completely suppressed combustion pathways, with no detectable CO2 formation. Oxygen-lean conditions further favored H2 formation across all active catalysts, with H2 selectivity exceeding 99% for Pd5. Kinetic analysis of Cu3Pd2 reveals positive fractional apparent orders in both C6H10 and O2 and an effective apparent activation energy of approximately 66 kJ·mol–1, while reactant composition and temperature systematically control H2/H2O branching. In situ XPS and in situ GIWAXS reveal that catalytic activity and cluster stability arise from the interplay of atomic composition, electronic structure, metal–oxygen interactions, and the chemical environment, with Cu exhibiting a composition-sensitive redox response and Pd-containing clusters accommodating oxygen while retaining electronically active Pd-derived states near the Fermi level. DFT/MLIP free-energy calculations identify kinetically accessible O-assisted first C–H activation pathways involving H transfer to cluster-bound O, with barriers strongly dependent on cluster composition and O configuration. These findings establish an ensemble-based structure–activity framework for controlling dehydrogenation pathways and provide design principles for catalysts that efficiently promote selective hydrogen release suitable for hydrogen carrier applications.
n24243f1e5fc9: Amorphous solid electrolytes offer opportunities for fast ion transport, yet the structural origins governing their performance remain difficult to resolve due to the absence of long-range order. While mixed-anion strategies have recently emerged to improve ion transport in sodium halide electrolytes, how sulfur incorporation modifies the local structure and Na+ transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a series of xNa2S-TaCl5 mixed anion solid electrolytes to elucidate the impact of sulfur on the structure and Na+ transport. Structural analyses reveal that sulfur incorporation reconstructs the connectivity of Ta-centered polyhedra while progressively disrupting the long-range crystalline ordering to form an amorphous framework. More importantly, neutron pair distribution function analysis reveals the sulfur-induced reconstruction of the local Ta-centered structure, with the emergence of coexisting edge-sharing- and corner-sharing-like motifs from the isolated polyhedra in crystalline NaTaCl6. Simulations further show that sulfur shifts the local polyhedral connectivity toward a larger proportion of edge-sharing configurations relative to the O-containing analogue. Matched-composition machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) comparing O- and S-containing amorphous models suggest that sulfur weakens Na-anion binding, shortens Na–anion residence times, and lowers the barrier for Na+ migration relative to the O analogue. As a result, the optimized composition achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 3.25 mS cm–1 with a low activation energy of 0.28 eV. When evaluated in all-solid-state sodium batteries with an uncoated NaNi1/3Mn1/3Fe1/3O2 cathode, the cell delivers a discharge capacity of 112 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles (82.6% retention) with a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.8%, demonstrating stable interfacial compatibility with uncoated layered oxide cathodes.
n8e3bc553562b: Redox-responsive prodrug nanodelivery systems hold immense promise in cancer therapy, offering advantages of improved pharmacokinetics, enhanced tumor selectivity, and increased safety. However, compared with standard therapeutic formulations, prodrug nanodelivery systems fail to yield superior antitumor efficacy at equivalent doses, attributable to inadequate drug activation and intratumoral accumulation. Herein, the three-in-one drug-release module, comprising an α-disulfide bond, an ethylene glycol moiety, and a short carbon chain, was covalently linked to paclitaxel (PTX) to construct three prodrug nanoassemblies (PSBA10 NPs, PSBA12 NPs, PSBA14 NPs). Notably, PSBA10 NPs, which possessed the shortest carbon chain, exhibited hypersensitive redox-responsive drug release and potentiated antitumor efficacy. Although PSBA10 NPs exhibited better safety than paclitaxel solution (Taxol) at equivalent doses, superior efficacy remained unattainable. Interestingly, a temporal-dose-regulated glutathione (GSH) gradient across the liver-blood-tumor axis increased the intratumoral accumulation of PSBA10 NPs by approximately 3-fold, resulting in pronounced antitumor efficacy superior to Taxol. This transient depletion of GSH in the liver and blood reduced the cleavage of disulfide bonds in the systemic circulation, enhancing tumor accumulation and selective activation of PSBA10 NPs. Our study highlighted a tumor treatment model based on the synergistic strategy of structural optimization and GSH gradient regulation across the liver-blood-tumor axis to boost the efficacy of chemotherapy.
nb55cf613d135: Peptide supramolecular systems offer recognition and biocompatibility for precision theranostics, yet their in vivo performance is limited by insufficient structural stability, poor retention, and loss of accessible recognition interfaces under physiological perturbations. Herein, a topology-programmed supramolecular assembly strategy was developed to stabilize adaptive peptide architectures through confinement-guided organization. A β-sheet-based peptide EH, with PD-L1 (programmed death-ligand 1) targeting, favorable assembly behavior, and hydrophobic anchoring potential, was screened from an amphiphilic peptide library and integrated with immunoactivating SeAD quantum dots into PLGA (poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)) microspheres featuring an interconnected hydrophobic channel network. This network guides channel-confined EH assembly through hydrophobic anchoring and β-sheet reinforcement, enabling ordered nanofiber alignment while preserving local conformational flexibility and exposed recognition motifs. This topology-programmed assembly converts dynamic peptide fibers into a structurally stabilized supramolecular interface, leading to prolonged tumor retention and sustained local immune checkpoint blockade. Meanwhile, ultrasound-activated SeAD induces immunogenic cell death and systemic antitumor immunity. By coupling confinement-stabilized peptide recognition with sonodynamic immune activation, EHSeAD@MS achieves durable local tumor intervention, immune microenvironment remodeling, and suppression of distant and metastatic lesions. It establishes a molecular design principle for balancing structural integrity and adaptive recognition in peptide supramolecules, providing a strategy for long-lasting peptide-based cancer immunotherapy.
n35c1d6c76223: Moiré superlattices form quantum-active interfaces in which geometric reconstruction of stacked two-dimensional (2D) materials generates emergent quantum phases that are not present in the parent materials. These engineered interfaces give rise to a wide range of quantum phenomena, including strongly correlated electronic states, flat-band formation, topological phases of matter, and spin–valley locking, all of which can be tuned in situ through the twist angle. Twisted hetero/homostructures of 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) exhibit an unprecedented degree of control over electronic and spin degrees of freedom, driving rapid advances in the emerging field of twistronics and opening pathways toward next-generation spintronic device applications. In this Review, we examine the fundamental concepts, applications, and prospects of twisted 2D TMDs. We outline the evolution from three-dimensional (3D) to 2D materials and the concept of twistronics, then highlight the emergent structural and magnetic properties of twisted 2D TMDs and their heterostructures. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future directions toward applications in spintronic and quantum technologies.
n44e1b667330b: Organic–inorganic hybrid halides offer a versatile platform for programmable multimodal functionalities, through structural softness and lattice‐charge coupling, despite the challenge of balancing the competing ferroic order, carrier transport, and thermal stability requirements. We present a composition‐driven lattice engineering strategy in a 1D iodide series based on 1,6‐diaminohexane (HDA), comprising orthorhombic non‐centrosymmetric phases of HDABiI5 (HBI) and HDASbI5 (HSI) together with a lower‐symmetry non‐centrosymmetric monoclinic phase of HDABi0.5Sb0.5I5 (HBSI) identified by its birefringent response, allowing systematic control of symmetry, lattice dynamics, and coupled transport phenomena. Through variable‐temperature crystallography and 1H NMR, multi‐perturbation Raman spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, photophysical measurements, and electronic structure calculations, we demonstrate a progression from a rigid Bi‐dominated lattice exhibiting strong piezoelectric and ferroelectric coupling to a softer Sb‐rich framework with enhanced anharmonicity, pyroelectricity, and photonic activity, while HBSI combines efficient thermal robustness and phonon transport. Density functional theory calculations show that Bi/Sb substitution tunes the electronic structure from indirect to direct bandgap, modulates oscillator strength, spontaneous polarization, pressure‐dependent electronic properties, thermoelectric and piezoelectric responses, while preserving low iodine‐vacancy formation energies. A trilayer HBI‐HSI‐HBSI architecture couples piezoelectric, triboelectric, pyroelectric, thermoelectric, ferroelectric, and photonic effects, showing 5.1‐fold synergistic enhancement in current generation through interfacial polarization and multimodal coupling.
nf622eb0b7e42: Thermal safety issues arising from electrolyte instability at elevated temperatures pose a critical challenge for lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs). Thermoresponsive electrolytes offer a promising solution, yet battery systems with high-rate capability and reliable thermal protection have not been realized. Herein, we introduce a bifunctional LiNO3 additive into a high-volume-fraction vinylene carbonate-based thermoresponsive electrolyte (HVCE-N) to enhance the performance of LMBs at room and elevated temperatures. Notably, the introduction of the LiNO3 additive modifies the solvation structure of Li+ and forms a Li3N/LiN x O y solid electrolyte interface with high ionic conductivity. Under thermal shock, HVCE-N undergoes a rapid liquid-to-solid phase transition upon free radical polymerization to form a polymer network. More importantly, LiNO3 can regulate the free radical concentration to control the degree of polymerization, thereby preserving high ion transport capability even after phase transition. As a result, a Li||NCM811 cell based on HVCE-N exhibits high-rate performance from 1C to 10C, and stable cycling at 100°C. When subjected to a thermal shock of 200°C, HVCE-N suppresses thermal runaway for Li||NCM811 pouch cell. This electrolyte design offers a new strategy to develop highly safe LMBs with high-rate performance.
n46b79de3a37e: Gallium-based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite-free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co-design of an aluminum-alloyed gallium–indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride-rich water-in-ionic-liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium-assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl-rich mixed Al–Ga–O shell susceptible to [GaCl4]−-mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential-resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI-based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI-derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride-dominated electrode–electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g− 1. Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm−3 normalized to the active-electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide-mediated oxide-displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte-design strategy for oxide-passivated liquid-metal and post-lithium anodes.
nb8709218f9eb: Sn oxides are promising CO2RR electrocatalysts for formate production, but their high activity is difficult to sustain because cathodic reconstruction can over‐reduce active oxide‐derived surfaces to metallic Sn. This dynamic evolution makes it challenging to identify and stabilize the true working‐state active phase. Here, we construct a descriptor‐guided framework that links dynamic Sn‐oxide reconstruction with electronic‐structure evolution and formate‐producing activity to identify and stabilize the favorable working‐state active phase. Electronic‐structure analysis shows that the optimal SnxOy/Sn surface stabilizes the *OCHO intermediate through coupled charge‐polarization redistribution and Sn 5s/5p orbital modulation. To quantify this effect, we develop a TD descriptor integrating Bader charge, Sn 5p coupling, and Sn 5s lone‐pair activation, which exhibits a volcano‐type correlation with the limiting free energy, with the minimum at TD = 0.67 corresponding to the most favorable reconstructed SnxOy/Sn surface. Guided by this descriptor, amorphous SnO2 is designed to stabilize the favorable SnxOy/Sn working state and suppress deep reduction, achieving an HCOO− partial current density of 438.0 mA cm−2 at −1.8 V vs. RHE, 1.8 times that of commercial SnO2. This work provides a descriptor‐guided strategy for stabilizing reconstructed active phases in CO2RR.
n68aa352a6d9f: Fullerene and its derivatives are widely adopted as electron transport layers (ETLs) in high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, fullerene materials are prone to aggregation and rearrangement under environmental stress, which acts as one of the critical factors restricting the long‐term operational stability of devices. Here, we report a host–guest supramolecular assembly strategy using rigid triptycene (TPC) molecules to stabilize fullerene‐based ETLs. The [6,6]‐phenyl‐C61‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)–TPC host–guest interaction enables the spatial isolation and noncovalent immobilization of PCBM cages, which suppresses the thermal‐driven aggregation, crystallization, and morphological variation of PCBM layers. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.83%, with 96.0% efficiency retention after 1000 h of 85°C thermal aging and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C photothermal maximum power point tracking. This work offers a supramolecular solution for high‐stability optoelectronic devices.
n06bf127143bf: Methylammonium (MA)‐free wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites are attractive top‐cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics. However, defect‐related donor‐state contributions can shift the perovskite Fermi level away from the valence‐band maximum (VBM), creating an unfavorable energetic mismatch with the hole‐selective Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite contact and contributing to voltage and fill‐factor losses in perovskite solar cells with an inverted structure. Here, we introduce 4‐(piperidin‐4‐yl)benzoic acid hydrochloride (PBAC) as a spatially organized molecular additive that regulates the carrier polarity of MA‐free WBG perovskites while passivating defects. PBAC shifts the Fermi level toward the VBM and reduces the Fermi‐level offset at the Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite interface. This carrier‐polarity regulation improves energetic compatibility at the hole‐selective contact, facilitating hole extraction and suppressing interfacial recombination. Defect passivation and strain relaxation further inhibit halide migration and stabilize the mixed‐halide lattice. As a result, MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells with bandgaps of 1.66 and 1.77 eV achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 24.66% and 20.74%, respectively. The unencapsulated PBAC‐treated 1.66 eV device retains 86% of its initial PCE after 1000 h of continuous AM 1.5G operation in ambient air. These results establish molecularly induced carrier‐polarity regulation as an effective strategy for reducing interfacial losses in MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells.
ne10dc85de69f: Anode‐free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) promise extreme gravimetric and volumetric energy densities but suffer from irreversible active lithium loss, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and dendritic proliferation. Herein, we report a catalyst‐induced bond‐cleavage redirection concept to unlock efficient sacrificial prelithiation, implemented via a dual‐side functionalized separator. On the cathode side, a 5 µm MoC1‐x/NC‐0.3Co coating redirects Li2C2O4 decomposition from high‐barrier Li–O cleavage to preferential C─C bond scission. Theoretical calculations and operando characterizations confirm this mechanistic shift, lowering the delithiation potential to 3.79 V at 60°C with a 99.5% Li+ utilization rate. To safeguard the liberated lithium inventory against depletion, the anode side integrates a PSSLi‐PFPE bilayer. This coating accelerates Li+ desolvation and drives the in‐situ construction of a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Li symmetric cells cycling for over 1700 h (1.0 mAh cm−2, DOD = 80.7%). Bridging fundamental bond kinetics with practical engineering, the assembled 1.0 Ah anode‐free pouch cell (NCM811||MoC1‐x/NC‐0.3Co‐LCO/PE/PSSLi‐PFPE||Cu) achieves gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 458.6 Wh kg−1 and 1005.2 Wh L−1, a power output of 989.1 W kg−1, retaining 80.1% capacity after 100 cycles. This non‐invasive separator strategy provides a unified framework connecting bond kinetics to practical cell manufacturing, charting a feasible avenue for high‐energy AFLMBs.
n4043e03c5a4b: Achieving both high thermoelectric performance and robust mechanical strength remains a key pursuit for the practical deployment of thermoelectric applications. Herein, a solid‐solution approach is employed in CaCd2Sb2 via alloying with EuMg2Sb2, achieving a synergistic optimization of electrical and phonon transport and mechanical performance. The incorporation of EuMg2Sb2 facilitates band degeneracy, thereby substantially improving the electrical transport properties. Together with the reduced thermal conductivity, the optimized composition exhibits a peak zT of ∼ 1.4 at 750 K and an average zT of ∼ 0.81 between 300 and 750 K. Furthermore, solid‐solution strengthening markedly enhances the mechanical properties, thereby ensuring mechanical integrity for reliable device integration. Leveraging transient liquid phase bonding, a 2 × 2 full‐Zintl module combining this optimized p‐type material with Mg3Sb2‐based n‐type legs achieves a conversion efficiency of ∼ 11% at a temperature difference of 422 K. This work highlights the viability of Zintl phases toward high‐efficiency thermoelectric modules.
nc51f342a34e4: Hole transport layer-free carbon-based perovskite solar cells (HTL-free C-PSCs) suffer rapid performance decay under operational stressors, driven by iodine migration and photogenerated superoxide radicals (O2 •−). To break this photo-oxidation-iodine migration vicious cycle, we design a multifunctional molecular stabilizer, tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)tetrathiafulvalene (4B-TTF). This tailor-made “molecular guard” works via two synergistic mechanisms: its reversible TTF core acts as a charge-transfer mediator, reducing I2 to I− and scavenging O2 •−, while four peripheral benzoic acid groups anchor to undercoordinated Pb2+ sites, passivating grain-boundary defects. Incorporating 4B-TTF into MAPbI3-based devices yields a champion power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.96%, vs. 17.58% for the control, by suppressing non-radiative recombination. Unencapsulated devices retain 96.4% of their initial efficiency after 1200 h under ambient storage and 93.5% after 120 h under harsh UV-oxygen exposure; encapsulated devices retain 90.32% after 700 h of continuous maximum power point (MPP) tracking under 1-sun illumination at 55°C in nitrogen. The strategy is further validated in Cs0.17FA0.83PbI3 systems, delivering a state-of-the-art PCE of 20.70%. This work provides a unified molecular-level strategy to concurrently address ionic, radical, and defect-related degradation, bridging the performance gap between low-cost HTL-free devices and conventional high-cost architectures.
n3c15830bf75e: Noncontact environmental perception is crucial for autonomous alerting and behavior control in mobile robots, yet existing artificial sensory systems still fall short in integrating weak‐stimulus detection, interaction‐direction discrimination, and multimodal sensing within a single device. Drawing inspiration from the electroreceptive hair‐like sensilla of treehoppers and the high‐curvature proboscis of butterflies, we report a Curved Bimodal Hair Sensor (CBHS) that achieves dual‐mode noncontact perception of electrostatic and airflow stimuli. The high‐curvature hair architecture enhances mechanical coupling, and a sliding‐rheostat‐based length‐encoded resistance mechanism enables stable detection of compressive and tensile loads down to 10−4 N. Electrostatic and airflow stimuli are inherently discriminated by their contrasting time scales and signal profiles. Under airflow, hair oscillation induces interfacial contact electrification, dynamically modulating the electrical state to enable wind‐speed detection as low as 0.9 m·s−1, with a random forest model classifying six speed levels at 98.89% accuracy. When integrated into a robotic platform, CBHS directly maps electrostatic polarity to approach and escape behaviors, while a four‐sensor array enables airflow‐direction‐guided vigilance and closed‐loop directional motion. This work presents a structure‐driven bioinspired strategy for low‐complexity multimodal artificial sensory systems directly coupled to robotic behavior.
ndfdc4f927a84: Entangled granular materials derive exceptional macroscopic rigidity from topological interlocking of their constituents. However, rationally designing particle geometries to maximize this effect remains a formidable challenge due to the immense configuration space and the prohibitive computational cost of discrete element simulations. Here, we present a data‐efficient and uncertainty‐aware design framework for autonomous discovery of optimal particle geometries that substantially enhance macroscopic yield strength beyond conventional heuristic shape families. A Semi‐Supervised Graph Wasserstein Autoencoder embeds discrete particle topologies into a continuous latent manifold, while Langevin‐based stochastic optimization explores the structure‐property landscape. By explicitly penalizing epistemic uncertainty through a Lower Confidence Bound acquisition strategy, the framework robustly avoids spurious optima under extreme data scarcity. The discovered low‐aspect‐ratio particle geometries achieve quasi‐cohesive behavior, high yield strength, and self‐supporting capability typically associated with slender fibers. Compression and angle‐of‐repose experiments on 3D‐printed assemblies confirm high simulation fidelity and validate geometry enhanced, interlocking‐dominated load‐bearing architectures.
n23aa477dea9d: AI‐Empowered Design of Granular Metamaterials An active learning scheme combining a Supervised Graph Wasserstein Autoencoder with Langevin‐based stochastic optimization is developed to identify optimal shapes of elongated, non‐convex particles that self‐assemble into strong, free‐standing structures with maximized yield stress. This work establishes a data‐efficient paradigm for optimizing granular metamaterials. More details can be found in the Research Article by Xin Bian, Yu Guo, and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77723).
n0e876811dbfb: Bio‐based aerogels are a compelling class of sustainable materials, with some of them distinguished by their exceptional thermal superinsulating performance, i.e. conductivity lower than that of air. However, their practical use is limited by poor stability in humid environment. Pectin/polyurea aerogels were developed to address this issue. Pectin was combined with polyurea precursors to explore how polyurea chemistry affects thermal performance at 25°C and high relative humidity (RH). ATR‐FTIR and NMR analyses confirmed the formation of a conformal polyurea network coating pectin nanofibrils. All aerogels displayed high specific surface areas (350–520 m2 g−1) and exceptionally low thermal conductivity, 0.015–0.018 W m−1 K−1. Among the formulations tested, the aerogel based on pectin/rigid aliphatic polyurea network demonstrated superior performance, maintaining a stable thermal conductivity of 0.015 W m−1 K−1 in 80% RH for nearly 300 days (duration of test). In addition to thermal superinsulation, this optimized formulation showed high mechanical strength, good flame retardancy, and effective acoustic reflectivity. This is the first report on biopolymer‐based aerogels retaining long‐lasting thermal superinsulating properties under extended humid exposure, with their performance matching that of the best silica aerogels. Pectin/polyurea aerogels possess strong potential as multifunctional and sustainable insulation materials.
ne1532b337e47: While triggering the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) represents an efficient approach to enhancing the intrinsic activity of iridium‐based catalysts for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), the irreversible lattice oxygen loss and subsequent Ir dissolution induce structural collapse, constituting the fundamental activity‐stability trade‐off. To address this challenge, we propose an amorphous support‐mediated *OH enrichment strategy that dynamically replenishes oxygen vacancies (Ov) to stabilize and optimize the LOM pathway. This concept is exemplified by engineering IrOx nanoparticles supported on amorphous zirconia (ZrOx). In addition to anchoring Ir sites and mitigating their over‐oxidation‐induced dissolution, the ZrOx support efficiently facilitates water dissociation, leading to the in situ accumulation of reactive *OH intermediates. This enrichment process dynamically replenishes the Ov generated during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), thereby accelerating the LOM rate‐determining step and simultaneously preserving the catalyst's structural integrity and boosting the intrinsic activity, as evidenced by in situ spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations. In PEMWE tests, the catalyst achieves a low voltage of 1.75 V at 2 A cm−2 and demonstrates stable operation for 1000 h. This work establishes a new design principle for developing highly efficient and durable Ir‐based OER catalysts for PEMWE applications.
nf005818c9a7f: The non‐ideal contact at the electron transport layer/metal electrode interface remains a primary obstacle to achieving both high efficiency and operational stability in perovskite solar cells. Here, we address this challenge by developing HL136, a novel cathode interfacial material with a DMAPF–IC–IDSe–IC–DMAPF structure, to engineer the [6,6]‐phenyl‐C‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)/Ag interface. Leveraging strong interfacial interactions and a pronounced dipole effect, HL136 effectively optimizes the energy‐level alignment and facilitates efficient electron extraction. For the inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) fabricated with HL136 (anti‐solvent‐free), we obtained a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.8%, combined with an exceptional open‐circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.158 V, short‐circuit current density (JSC) of 26.5 mA cm−2, and fill factor (FF) of 0.841. Furthermore, large‐area modules achieve a PCE of 24.7% and retain 95.5% of their initial efficiency after 1500 h of continuous illumination. This work highlights that rational cathode interfacial engineering is a potent strategy for concurrently enhancing efficiency, scalability, and long‐term durability in inverted perovskite solar cells.
n27f345af382c: Phase change materials (PCMs) have garnered widespread interest in battery thermal management (BTM) for their excellent temperature regulation, high thermal storage density, and passive cooling without additional power consumption. Nevertheless, conventional PCMs fail to simultaneously mitigate capacity degradation caused by extremely high/low ambient temperatures and suppress battery thermal runaway (BTR) risks. Herein, a Janus‐structured phase change composite built on aramid nanofiber (ANF) aerogels, is engineered for multi‐mode adaptive BTM applications. The bilayer asymmetric architecture is constructed with boron nitride nanosheets embedded in the large‐pore ANF layer to deliver high thermal conductivity (1.860 W m−1 K−1) and large latent heat (189.23 J g−1) after PCM impregnation, while fluorosilane modification imparts the small‐pore ANF layer remarkable thermal insulation (0.028 W m−1 K−1) and flame retardancy. The as‐resulted composite with a thickness of 7 mm achieves an 8.60°C reduction in the surface temperature for commercial 2000 mAh lithium‐ion batteries under 3 C charge/discharge cycling. It also drastically decreases the peak runaway temperature from 798.29°C to 240.85°C and effectively blocks BTR propagation between adjacent cells. Meanwhile, the composite raises the usable discharge capacity from 770 to 1275 mAh at −20°C, offering a promising strategy for developing multi‐mode adaptive BTM systems.
n62e2de46ab25: Interfaces in perovskite solar cells govern crystallization kinetics, interfacial energetics, defect formation, charge transport dynamics, and nonradiative recombination of charge carriers, thereby critically determining device efficiency and operational stability. Here, we report an in situ dual‐interface engineering strategy using a multifunctional additive, maleimido propionic acid hydrazide hydrochloride (MPAH.HCl), incorporated directly into the perovskite precursor. During film formation, MPAH.HCl undergoes spontaneous bifurcation‐driven bidirectional segregation, with Cl− preferentially enriching at the buried interface and MPAH+ accumulating at the near top surface. At the buried interface, Cl− modulates crystallization dynamics, promotes grain growth, passivates deep‐level defects, and improves energy‐level alignment. Simultaneously, surface‐segregated MPAH+ effectively passivates dominant vacancy (VI, VPb, VFA) and antisite (PbI, IPb, IFA) defects. This synergistic dual‐interface modulation suppresses nonradiative recombination while facilitating efficient charge extraction and transport. As a result, optimized inverted perovskite solar cells achieve a fill factor of 86.6% (vs. 80.6% for the control), with a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.10% for 0.09 cm2, and 24.28% for 1 cm2 devices. Furthermore, enhanced crystallinity and stabilized interfacial chemistry significantly improve device stability under ambient, thermal, and operational stress conditions. This work introduces bifurcation additive segregation as an effective strategy for simultaneous buried and top‐interface optimization, enabling highly efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.
n29bc4e97b0f6: Tricuspid valve insufficiency and restricted opening remain clinical challenges in structural heart disease interventions, often requiring invasive repair or replacement. Inspired by natural organisms such as the nautilus, jellyfish, and lotus leaf, we propose a bioinspired helical hydrogel scaffold featuring a Janus wettability interface for magnetically and thermally responsive tricuspid valve repair. The scaffold comprises a spiral architecture and a trilayer hydrogel system, integrating a hydrophobic PDMS/CNT/Fe3O4 surface for blood‐facing anti‐thrombotic performance and a hydrophilic P(HEMA‐co‐AAm) surface for enhanced tissue adhesion. The magnetic responsiveness endowed by Fe3O4 nanoparticles enables remote, non‐contact clamping under external fields, while the incorporation of a thermoresponsive P(NiPAAm‐bis‐AA) hydrogel ensures in situ mechanical anchoring and dynamic adhesion at physiological temperature. In vitro mechanical and actuation tests, ex vivo porcine heart simulations, and in vivo biocompatibility assessments demonstrated the scaffold's reliable fixation, fatigue resistance, blood compatibility, and stable integration under cardiac‐mimicking conditions. This work presents a minimally invasive, suture‐free solution with high translational potential for tricuspid valve repair, and offers a modular platform for expanding intelligent hydrogel devices to other cardiac and interventional applications.
n003266121ca5: Two‐dimensional nanofluidic membranes are emerging as attractive functional materials for osmotic energy conversion, yet their practical implementation is hindered by the intrinsic trade‐off between ionic conductivity and mechanical robustness. Here, inspired by the hierarchical brick‐and‐mortar architecture of nacre and amino‐acid‐regulated ion transport in biological channels, a biomimetic hybrid nanofluidic membrane is developed by integrating glycine‐grafted poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA_Gly) into natural vermiculite via a simple vacuum‐assisted infiltration process. The grafted polymer simultaneously reinforces interlayer interactions and constructs bio‐inspired ion‐transport pathways while preserving the ordered lamellar framework. Consequently, the composite membrane achieves a nearly threefold enhancement in ionic conductivity together with a ∼3.5‐fold increase in tensile strength, effectively breaking the conventional conductivity–mechanical trade‐off. The universality of this biomimetic hybridization strategy is further demonstrated in graphene oxide– and MXene‐based nanofluidic membranes, which exhibit concurrent improvements in ion transport and mechanical performance. When applied to osmotic energy harvesting, the optimized membranes deliver a high power density of 18.8 W m−2 under parallel ion transport, exceeding most reported two‐dimensional nanofluidic membranes and surpassing the commonly cited commercialization benchmark. This work establishes a scalable biomimetic materials design strategy for constructing mechanically robust, high‐performance nanofluidic membranes, offering new opportunities for advanced energy‐conversion applications.
n2aab5b3f080e: Aqueous Zn||I2 batteries are promising candidates for safe and flexible energy‐storage systems, yet their practical application is hindered by polyiodide shuttling, self‐discharge, and unstable Zn deposition. Herein, inspired by the classical starch‐iodine complexation phenomenon, a bio‐inspired PVA/AP double‐network hydrogel electrolyte is developed by integrating amylopectin (AP) helical host sites within a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) supporting framework. Unlike conventional confinement strategies based on physical blocking or nonspecific adsorption, the AP‐derived helical domains enable reversible host‐guest interactions with polyiodides, thereby regulating polyiodide chemistry while preserving iodine‐redox reversibility. Meanwhile, the PVA framework provides structural support and continuous Zn2+‐transport pathways, enabling the effective utilization of AP within a self‐supporting hydrogel network. Experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that the AP‐derived helical environment reversibly confines polyiodides while promoting homogeneous Zn deposition. Consequently, the hydrogel electrolyte enables stable Zn plating/stripping for 2100 h and excellent resistance to self‐discharge with 98.1% capacity retention after 48 h resting. The corresponding Zn||I2 battery exhibits durable cycling over 5000 cycles with 80.1% capacity retention while maintaining reliable operation under flexible and abuse conditions. This work translates starch‐iodine complexation into a hydrogel‐electrolyte design principle and establishes a biomolecular host‐guest strategy for regulating polyiodide chemistry in flexible aqueous Zn||I2 batteries.
na1e64b41099a: Phototransistors offer intrinsic gate‐controlled gain amplification, providing much higher responsivity than photodiodes, but this advantage is generally limited by the gain‐speed trade‐off: high gain typically relies on long‐lived trapped carriers, which inevitably slows the photoresponse. Although low‐dimensional semiconductors and hybrid heterojunctions have improved responsivity and detectivity, they still predominantly operate through slow, trap‐mediated gain, leaving the trade‐off unresolved. Here, sub‐10 nm organic–inorganic single‐crystalline van der Waals heterojunctions are introduced to decouple gain from slow carrier trapping. Specifically, a bilayer molecular crystal (C6‐DPA) is integrated onto a monolayer MoS2 channel. Reducing the heterojunction thickness to the exciton diffusion limit, localized Frenkel excitons in C6‐DPA efficiently undergo interfacial charge separation and transfer across the type‐II interface, while the separated charges rapidly modulate the MoS2 channel conductance through the field effect. Gain therefore arises from efficient channel gating rather than prolonged trapped‐carrier circulation. The resulting phototransistors achieve a responsivity of 1.07 × 105 A W−1, rise/decay times of 771.2/809.8 µs, and a specific detectivity of 2.19 × 1015 Jones under their respective optimized operating conditions. These results demonstrate that the gain–speed trade‐off in phototransistors arises primarily from trap‐mediated gain mechanisms and can be mitigated through exciton‐engineered ultrathin single‐crystalline organic–inorganic van der Waals heterojunctions.
n411ed83c36eb: Broadband convolution processing is critical for accurate color image recognition. However, current broadband convolution processing involves a photoresponse matrix based on continuous‐voltage modulation devices, resulting in high energy consumption. Here, we demonstrate an InSe neuromorphic device that integrates broadband convolutional processing with perception, memory, and computation functions to realize high‐accuracy recognition of color images with the potential for low latency and reduced energy consumption. A photoresponse matrix was constructed using voltage pulses for broadband convolutional processing. The device's broadband perception capability originates from the moderate bandgap of approximately 1.3 eV in InSe, while its memory function is attributed to the ferroelectric polarization effect of Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3 (PZT). Analog computation is realized via bias‐dependent, continued nonvolatile positive and negative photoconductive responses. Moreover, the multiband non‐volatile photocurrent matrixes generated by the InSe neuromorphic devices are used for broadband convolution processing of color images. Furthermore, combining the multifunctional InSe neuromorphic device with a convolutional neural network achieves 97.4% recognition accuracy for color “S”, “D”, “U” letter images after only ten training epochs. The proposed work is promising to set the stage for next‐generation intelligent machine vision systems in imminent embodied artificial intelligence humanoid robots.
n6ed4e4f96266: Flexible perovskite solar cells (f‐PSCs) are highly promising for lightweight, bendable, and integrable photovoltaic applications. However, fabricating high‐quality perovskite films on low‐temperature‐resistant plastic substrates remains a great challenge. This issue is particularly prominent in p‐i‐n type PSCs, where the self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) based buried interface suffers from inferior wettability and tends to induce undesirable phase transformation of perovskite. Herein, we propose an interfacial seeding strategy that introduces an ultrathin perovskite layer into the SAM layer prior to the deposition of perovskite films. This buried‐interface modification facilitates the homogeneous distribution of SAMs on the bottom electrode and enhances the affinity of the SAM surface toward the polar perovskite precursor, thereby improving perovskite coverage on the hydrophobic substrates. Moreover, the buried ultrathin perovskite serves as a well‐defined nucleation template that triggers the homogeneous crystallization of the upper perovskite layer. This significantly enhances the crystal quality and interfacial integrity, while suppressing defect states and reducing the Young's modulus of the perovskite films. As a result, a champion efficiency of 25.18% was achieved for f‐PSCs, accompanied by significantly improved resistance against long‐term storage, thermal aging, light exposure, and repeated bending.
nea8def64f388: Atmospheric water harvesting is an effective method for obtaining fresh water. However, problems such as secondary evaporation from water separation and declining efficiency need to be addressed urgently. Here, we demonstrate a biomimetic cactus fog collector embedded in the soil that overcomes these challenges by integrating vortex‐assisted, multi‐level‐structured water transport and temperature‐difference condensation mechanisms. Our device integrates fog collection and condensation to efficiently collect water and enable immediate irrigation to the plant roots without requiring external energy. The cylindrical collector is fabricated using metal 3D printing, with a surface covered in conical spines of varying wettability, asymmetric through‐holes, and internal capillary grooves. In wind tunnel tests simulating coastal fog, the bionic design achieved a water production rate of 152 kg m−2 h−1 and a collection efficiency of 49%. In addition, we utilized the natural temperature difference between the soil and the air to achieve a passive condensation rate of 895.6 g m−2 h−1. Field tests have shown that our system can sustain crop growth under water‐scarce conditions. Our work presents a new paradigm for atmospheric water utilization, from the development of biomimetic materials to integrated passive irrigation, providing a scalable strategy for agriculture in arid regions.
n6c1d3f211d3d: The systematic design of chiral metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) that combine structural rigidity with dynamic, full‐color gamut circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) remains a significant challenge. This study proposes a charge delocalization‐guided ligand functionalization strategy that enhances ligand p‐π conjugation and intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) by systematically regulating the quantity and location of amino groups on aromatic pyridine ligands, thereby enabling solid‐state continuous emission tuning across the full‐color gamut (385–661 nm). This series of MOFs exhibits rapid and reversible fluorescence switching in dichloromethane (DCM). Spectroscopic analysis and DFT calculations indicate that this is due to the weak N─H···Cl host‐guest interactions, which cause electronic localization of the ligands and a shift in the charge transfer mechanism from LMCT to LLCT. Notably, D/L‐DPA‐MOF and D/L‐DPAD‐MOF exhibit an asymmetry factor |glum| as high as 10−2 and outstanding CPL brightness in DCM. Capitalizing on the scalability of this series of layered columnar structures, we synthesized 2D chiral metal‐organic heterostructures and explored their applications in advanced optoelectronics. This work establishes a universal new paradigm for the development and information encryption application of dynamic full‐color gamut luminescent chiral MOFs through the precise control of excited‐state electron distribution.
n8cea7ca2b21a: Metal single-atom catalysts can catalyze electrolyte decomposition to regulate solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation, yet the intrinsic reaction pathways at isolated active sites hinder targeted SEI composition design. Herein, we innovatively construct a Bi@NC anode decorated with CoN4 single sites and Co4 clusters via a thermodynamically driven phase separation mechanism. This dual-site design overcomes the limitations of isolated CoN4, enabling the formation of an inorganic-rich and multifunctional gradient SEI that ensures high structural flexibility, rapid Na+ diffusion, and effective dendrite suppression. Specifically, Co4 clusters preferentially catalyze organic electrolyte decomposition to favor the formation of inorganic Na2CO3, while simultaneously upshifting the Co d-band centre of CoN4 to enhance PF6 − adsorption and P–F bond (NaPF6) cleavage. The electronic synergy between CoN4 and Co4 clusters further induces local electron delocalization, optimizing the reaction microenvironment. As a result, the anode delivers an exceptional rate capability of 325 mAh g−1 at 90 A g−1, enabling full charging within 13 s. Remarkably, it achieves ultralong cycling stability with a capacity of 373 mAh g−1 after 20 000 cycles, maintaining 96.4% of its initial capacity with a decay rate of only 0.00018% per cycle. This work provides a new paradigm for designing durable, fast-charging anodes through interfacial catalytic chemistry.
n645fc203f5b3: Single‐crystalline Ni‐rich layered oxide cathodes exhibit superior cycling and thermal stability over conventional polycrystalline counterparts by eliminating grain‐boundary‐associated degradation. However, the extended Li+ diffusion length in single crystals limits practical particle sizes to only a few micrometers, creating a fundamental trade‐off between electrode density and electrochemical performance. Here, we report a practical synthesis strategy for ultra‐large (≈15 µm) single‐crystalline and quasi‐single‐crystalline LiNi0.95Co0.04Mn0.01O2 cathodes that deliver an exceptional rate capacity of 170 mA h g−1 at 5 C despite their unprecedented particle size. Using these grain‐engineered architectures, we identify oxygen transport during high‐temperature synthesis as a previously overlooked factor governing defect formation in ultra‐large Ni‐rich cathodes. In single‐crystal particles, sluggish oxygen diffusion through the ordered bulk lattice produces a pronounced oxygen‐deficient structural state, accompanied by severe cation disorder. In contrast, internal grain boundaries in quasi‐single‐crystal particles act as rapid oxygen‐transport channels, enabling efficient oxygen redistribution during sintering and thereby suppressing oxygen vacancy formation and cation mixing while preserving structural integrity. Consequently, ultra‐large quasi‐single‐crystal cathodes simultaneously achieve high electrode density, fast reaction kinetics, excellent thermal stability, and long‐term cycling durability. This work identifies grain‐boundary‐assisted oxygen transport as a key design consideration for defect control in ultra‐large, highly Ni‐rich layered oxide cathodes.
n33e4a1e11a74: Phosphorescent Pt(II) emitters are promising candidates to overcome the low blue index (BI) issue of commercialized blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs); however, developing high-performance deep-blue OLEDs with high color purity, particularly with a full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of less than 20 nm, is a major challenge. Herein, we report a synergistic design strategy, involving the regulation of both molecular geometry and excited-state properties to balance the efficiency and color purity of deep-blue Pt(II) emitter toward the Broadcasting and Television 2020 (BT.2020) standard. A bottom-emitting OLED displays deep-blue light peaking at 461 nm, a small FWHM of 19 nm, and high external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) of 29.1% and 22.9% at 1000 and 10000 cd/m2, respectively; and realizes a record-high maximum brightness of 49971 cd/m2 for non-sensitized deep-blue OLEDs with CIEy < 0.15. A top-emitting OLED exhibits a further narrowed spectrum with a FWHM of 13.3 nm, and achieves a Commission Internationale de l'Éclairage y coordinate (CIEy) of 0.053, extremely close to the BT.2020 blue standard. This OLED also exhibits an outstanding maximum BI value of 464 cd A−1 CIEy −1 and maintains a BI of 435 cd A−1 CIEy −1 at 1000 cd/m2.
n9933effc5e4e: Marine Internet of Things (IoT) systems require reliable self‐powered sensor nodes for long‐term ocean monitoring. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) provide a promising solution for harvesting irregular ocean wave energy, but the low frequency, small amplitude, and randomness of ocean waves significantly limit the performance of conventional TENG designs. Here, a double‐pendulum wave energy harvester integrating bearing‐joint triboelectric nanogenerators is proposed. The double‐pendulum structure effectively amplifies low‐frequency wave motion and directly converts rotational motion into electrical output. Not only does one single joint generation unit deliver an average output power of 1.16 mW, but it also achieves notable improvements in peak and average power density among bearing‐type TENGs, reaching 52.46 and 17.95 W·m−3, respectively. The architecture exhibits rapid capacitor charging and excellent durability under simulated ocean wave conditions, enabling the operation of multiple electronic devices without external power. This strategy provides a promising route toward low‐maintenance, long‐lasting power sources for self‐powered Marine IoT systems in complex ocean environments.
nae8101041523: Mixed halide perovskites (MHPs) are promising semiconductors for optoelectronic devices requiring tunable bandgaps, yet they suffer from operational instability caused by phase segregation. Phase segregation is strongly mediated by water, an inevitable and even intentionally introduced molecule during the fabrication of perovskites. However, the role of water in phase segregation remains unclear, as it is often coupled with the coexisting oxygen in air. Herein, we resolve this issue by utilizing vacuum to induce sequential desorption of oxygen and water from MHP, and in situ monitoring of the phase segregation evolution. Our results show that following the initial oxygen desorption, water at the perovskite surface and subsurface desorbs at two different stages. The former activates the defects and enhances the phase segregation, while the latter removes the water‐induced lattice expansion and suppresses the phase segregation. These effects can be correlated with the photovoltaic performance, where the surface water removal raises the hysteresis by 67% and lowers the efficiency by 6.6%, while the further removal of subsurface water reduces hysteresis by 60% and increases efficiency slightly by 0.9%. This work unveils the double‐sword role of water in the phase segregation of MHP, providing inspiring insights for the optimization of relevant optoelectronic device performance.
n9308215f1ac3: Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation has emerged as a sustainable and promising technology for seawater desalination, but its practical deployment is severely hindered by the ubiquitous presence of oil contamination in marine environments. Here, a hierarchical evaporator (GSPMS) was developed to achieve the simultaneous recovery of freshwater, solid salts, and oil. In the design, a mangrove‐inspired hydrophilic sponge (GSMS) ensures continuous capillary water transport and directs salt crystallization in predefined regions, while a Salvinia‐inspired hydrophobic‐oleophilic sponge (GPMS) selectively captures oil droplets and continuously expels them through capillary‐assisted siphon transport. Consequently, the GSPMS exhibits a stable evaporation rate of 3.43 kg m−2 h−1 along with a salt harvesting rate of 165.8 g m−2 h−1 over 50 h of continuous operation in 20 wt% brine. For seawater containing 20 vol% oil, the evaporator also delivers an evaporation rate of 4.11 kg m−2 h−1 and an oil recovery of 97.73%, while maintaining a separation efficiency above 99% over 10 cycles. This dual‐bioinspired strategy offers a promising strategy toward zero liquid discharge desalination and the comprehensive utilization of seawater resources, highlighting the potential of integrated multi‐resource recovery in solar‐driven water treatment.
n4b4a1b684163: Thermal safety is a key challenge for high‐energy lithium metal batteries. Conventional separators deform under overheating while sustaining ion transport, accelerating thermal runaway. Herein, we report an aramid‐supported shape memory separator that converts temperature rise into reconstruction of ion transport pathways. A covalently crosslinked PETMP‐TMPTA‐IBOA network is photopolymerized within a porous aramid scaffold. At normal operating temperatures, the interconnected pore structure affords an ionic conductivity of 0.29 mS cm−1 and enables stable Li plating/stripping for over 3000 h. At 140°C, the shape memory network undergoes thermomechanical rearrangement, constricting the percolating pores and increasing the ionic resistance by one order of magnitude. Meanwhile, the aramid scaffold preserves dimensional integrity up to 175°C and maintains electrode isolation after ionic shutdown. The separator is compatible with high‐energy NCM811 and Li‐rich Mn‐based oxide cathodes. In particular, a Li‐rich cathode with high mass loading of 16 mg cm−2 cycles stably for 100 cycles at 0.5 C, delivers nearly 250 mAh g−1 at 60°C, and remains operable up to 125°C. This work establishes thermomechanical reconstruction of ion transport pathways as a general design principle for intrinsically self‐protective lithium metal batteries that reconcile high energy operation with autonomous overheating protection.
n5464622fba7d: Advanced cryptomaterials capable of storing concealed information and selectively revealing it through dynamic pathways are desirable for next‐generation cryptography. However, simultaneously achieving high‐dimensional information encoding, scalable material fabrication, and secure yet equipment‐free decryption remains an unresolved challenge. Herein, we present a class of dynamic supramolecular cryptomaterials (DSCs) that couple compositional encoding with mechanical decryption, establishing a fundamentally different cryptographic paradigm. Multi‐component functionalized colloids are embedded within polymer matrices via dynamic supramolecular interactions, producing visually indistinguishable precursor materials in which the encoded information is completely concealed. Upon prescribed oscillatory shearing stimulus, transient supramolecular networks are selectively activated, driving a disorder‐to‐order transition and leading to highly ordered superstructures with formulation‐specific optical fingerprints, jointly governed by material composition and the mechanical activation. By independently programming composition, including the colloids and polymer, the DSCs enable continuous structural‐color regulation across 410–753 nm while simultaneously tailoring color saturation and brightness. The multidimensional compositional space provides exceptional information density, with each pixel capable of encoding up to 393 identities. This work establishes a general materials design strategy that transforms composition from a passive formulation parameter into an active information carrier and introduces mechanically programmable supramolecular cryptomaterials as a scalable platform for high‐security information encryption and advanced anti‐counterfeiting.
nf7a2972ec521: Electrocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production through the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) offers a promising route for sustainable H2O2 synthesis under ambient conditions. However, the development of electrocatalysts that simultaneously exhibit high activity, selectivity, and stability remains challenging. Specifically, achieving precise control over catalytic centers remains challenging. Herein, an electron-deficient linker engineering approach based on π-conjugation tuning is proposed to tailor the electronic structure of nickel phthalocyanine (Ni−N4) active sites in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Three dianhydride derivatives (i.e., benzene-1,2,4,5-tetracarboxylic dianhydride (PMDA), 1,4,5,8-naphthalenetetracarboxylic dianhydride (NTDA), and perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTDA)) were utilized to synthesize NiPc-PMDA, NiPc-NTDA, and NiPc-PTDA COFs. Benefiting from the π-conjugation-tuned linker electronic properties, NiPc-PTDA demonstrates an outstanding 2e− ORR selectivity of 92% and a high H2O2 production rate of 34.8 mol gcat −1 h−1 in a two-electrode flow cell. Combined theoretical and experimental results support a correlation between linker electronic properties, the electronic state of the Ni centers, Ni–*OOH interaction, and the thermodynamic branching between H2O2 release and further *OOH reduction. This work highlights the role of linker electronic properties in regulating catalytic centers and provides a π-conjugation-guided linker-design approach for selective H2O2 electrosynthesis in NiPc-based COFs.
n94f0befdf10b: Exotic nanoparticle superstructures can be accessed by harnessing nanoparticle softness and charge regulation, features often viewed as obstacles to structural control. Here, we show that regulated charge mismatch in polymer‐grafted nanoparticles enables the assembly of high‐stoichiometry cubic superlattices. By co‐tuning grafting density, particle size, and bulk composition, we realize ionic‐lattice analogues, such as CaF2${\rm CaF}_2$ and Th3P${\rm Th}_3{\rm P}$4$_4$, as well as single‐component A3${\rm A}_3$ and A7${\rm A}_7$ superlattices without atomic counterparts. The A3${\rm A}_3$ superlattice has recently been identified theoretically as a photonic band‐gap lattice. These phases emerge from a 1:1 “parent” lattice when local charge neutrality cannot be satisfied, driving either progressive interstitial filling or reorganization into a larger basis. For instance, the systematic occupation of ZnS tetrahedral sites yields CaF2${\rm CaF}_2$, while ligand‐swapping symmetry breaking converts CsCl into Th3${\rm Th}_3$P4${\rm P}_4$. Upon heating, the assemblies exhibit reversible lattice contraction and pronounced negative thermal expansion. Furthermore, the energetic penalty for defects increases with nanoparticle size, facilitating the scalable production of high‐quality, open superlattices for photonic applications.
n382c95703d5f: Electrostatically Assembled Photonic Superlattices Charge‐regulated nanoparticles assemble beyond conventional 1:1 stoichiometry into exotic open superlattices. Controlled charge mismatch and interstitial site filling enable high‐stoichiometry structures and non‐atomic analogues like the photonic A3 lattice. The cover illustrates this electrostatic assembly pathway bridging programmable nanoparticle crystallization with emergent optical and photonic functionalities. More details can be found in the Research Article by Surya K. Mallapragada, Alex Travesset, David Vaknin, and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77545). Artwork by INMYWORK Studio.
n28eb0f8a02d1: Next‐generation food packaging is evolving beyond passive containment toward adaptive systems capable of preserving food quality and communicating freshness changes. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer programmable metal–ligand chemistry, tunable porosity, high loading capacity, selective adsorption, and responsive signal transduction, making them promising building blocks for active and intelligent packaging. However, their practical performance may be limited by framework instability under humid or acidic conditions, poor processability, and potential migration of metal ions and organic linkers. Integrating MOFs with food‐compatible polymers provides processable architectures in which interfacial interactions regulate structural stability, molecular transport, and functional accessibility. This Review connects MOF structural engineering and MOF–polymer interfacial engineering with controlled release, antimicrobial activity, atmosphere regulation, and freshness monitoring. Particular emphasis is placed on how metal–ligand chemistry, defect structures, particle and pore architectures, and interfacial interactions govern pore accessibility, transport kinetics, stability, and signal transduction. Toxicological safety, migration assessment, and regulatory considerations are further discussed. Overall, this Review provides mechanistic design principles for balancing functionality, stability, and safety toward practically viable MOF‐based food packaging systems.
ne000dee882ab: The pH-universality of hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts enables their cost-effective and scalable application. Proton behavior regulation enhances HER activity under specific pH conditions, yet achieving pH-universal performance remains a significant challenge. Here, we propose interfacial proton engineering to achieve pH-universal HER within the built-in electric field (BIEF) of a crystalline/amorphous Re-based heterostructure (Re(c)/ReO x (a)). Specifically, the catalyst exhibits a hydrophilic and aerophobic surface that facilitates mass transport, and its doubled free water content enhances proton source accessibility, promoting water dissociation at amorphous ReO x sites. Simultaneously, BIEF-induced strong electronic interaction generates low-valence Re sites with a downshifted d-band center, enabling efficient proton retention and conversion, thereby creating an “acid-like” microenvironment in alkaline media. In situ Raman and ΔpH analyses confirm the constructed interfacial proton microenvironment, demonstrating a triple synergy of free water enrichment, water dissociation, and proton retention. As a result, the Re(c)/ReO x (a) shows a minimal overpotential gap of only 11 mV at 1 A cm−2 across the pH range. Its cost-normalized activity is 20.6 and 106.8 times higher than that of Pt/C in acidic and alkaline media, with excellent alkaline stability for 1000 h at 1 A cm−2. This work provides an interfacial proton perspective for designing pH-universal HER electrocatalysts.
n5fe812f81142: Polymer dielectrics operating under extreme environments require increasingly higher demands on electrical insulation performance. Polyimide (PI), one of the most promising candidates for high-temperature energy-storage dielectrics, tends to form charge-transfer complexes (CTCs) under high temperatures and high electric fields, which promotes carrier migration and increases dielectric loss. In this work, by introducing 3,9-Bis[2-(3,5-diamino-2,4,6-triazaphenyl) ethyl]-2,4,8,10-tetraoxaspiro[5.5]undecane (DTI) into semi-aromatic polyimide (SPI), a topology-regulated SPI-co-DTI network was constructed. The electron-deficient triazine units in DTI can induce local electrostatic-potential heterogeneity and polarized transport barriers. The helical configuration of DTI further disrupts the continuity of interchain coupling and blocks charge-transport pathways. SPI-co-0.5%DTI achieves a discharged energy density (U d) of 8.79 J cm−3 with an efficiency (η) above 90% at 150°C and 780 kV mm−1. At 200°C, SPI-co-0.5%DTI still maintains a high U d of 5.93 J cm−3, which is 103% higher than that of SPI at the same conditions. This work provides a new design concept and paradigm for developing high-performance polymer dielectrics for harsh-environment applications.
n6275405b4c2f: Multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) with high recoverable energy storage density (W rec) and high efficiency (η) are essential electronic components in advanced electronic devices and pulsed power systems. However, achieving both high W rec and η remains a long-standing challenge.
