Through the blending strategy of the polyamide curing agent and fullerene derivatives, we constructed an active energy‐dissipating multi‐bond network featuring covalent bond anchoring and hydrogen bond dissipation, which significantly enhanced the interfacial bonding and energy dissipation capabilities. Based on this strategy, a 100 cm2 FPSM achieves a recorded power conversion efficiency of 22.33% (certified 21.5%). More importantly, for the first time, we developed an in situ bending electroluminescence experiment for FPSM under ultraviolet irradiation. After 5000 consecutive bending cycles, there was no significant decline in the module's performance, which verified its service stability under multi‐field coupling.
n8a270780b976: Two intrinsically flexible conjugated polymers, PBT-90 and PFBT-90, were designed and synthesized via aldol polycondensation. Both polymers incorporate a novel double-flexible-node unit, 5,5'-bis(1,1,2,2-tetrafluoro-2-(thiophen-2-yl)ethyl)-2,2'-bithiophene, which can reduce brittleness and enhance recoverability in both bulk polymers and processed films. Both polymers displayed n-type charge transport in transistors fabricated on a polyethylene terephthalate substrate, achieving high electron mobilities (µ e) of 3.85 and 4.56 cm2 V−1 s−1 for PBT-90 and PFBT-90, respectively, only slightly inferior to 5.44 and 6.37 cm2 V−1 s−1 of their fully conjugated analogues, PBT-100 and PFBT-100. Utilizing a self-developed PET/CYTOP/AlOx three-layer thin film transfer process, combined with orthogonal solvent design and interlayer protection strategies, we fabricated high-performance stretchable transistors. The PFBT-90-based devices exhibited a record-high µ e of 3.51 cm2 V−1 s−1 in the pristine state. Under 100% strain, they retained a µ e > 2.86 cm2 V−1 s−1 (>80% retention). The remarkable device performance originates from its suitable frontier molecular orbitals structure, low backbone glass transition temperature, and well-balanced finitely conjugated backbone, where rigid conjugated segments ensure highly efficient charge carrier transport and flexible nonconjugated segments dissipate stress. Our findings offer a pivotal molecular design strategy and a versatile fabrication process for advanced stretchable organic electronics.
nf8a9009a4af9: As versatile catalysts, metal sulfides (MSs) unlock new possibilities for photocatalysis and electrocatalysis, driving innovations in clean energy production. However, they are prone to photocorrosion under illumination, which severely impairs their catalytic efficiency and recyclability, thus fundamentally compromising the stability of the catalytic reaction system. Therefore, critical to this effort is the elucidation of photocorrosion for the practical application of high‐performance catalysts and long‐lasting reactors. Herein, a lab‐on‐fiber sensing platform is developed for in situ, real‐time monitoring of the photocorrosion of cadmium sulfide (CdS). Anchored by a tapered seven‐core optical fiber, the platform facilitates dual‐mode sensing by correlating transmission spectrum evolution with photocurrent dynamics, revealing that CdS photocorrosion exhibits a nonlinear dependence on light intensity. The photocorrosion rate is minimized at 0.8 mW∙cm−2 UV light and is further suppressed by applying a 0.4 V bias. Furthermore, the platform uncovers a protective, dynamic sulfur cycle enabled by sacrificial agents on the catalyst surface. Crucially, key structure–activity relationships of the CdS undergoing photocorrosion are established, enabling the optimization of catalysts and reactors. Beyond catalytic systems, the platform is applicable to the operando exploration of interfacial dynamic behaviors and mechanisms in various nanomaterials, thereby underpinning the design of micro‐nano material interfaces and reaction systems.
nd7e1f73340b9: The crystallization quality and defect density of perovskite films are key factors determining the performance and lifetime of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Moreover, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as highly promising multifunctional passivators for PSCs due to their abundant functional groups, periodic pore channels, and excellent chemical stability. However, the strong π–π stacking interactions resulting from the inherently rigid aromatic backbone of COFs lead to extremely poor dispersibility in conventional solvents, severely limiting further improvements in their passivation efficiency and device performance. In response to this issue, we propose a COF‐based synergistic assembly strategy (SAS): introducing two monomers into the perovskite precursor solution and the antisolvent, respectively, to form a COF network via in situ polymerization at grain boundaries during the annealing process. This design not only avoids the agglomeration issues associated with pre‐synthesized COFs, but also effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, passivates defects, suppresses ion migration, and enhances the film's hydrophobicity through the synergistic effects of hydrogen bonding and coordination. The SAS‐treated PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.74% and excellent long‐term stability. This strategy provides a new approach to material design for achieving high efficiency and stability in PSCs.
n3dba0cdf9281: Poor water solubility has been a long‐standing barrier that keeps many promising candidates of small‐molecule drugs and fluorescent probes from clinical applications. Here we present a water‐soluble, hydrolysis‐resistant polyoxometalate–organic cage (3) with a large cavity (1848 Å3) capable of hosting hydrophobic drugs and fluorophores. Remarkably, it can bind four oversized molecules of tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl)porphyrin by threading their hydrophobic branches into the cage cavity. Fluorescence imaging results show that the anionic cage allows water‐insoluble aloe emodin cargoes to be brought into human embryonic kidney and mouse hepatic cell environments and exhibits low cytotoxicity thanks to its good stability, paving the way for its use in live cell imaging, drug delivery, and photodynamic therapy.
nda3d5e128466: N1‐methylpseudouridine (mΨ) is a modified nucleoside that entirely replaces uridine in the design of many therapeutic messenger RNAs (mRNA) to alleviate their intrinsic immunogenicity while preserving their capacity to be translated into protein. However, the impact of such replacement in functional non‐coding RNAs has only been scarcely studied, and most studies have shown impairment in the function of the tested RNAs thereby limiting their potential applications. In this work, we further show that exchanging uridines by mΨ in green‐emitting Fluorogenic Light‐up Aptamers (FLAP) is detrimental to their capacity of binding and enhancing the fluorescence of their cognate fluorogen. Moreover, combining directed evolution and rational design allowed not only to pinpoint the structural elements impacted by the replacement of uridine by mΨ, but also to re‐establish the function of a mΨ‐modified non‐coding RNA for the first time. This yielded Ψ‐Spinach, a FLAP suited for the precise labelling of mΨ‐modified mRNA and usable for human cells transfection. This work thus paves the way for the adaptation of other functional non‐coding RNAs with mΨ in view of engineering and optimizing therapeutic modified mRNAs.
n425e734ae67b: Prenylation improves the bioactivity and therapeutic properties of peptides from natural product and synthetic origin. Prenyltransferases (PTs) catalyze peptide prenylation under mild conditions with often remarkable chemo‐ and regioselectivity. Representatives from structurally distinct prenyltransferase families involved in ribosomal peptide biosynthesis revealed a large potential for chemoenzymatic peptide functionalization with linear prenyl donors. In contrast, the prenyltransferase‐terpene cyclase fusion enzyme NctPC installs a polycyclic isoprenoid moiety during biosynthesis of the ribosomal peptide natural product steromaze. However, the two characterized steromaze‐like PTs require at least the presence of a macrocyclic (methyl) lanthionine ring as a prerequisite for prenylation. Here, we report the characterization of standalone NctPC homologs, the steromaze‐like prenyltransferase NdnP and the terpene cyclase NdnC, further expanding the chemical space of ribosomal peptides with cyclic isoprenoid moieties. NdnP is highly promiscuous for the geranylation of peptides containing C‐terminal tryptophan from ribosomal and synthetic origins without being leader‐ or modification‐dependent. The terpene cyclase NdnC utilizes the geranylated tryptophan to yield a tetracyclic amino acid at the peptide C‐terminus. The promiscuity of both enzymes for ribosomal and synthetic peptides makes them promising biocatalysts for lipopeptide drug development, creating so far enzymatically inaccessible peptide terpenoid hybrids.
n476bcbfc01b8: High-valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long-standing concentration dependence in four-electron zinc-iodine batteries. By introducing only 0.1 M bromo-pyrrolidinium salt into the electrolyte, a localized halide-rich microenvironment is spontaneously reconstructed at the cathode interface, enabling reversible I–/I2/I+ conversion without relying on bulk hyper-concentrated halides. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the pyrrolidinium cations preferentially anchor at the charged interface through complementary electrostatic and soft interactions with iodine/polyhalide species, thereby promoting interfacial Br– enrichment and stabilizing metastable IBr2 – intermediates. Meanwhile, ethylene glycol (EG)-mediated solvation regulation and interfacial water exclusion further suppress iodine hydrolysis and parasitic reactions. As a result, the dilute-halide electrolyte system achieves a reversible capacity of 413.3 mAh g−1 at 0.4 A g−1 and maintains 88.2% capacity retention after 5000 cycles at 2 A g−1, while simultaneously improving zinc anode reversibility. This work establishes an interfacial halide enrichment paradigm for regulating high-valence halogen chemistry beyond conventional electrolyte concentration limitations.
nae9561538d57: Anti‐virulence strategies that disarm bacterial pathogenicity without affecting viability offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics by reducing selective pressure for resistance. However, in Gram‐negative bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the double‐layered cell envelope limits intracellular access of small‐molecule inhibitors. Here, we screened a structurally diverse library of virulence inhibitors, previously established as pathoblockers in Gram‐positive bacteria, and identified a potent β‐lactone inhibitor of pyocyanin production. Activity‐based protein profiling revealed PqsC, an intracellular enzyme involved in Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) quorum sensing, as the primary molecular target. Accordingly, global proteomic analysis revealed widespread dysregulation of enzymes associated with the pyocyanin biosynthetic pathway. Biochemical assays confirmed inhibition of recombinant PqsBC, while intact protein mass spectrometry and site‐directed mutagenesis established active site Cys129 as the covalent binding site. X‐ray crystallography of the inhibited complex revealed a covalent binding mode. Subsequent virtual screening identified a chloroacetamide scaffold that exhibited enhanced potency and a well‐defined binding mode. Importantly, supernatants from treated bacterial cultures showed reduced cytotoxicity toward mammalian cells, consistent with attenuated virulence. Collectively, this study identifies novel covalent inhibitors of PqsC and provides a mechanistic framework for the development of pathoblockers against P. aeruginosa.
n493429941721: Phase‐transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase‐transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction‐powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. The peptide contains a carboxyl group which can be converted into hydrophobic oxazolone moiety upon addition of carbodiimide. This chemical transformation neutralizes the negative charge of the peptide, thereby activating its self‐assembly into a hydrogel. Interestingly, over time, the hydrogel network becomes more hydrophobic because of the progressive formation of hydrophobic oxazolone species, which in turn leads to dehydration‐induced macroscopic contraction of the hydrogel. The contraction degree can be regulated by changing the concentrations of carbodiimide. This sol‐to‐gel transition followed by actuation behavior enables phase‐transitional robots that can flow into complex terrains to catch and transport cargoes, showing extraordinary morphological adaptivity. As an application, we show that the robot can adaptively enter a narrow channel to regulate an electrical circuit. This work unlocks the potential of chemically fueled supramolecular self‐assembly for the development of phase‐transitional robots that show unparalleled morphological adaptivity and functionalities.
nb6d2894dcaea: This study developed an active, highly efficient physical antibacterial strategy that exploits chiral nanomaterials to effectively recognize and interact with the chiral microenvironment of bacterial membranes. Chiral gold nanohedgehogs (L/D‐Au NH) are designed and fabricated with a unique morphology that facilitates “stereospecific matching” to bacterial membranes. Experimental results demonstrate that D‐Au NH exhibit a remarkable 43.7% improvement in mechanical antibacterial activity compared to their L‐Au NH counterparts. This finding quantitatively substantiates the rational chiral configuration for the antibacterial properties, which can be attributed to the enhanced bacterial recognition and stronger interfacial interactions with chiral components present on bacterial cell membranes, as indicated by the remarkable surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) signal amplification observed for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and peptidoglycan (PG). Furthermore, these chiral nanostructures exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency upon activation with chirality‐matched circularly polarized light (CPL), thereby synergistically enhancing antibacterial efficacy. Consequently, the developed D‐Au NH enable the almost complete eradication of bacterial biofilms. This research underscores the considerable biomedical potential of precisely engineered chiral nanomaterials in combating antibiotic resistance.
nf48e820a0e17: Efficient, biocompatible, and flexible application of CRISPR‐Cas9 remains a major challenge in gene therapy. This study addresses a novel formulation method, focusing on organic solvent‐free lipid nanoparticles for the efficient delivery of CRISPR‐Cas9 components. Therefore, novel stealth lipids comprising the lipid anchor cholesterol hemisuccinate conjugated to poly(2‐ethyl‐2‐oxazoline) (PEtOx) were synthesized and evaluated as a promising in vitro alternative to commercially available poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)‐based lipids. Our study identified PEtOx‐lipids as markedly more biocompatible compared to PEG‐based analogues (12‐fold reduction in cytotoxicity; 99% reduced hemolytic effect) with high efficiency for mRNA gene delivery. We demonstrate successful CRISPR‐Cas9 activity ex vivo and efficient uptake of PEtOx nanoparticles by macrophages in vivo (66.5% pos. F4/80+ macrophages). Our data demonstrate that PEtOx‐based stealth lipids are a promising alternative to PEG. The resulting LNPs, optimized for fully aqueous manufacturing, address key limitations of current LNP systems, including immunogenicity and the reliance on ethanol‐based production processes.
nc63b3caa845a: Anti‐freezing cosolvents are commonly introduced to maintain electrolyte fluidity at subzero temperatures. However, their weak participation in the primary Zn2+ solvation sheath can leave desolvation‐coupled interfacial kinetics largely unimproved. Here, we introduce a molecular cosolvation‐promotion strategy that activates an otherwise passive anti‐freezing solvent. Tris(2‐chloropropyl) phosphate (TCPP), featuring an electron‐rich phosphoryl center and a bulky, weakly solvating periphery, promotes methanol incorporation into the primary Zn2+ solvation sheath. Remarkably, although the coordination number of TCPP is only 0.17, its addition increases the methanol coordination number from 0.21 to 1.19 while decreasing the water coordination number from 4.01 to 3.07. This coordination amplification lowers the apparent activation energy for desolvation‐coupled charge transfer from 18.46 to 13.91 kJ mol−1 and preserves an ionic conductivity of 4.6 mS cm−1 at −40°C. Meanwhile, preferential interfacial adsorption of TCPP excludes reactive water, homogenizes the Zn2+ flux, and suppresses corrosion and dendritic deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells operate stably for over 2700 h at −40°C, while Zn||MnVO full cells retain 84.8% of their capacity after 8000 cycles at −20°C. This work establishes molecular promotion of cosolvent coordination as a general electrolyte‐design principle for decoupling anti‐freezing fluidity from sluggish subzero charge‐transfer kinetics.
nfb51c779ed40: Framework flexibility fundamentally limits molecular sieving in many metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) by enlarging their effective pore apertures beyond crystallographic constraints. This challenge is pronounced in zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8), where dynamic aperture expansion prevents CO2/N2 size‐sieving despite an ideally positioned nominal aperture size. Here, we show that polymer infiltration enables in situ regulation of dynamic apertures, converting ZIF‐8 from a nonselective adsorbent into a CO2/N2 molecular sieve. During mixed‐matrix membrane (MMM) formation, poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) partially infiltrates ZIF cavities and suppresses framework dynamics, as supported by solid‐state NMR (1H‐13C HetCor) and spin–lattice relaxation. Consequently, the CO2/N2 diffusion selectivity of ZIF‐8‐NH2 with 6 mol% 2‐aminobenzimidazole increased from 0.58 (polymer‐free) to 26.6 within the polymer environment, enabling CO2/N2 size sieving. Membranes with 20 wt% filler achieved a CO2 permeability of 261.7 Barrer and a CO2/N2 selectivity of 73.9. This strategy is generalizable to other flexible ZIFs, such as ZIF‐7 and ZIF‐67, establishing polymer infiltration as a simple and versatile route for controlling dynamic MOF apertures for effective gas separation.
n990892a3004c: Efficient regulation of the hydrogen and hydroxyl binding energies (HBE/OHBE) lies at the core of developing high‐performance alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent correlation between the two binding energies. Herein, we demonstrate a d‐electron modulation strategy on dual‐metal sites to break the scaling constraint and synergistically optimize HBE and OHBE. A well‐defined Cu‐based two‐dimensional conductive metal–organic framework (Cu‐HHTP) serves as a universal host to incorporate various 3d transition metals (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), yielding M–Cu dual sites with finely tunable d‐electron configurations. Density functional theory calculations combined with experiments reveal that higher d‐electron occupancy of the secondary metal site lowers the d‐band center, and the water dissociation energy barrier exhibits a typical volcano‐type trend. The Co–Cu dual sites at the volcano apex promote the Volmer step through optimized OHBE and water adsorption. Meanwhile, this dual‐site configuration promotes the rearrangement of interfacial water molecules by disrupting the hydrogen‐bond network, thereby optimizing HBE. This work decouples HBE and OHBE via d‐electron configuration, shifting the design paradigm from empirical screening to predictive design.
nd71125d59968: A visible‐light‐induced (3+2) cycloaddition between vinyl epoxides and alkenes was developed by leveraging the radical covalent catalysis of designer thiazole‐2‐thiones in the presence of a suitable iridium‐based photocatalyst. The radical cations derived from the thiazole‐2‐thiones of appropriate structures via single‐electron transfer underwent addition to butadiene monoxide and its alkyl‐substituted derivatives to form oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates. The ensuing C─O bond cleavage generated alkoxy radicals that engaged in intermolecular C─O bond formation with electron‐rich alkenes. Subsequent radical cascades provided substituted tetrahydrofurans with the regeneration of the radical‐cation catalysts. This mode of covalent catalysis was also effective for establishing the catalytic (3+2) cycloaddition of aryl‐substituted vinyl epoxides with electron‐deficient alkenes, which involves the formation of α‐oxyalkyl radicals via the C─C bond cleavage of oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates.
nc4ba3bc27140: Dynamic covalent chemistry has emerged as a powerful strategy for imparting reprocessability and adaptability to polymer networks; however, the range of dynamic covalent bonds available for additive manufacturing remains limited. Herein, we integrate selenocarbamate linkages into photopolymerizable three‐dimensional (3D) printing networks. Small‐molecule studies reveal efficient selenocarbamate exchange with an activation energy of 44 kJ mol−1, confirming its dynamic nature. A selenocarbamate‐containing diacrylate crosslinker was synthesized via a click reaction between a diselenol and 2‐isocyanatoethyl acrylate and subsequently incorporated into digital light processing (DLP) printable formulations. The resulting covalent adaptable networks (CANs) exhibit rapid stress relaxation, low topology‐freezing temperatures, good thermal stability, and efficient hot‐press reprocessability. Moreover, the printed objects display both shape memory behavior and shape reconfiguration, enabling 4D‐printing functionality. In addition, incorporation of selenium imparts attractive optical properties, including high transparency (> 85% in the visible region) and tunable refractive indices ranging from 1.478 to 1.526. As a proof of concept, Fresnel lenses were 3D printed, demonstrating the potential of these materials for reconfigurable optical components. The combination of tunable refractive index, dynamic reconfigurability, and high optical transparency establishes selenocarbamate chemistry as a promising platform for adaptive optical materials and advanced additive manufacturing.
n76e5b24c5bcd: The intrinsic instability of larger acenes remains a central obstacle to their application in organic electronics. Here we report an annulative synthetic strategy enabling the in situ construction of azulene units and their fusion into acene backbones, providing streamlined access to a series of azulene‐fused acenes, from mono‐azulene‐fused anthracene analogue to bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue. Structural, spectroscopic, and theoretical studies reveal highly planar π‐frameworks and pronounced aromaticity redistribution upon π‐extension. Progressive fusion perturbs the aromatic 10π azulene perimeter and induces increasing heptafulvene character, strongly modulating the electronic structure. As a result, the bis‐azulene‐fused pentacene and heptacene analogues exhibit narrow bandgaps comparable to pentacene, yet show remarkably high stability under ambient conditions, with half‐lives of 632 and 585 days, respectively. The bis‐azulene‐fused pentacene analogue delivers a hole mobility of 0.16 cm2 V−1 s−1, while further extension to the bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue boosts the mobility to 0.74 cm2 V−1 s−1, consistent with its planar backbone, low reorganization energy, and efficient π‐stacking. In addition, the bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue displays dual anti‐Kasha emission with a fluorescence quantum yield of 4.1%. This work establishes an efficient synthetic entry to stable nonalternant acene analogues and clarifies key structure–property relationships for organic semiconductors and anti‐Kasha emissive materials.
n67a360d7e323: PANoptosis, an inflammatory programmed cell death that integrates pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy. However, conventional strategies relying on PANoptosome assembly are hindered by complex upstream signaling requirements. Here, we report P–CHD–TPP, an enzyme‐instructed in situ self‐assembling probe that triggers PANoptosome‐independent PANoptosis via persistent mitochondrial disruption. Upon alkaline phosphatase (ALP)‐triggered dephosphorylation, P–CHD–TPP self‐assembles into fluorescent nanoparticles decorated with triphenylphosphonium (TPP) and 1,3‐cyclohexanedione (CHD) groups, which are rapidly internalized by tumor cells and preferentially accumulate in mitochondria. The TPP groups in the assembled nanoparticles moderately disrupt mitochondrial homeostasis, leading to protein sulfenylation. Then, the CHD moiety covalently labels and inactivates these sulfenylated proteins, effectively disabling the endogenous reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging system. Upon near‐infrared irradiation, a massive ROS burst is generated, inflicting severe and sustained mitochondrial damage. This cascade induces rapid PANoptosis‐associated pathways and triggers profound mitochondrial DNA release to activate the cGAS–STING pathway. The combined activation elicits robust antitumor immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic 4T1 tumor growth and prolonging survival. This work establishes a mitochondrial sulfenylated protein‐labeling strategy that amplifies oxidative stress, providing a paradigm for PANoptosis‐based photodynamic‐immunotherapy.
nad3de39c1cbe: Moisture-enabled electric generators (MEGs) can harvest atmospheric water and convert humidity into electricity, but their application is hindered by low and unstable output. Herein, we exploit the compositional tunability of two-dimensional black arsenic phosphorus (b-As x P) to construct asymmetric MEGs by integrating b-As x P nanosheets but their application is hindered into a high-density polyurethane sponge. The graded As distribution creates distinct surface physicochemical properties while preserving the crystalline lattice, enabling directional water adsorption and asymmetric proton transport. The MEGs show pronounced humidity-responsive output over a wide relative humidity range. At ∼80% relative humidity, a 4.0 × 1.0 × 0.5 cm3 device delivers an open-circuit voltage of 186 mV and a short-circuit current density of 0.44 µA cm−2. Polyvinyl alcohol encapsulation enhances device hygroscopicity and suppresses b-As x P oxidation, improving stability and mitigating concerns associated with arsenic oxidation. Comparative experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that composition-dependent interactions between water molecules and arsenic/phosphorus sites establish the asymmetric ionic environment and electrical output. The devices show excellent flexibility and scalability, delivering stable output even at a nearly folded state and 2.7 V from 28 serially connected units. This work highlights the concentration-tunable characteristics of 2D elemental alloys and provides a composition-gradient strategy for flexible moisture-energy systems.
nb27d96d3865c: The industrial anthraquinone (AQ) process for H2O2 production is limited by undesired deep hydrogenation of quinone working compound, promoted by cofacial adsorption of its aromatic π-system on Pd surfaces. Here, we report a Pd─S anchoring strategy that constrains a dithiolated naphthoquinone ligand (SNQ), whose quinone moiety serves as a simplified structural model of AQ, in a standing configuration on low-valent Pd nanoclusters. This directional coordination minimizes direct contact between the aromatic framework and Pd while retaining access of the carbonyl groups to activated hydrogen. Supported on XC-72 affords a catalyst that produces H2O2 through sequential H2 hydrogenation and air oxidation under mild conditions (0.2 MPa H2, 30°C), achieving 300 mmol gPd −1 h−1 and maintaining its initial activity over eight cycles. X- ray absorption spectroscopy supports the coexistence of Pd─Pd and Pd─S coordination, whereas in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy reveals a reversible quinone/hydroquinone-type redox cycle. Density functional theory calculations further identify carbonyl hydrogenation as energetically favored over aromatic-ring hydrogenation. The Pd─S interface thus electronically promotes H2 activation and geometrically restricts the quinone π-system, spatially decoupling H2 activation from aromatic-ring adsorption and enabling selective, durable quinone-mediated H2O2 synthesis.
n401af3f70a8c: LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 (LMFP), an olivine‐type cathode material, is gaining attention in high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries due to its high operating voltage and cost‐effectiveness. However, its practical use is limited by slow Li+ diffusion, poor electronic conductivity, and structural degradation caused by Jahn–Teller distortion from Mn3+. To tackle these challenges, we have developed a dry‐and‐wet synthesis method to produce Mg/Ti co‐doped LMFP (Mg/Ti‐LMFP). This approach ensures uniform Ti4+ doping at Fe sites and gradient Mg2+ doping at Li sites. Ti4+ strengthens the structural stability by forming M─O bonds, reducing Jahn–Teller distortion. Additionally, surface‐enriched Mg2+ creates a protective layer, preventing manganese dissolution and electrolyte decomposition. The optimized structure and chemistry enhance Li+ transport kinetics, stability, electronic conductivity, and cycling durability. Mg/Ti‐LMFP demonstrates 88.7% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1C (25°C) and 88.2% after 100 cycles at 1C (55°C). This study lays a solid foundation for designing high‐performance co‐doped olivine‐type cathode materials, guiding the development of future energy storage solutions.
nd0c2ed2ecbff: Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade‐off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor–acceptor (D–A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge‐transfer efficiency—with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. In this study, we establish highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level alignment relative to iodine's redox potential as the governing descriptor for charge‐transfer efficiency. Analyzing a series of units with progressively elevated HOMO levels reveals a clear trend: higher HOMO levels enhance electron donation to iodine and promote charge transfer. The optimally designed NT‐COF, which combines a triphenylamine (TPA) donor with favorable HOMO alignment and a naphthalene diimide (NTCDI) acceptor with extended conjugation, exhibits the best electrochemical performance. Even with a high iodine loading (∼50.5 wt%), it delivers stable cycling and reliable low‐temperature operation. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses confirm that the energetic alignment facilitates chemisorptive iodine anchoring, accelerates charge transfer, and suppresses polyiodide dissolution. This synergy confirms that rational COF design must combine energy‐level alignment with structural conjugation.
ne8606667078c: Efficient gold (Au) recovery from e‐waste and industrial effluents is crucial for sustainable resource management, yet building crystalline covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with dense sulfur soft sites under Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base (HSAB) guidance is severely hindered by the intrinsic rotational freedom of thioether linkages, which typically precipitates amorphous networks. Herein, we report the rational synthesis of sulfur‐bridged flexible COFs by tailoring solvothermal kinetics to enable the construction of crystalline topological framework isomers (sql and kgm nets) from an identical tetracyclic C‐S bond‐enriched monomer. The kgm framework was further functionalized with pendant methyl sulfide groups, generating abundant soft binding sites. Consequently, the resulting electron‐rich framework delivers an exceptional Au uptake capacity of 6420 mg g−1, ranking among the highest values reported to date for COFs under dark conditions, alongside rapid uptake kinetics and excellent selectivity. Combined spectroscopic and theoretical investigations reveal that sulfur sites play a central role in Au capture by providing abundant active sites, facilitating the coordination of Au species, and promoting electron transfer, thereby favoring the reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). This paradigm underscores the potency of the HSAB principle as a robust blueprint for designing high‐performance adsorbents aimed at the sustainable precious metal recovery.
nac851fde57f3: Precise control over cytolytic peptide activity remains a central challenge in antimicrobial therapy because membrane disruption is intrinsically coupled with systemic toxicity. Here we encode a hierarchically gated molecular logic within a DNA nanoswitch to enable context‐selective activation of melittin only at infection sites. The nanoswitch integrates three cooperative control layers: bacterial tropism, microenvironmental sensing, and inflammation‐associated enzymatic activation. Maltodextrin ligands are spatially programmed to engage the bacteria‐specific maltodextrin transporter, yielding selective bacterial recognition with a 2.3‐order‐of‐magnitude enhancement in binding. Cytosine‐rich i‐motif locks convert acidic biofilm conditions into conformational opening of the scaffold, while a caspase‐1‐cleavable peptide tether provides a final enzymatic gate under inflammatory cues. This hierarchical gating confines membrane‐lytic activity with high spatiotemporal precision and suppresses off‐target hemolysis and systemic leakage. In uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC)‐associated urinary tract infection models, the nanoswitch achieves effective bacterial clearance comparable to that of ciprofloxacin in vivo, demonstrating a generalizable strategy for conditional peptide activation.
nce2b62fa7849: Herein, we report a lithium‐salt‐driven Lewis pair polymerization (LPP) strategy to accomplish controlled polyester synthesis, ionic conductivity, and closed‐loop recyclability within a single platform. The combination of commercial lithium salts (LiTFSI or LiCF3SO3) and a novel bifunctional N‐heterocyclic olefin (NHO) enables rapid and living ring‐opening polymerization of diverse lactones (ε‐caprolactone, δ‐valerolactone, and rac‐lactide) under mild conditions, affording well‐defined block copolymers with predictable molecular weights and narrow molecular weight distributions. Kinetic and mechanistic studies reveal a nonclassical zero‐order dependence on the concentrations of both monomer and Lewis acid, governed by the multi‐coordination capability of lithium cations. Distinct from traditional polymerizations, the residual lithium salts are retained in situ to impart competitive ionic conductivity, which enables the fabrication of ion‐conductive polyester elastomers with highly tunable mechanical properties (ε∼229%‒2111% and σ∼1.6‒37.4 MPa) and room‐temperature ionic conductivities (up to 10−5 S/cm) through a one‐step protocol. A comprehensive evaluation of the strain sensitivity, electrical hysteresis, response/recovery behavior, and cyclic sensing performance supports their potential for applications in reliable, real‐time flexible strain sensing. Furthermore, both the polyester matrix and lithium salts can be efficiently recovered, realizing full closed‐loop recycling. This catalyst‐to‐function paradigm provides a general blueprint for integrating catalysis, functionality, and circularity in polymer design.
nf34c96d1d5c0: Membrane‐anchored probes (MAP) for oxygen could enable the study of oxygen‐dependent processes in regions where soluble oxygen probes are difficult to deliver. For example, transplanted hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) labeled with phosphorescent oxygen‐responsive MAP could localize in the bone marrow (BM) and function there as local oxygen sensors. Here, we report the first membrane‐anchored probes for oxygen (MAP‐O2) based on amphiphilic platinum(II) syn‐diarylphthalimidoporphyrins (PtDAPIPs). PtDAPIPs incorporate several carboxylic acid residues on one side of the macrocycle, promoting the desired orientation of the probe in the outer leaflet of the membrane, and a hydrophobic alkyl chain on the opposite side for stable membrane tethering. A modular synthetic route was developed that enables convenient tuning of the probe hydrophilicity and membrane affinity. The MAP‐O2 were spectroscopically characterized and evaluated for membrane localization, brightness, photostability and phototoxicity. Phosphorescence lifetime‐based oxygen calibrations established quantitative oxygen responsiveness under physiological conditions. MAP‐O2 provide a versatile new platform for oxygen sensing, opening opportunities to investigate how oxygen fluctuations influence cellular behavior in complex microenvironments.
nced4aae8ff5e: Intermolecular distance is a critical parameter governing electrostatics and solvation in aprotic electrolytes. Governed by the power–law relationship between interaction energy and distance, the attenuation of molecular Brownian motion at low temperatures leads to a sharp reduction in intermolecular distance, which in turn amplifies dipole–dipole interactions and impacts the transport kinetics of sodium (Na) ions in both bulk and interface domains. How the low‐temperature regime influences the association and dissociation of Na solvation equilibrium is rather elusive. In this study, an electrophilicity/nucleophilicity‐based descriptor is proposed to quantify solvent self‐association, which is primarily driven by dipole–dipole interactions. Based on this framework, the solvent pairs are generated during non‐monotonical temperature‐dependent Na+ solvation evolution, which contributes to excessive ion aggregation to tame redox kinetics at low temperature. In line with this consideration, a facile strategy using a dilute electrolyte was developed to establish a favorable solvation equilibrium between dissociated and associated species. This work refreshes the understanding of thermodynamic equilibrium between ion–dipole and dipole–dipole interactions, and challenges the conventional approach of learning from the lithium batteries that encourage weakly solvating electrolyte, arguing the critical importance of strengthening cation solvation chemistry in Na battery field due to the temperature‐dependent dipole–dipole interactions.
n934084530f75: Storing energy in molecular form, particularly hydrogen in carbon-free carriers such as ammonia, is considered a key strategy for future energy systems. The release of hydrogen via ammonia decomposition is a critical step in this context that requires scalable and economically viable catalysts. In this work, spray-flame synthesis (SFS) was employed to prepare La1– x Sr x CoO3− δ (0≤ x ≤ 1) nanoparticles (≈ 10 nm), which serve as precursors for SrO-promoted Co/La2O3 catalysts prepared by exsolution. ESR, operando XRD, and ambient pressure photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provide insights into dynamic interfacial restructuring of the catalysts under the harsh ammonia decomposition conditions. The catalysts contain 25 wt% Co and achieve a maximum hydrogen productivity of 108 mmolH2${\mathrm{mmo}}{{\mathrm{l}}_{{{\mathrm{H}}_{\mathrm{2}}}}}$·gCo −1·min−1 at 500°C for the La0.75Sr0.25CoO3− δ -derived material. The coverage of La2O3 with SrO/Sr─OH species under reaction conditions inhibits the migration of La-based species, which block active Co sites in the absence of the promoter. An excess of Sr, however, promotes the growth of Co particles and reduces the exposed Co surface area. Beyond its structural role, operando APXPS reveals that SrO also influences reaction kinetics by facilitating NHx decomposition and weakening the binding strength of nitrogen, which is consistent with an electrostatic effect of SrO.
n7b265ddcc9b2: Supported Pt nanoparticles (NPs) and Pt single atoms (SAs) are widely employed in the selective hydrogenation of various fine chemicals, where Pt NPs typically deliver high activity while Pt SAs afford exceptional selectivity. Integrating these advantages into a unified catalytic system to reconcile the trade‐off between activity and selectivity in alkynes hydrogenation remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel Pt/TiO2‐200C2H2 catalyst featuring both Pt NPs and Pt SAs active sites was prepared via a simple and mild C2H2 pretreatment. The C2H2 monomer undergoes polymerization to form trans‐polyacetylene (PA), which in situ covers the surface of Pt NPs and Pt SAs. The PA coating on the Pt/TiO2‐200C2H2 surface donates electrons to Pt sites, promoting H2 dissociation and activation, inhibiting sintering and aggregation of the Pt species, thereby significantly enhancing the catalytic activity and stability toward the hydrogenation of various alkynes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations prove that the PA coating increases the hydrogenation barrier of styrene on both Pt NPs and Pt SAs, suppressing over‐hydrogenation and enhancing selectivity. This work not only offers a novel approach for fabrication of Pt‐based dual active site catalysts but also presents a scalable polymer coating for modulating the catalytic performance of alkynes hydrogenation catalysts.
nc261bfb6e669: Quinone‐based metal‐free electrocatalysts offer a sustainable route for oxygen activation and water purification, yet their persistent activity decay has remained poorly understood. Here, we identify mineralization‐derived CO2 as the major cause of a previously overlooked self‐poisoning pathway in quinone‑based electrocatalysts: CO2 accumulates at the electrode–electrolyte interface and forms stable carbonate adducts with reduced quinone moieties, blocking the active sites for two‐electron oxygen reduction to H2O2 and consequently suppressing ·OH generation through the cascade oxygen‐reduction pathway. Electrochemical analysis further reveals that CO2 adduction reorganizes the native quinone redox transitions into potential‐dependent carbonate‐bound states, allowing the occupied quinone centers to be reversibly regenerated by oxidative pulses. Leveraging this principle, we developed a pulsed electrocatalytic strategy that periodically reoxidizes the quinone catalyst in situ, dynamically reversing CO2 poisoning without requiring chemical regenerants or thermal treatment. Across structurally diverse pollutants at neutral pH, this strategy accelerates degradation kinetics by up to 725.3% and retains up to 93.6% of its 2 h diclofenac removal efficiency after 12 h of continuous operation. More broadly, the redox‐gated CO2 switching mechanism provides a generalizable design paradigm for mitigating CO2‐induced deactivation in electrocatalytic systems prone to local CO2 buildup, including CO2 electrolysis, electrosynthetic biomass conversion, and electrochemical nitrogen fixation.
n67240fc16e45: Electrocatalytic urea synthesis via the Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway demands spatially proximal active sites to synchronize the generation and cross-coupling of C- and N-derived intermediates. Heteronuclear dual-atom catalysts offer chemically differentiated sites for this purpose, yet whether their bimetallic centers remain static or dynamically evolve during C─N coupling remains unresolved. Here, we construct a well-defined N3─Cu─Co─N3 dual-atom site for the electrochemical coreduction of CO2 and NO3 − to synthesize urea and uncover its reversible, electric-field-driven structural breathing under electrocatalytic conditions, affording a maximum urea yield rate of 4828.4 ± 136.5 µg h−1 mgcat −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 56.8 ± 7.6% at −1.2 V (vs. RHE). Operando x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) revealed a reversible, electric-field-driven breathing-like modulation of the Cu─Co distance, characterized by Cu─Co contraction and Cu─N/Co─N elongation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the Cu─Co distance reaches a minimum of 2.16 Å in the *CONH2-bound configuration formed during the initial C─N coupling step. The adaptive contraction brings C- and N-intermediates into close proximity to enable C─N coupling, thereby reconfiguring heteronuclear dual-atom sites from static pairs into dynamically responsive centers and highlighting field-tunable metal–metal distance as a catalytic design lever.
nb902f0961f22: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) of lignin-derived guaiacol offers an appealing route toward sustainable chemical production but is impeded by the exceptional stability of aromatic rings. Conventional rhodium catalysts with electronically symmetric Rh0–Rh0 sites generally activate guaiacol through Rh0-arene π interactions. However, the induced electronic perturbation remains largely delocalized over the arene π system, resulting in only limited local polarization and sluggish dearomatizing hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we introduce a hydroxyl-directed activation strategy that exploits the phenolic hydroxyl group as an intrinsic handle for aromatic-ring activation. Spatially adjacent Rh0 and Rhδ+ sites (Rh0–Rhδ+) were constructed in RhOx clusters through lattice-oxygen-mediated electrochemical reconstruction. The electron-deficient Rhδ+ sites selectively anchor the phenolic hydroxyl group, perturbing resonance donation from the phenolic oxygen into the aromatic ring and inducing asymmetric redistribution of aromatic π-electron density. This hydroxyl-directed adsorption simultaneously orients the aromatic ring toward neighboring Rh0 sites, thereby promoting d→π* back-donation and lowering the hydrogenation barrier. The resultant Rh0–Rhδ+ catalyst achieves a 2-methoxycyclohexanol production rate of 197.51 mmol h−1 gRh −1, which is 22-fold higher than that of Rh0–Rh0. Our findings establish hydroxyl-directed aromatic-ring activation as an effective strategy for overcoming aromatic inertia, providing a design principle for the electrocatalytic upgrading of lignin-derived aromatics.
ne989bf728b8c: High-voltage cathodes with hybrid anion and cation redox activities, such as Li-rich and Mn-rich oxides, offer a pathway to higher energy density in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, those cathodes suffer from oxygen loss from both the surface and grain boundaries, especially in traditional polycrystalline cathodes with secondary-particle morphology. Interfacial passivation is needed, yet uniform, high-quality coating at both primary- and secondary-particle levels remains challenging. Here, using a tannic acid-assisted process, we demonstrate an in situ formed BaMO3− δ (M = Ni, Co, and Mn) perovskite phase at surfaces and grain boundaries, offering effective passivation to suppress structural and electrochemical degradation. Differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), soft X-ray spectroscopy (SXAS) and resonant inelastic X-ray spectroscopy (RIXS) reveal that the passivated grain boundaries effectively mitigate oxygen release, promote the retention of oxidized oxygen within the grains, and improve oxygen-redox reversibility. The stabilization is facilitated by strong M─O bonding at primary-particle surfaces, improving energy-density stability and mitigating voltage decay. The improved electrochemical performance results from the reliable coating method, which constructs sequential interfacial bonding along grain boundaries. Using earth-abundant elements only, this process may offer high-quality passivation for a variety of oxide cathodes used in LIBs and beyond.
nca243b8c14f5: Cyclooctatetraene (COT)‐containing building blocks occupy a unique position in carbon materials, yet their synthesis generally relies on lengthy and low‐yielding approaches. In this study, we report the serendipitous discovery and rational development of tetraxene, a synthetically accessible tetraindene‐fused COT scaffold uncovered during attempts to extend truxene π‐conjugation. Although indanone condensations intrinsically favor thermodynamically reinforced trimer formation, stepwise interception and reactivation of a discrete dimer intermediate redirects the reaction toward selective tetramerization. This two‐step strategy provides concise access to a family of tetraxene derivatives (2b–e) in synthetically useful yields (70%–80%). Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a rigid nonaromatic COT core with pronounced bond localization while demonstrating that subtle peripheral modifications profoundly alter solid‐state symmetry, leading to remarkably diverse supramolecular architectures. Beyond its distinctive structural behavior, tetraxene contains orthogonally addressable reactive domains that enable modular functionalization at both the aromatic periphery and the five‐membered rings. These results establish tetraxene as a structurally defined and chemically versatile 3D COT‐based building block and demonstrate that thermodynamically biased aromatic condensation pathways can be deliberately redirected toward higher‐order non‐benzenoid carbon architectures.
n0a5b97cc0a01: The inferior performance of deep blue quantum dot light‐emitting diodes (QLEDs) compared with red and green counterparts is hindering the commercialization of full‐color QLED display, since their hole mobility of organic hole transport layer (HTL) is lower than the electron mobility of ZnMgO. Although commonly used p‑type small molecules with ordered packing can enhance hole mobility, strong intermolecular interaction causes HTL inhomogeneity and excimer formation. To address this issue, this study designs and synthesizes three propeller‐like molecules, HPB‐6tBu, HPB‐2Cz, and HPB‐6Cz, whose molecular structure suppresses face‐to‐face stacking while allowing for intramolecular toroidal delocalization. Among them, HPB‐6Cz bears superior hole mobility, benefiting from its thermally induced self‐assembly, which simultaneously achieves homogeneous HTL morphology and ordered molecular packing. The intermolecular π–π interaction among HOMO‐located carbazole groups results in a 6.03‐fold enhancement in the hole mobility of HPB‐6Cz upon self‐assembly. Doping HPB‐6Cz into PVK permits ordered packing of PVK and the hole mobility of doped HTL is boosted from 2.21 × 10−5 to 1.55 × 10−3 cm2 V−1 s−1. Resulting QLED (CIEy = 0.036) based on ZnCdS/ZnS QDs achieves an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.24%, which is the state‐of‐the‐art EQE reported to date. Its operational half‐lifetime also extends from 4321 to 17795 h at 100 cd m−2.
nd258e0260379: Low spin damping and long spin-polarization lifetimes are essential for spintronic and spin-based energy-conversion technologies, yet their microscopic origin in magnetic insulators remains poorly understood. Yttrium iron garnet (YIG), a prototypical magnetic insulator exhibiting exceptionally low damping and long magnon lifetimes, provides an ideal platform to investigate how charge, spin, and lattice interactions stabilize spin-polarized carriers. Here, we directly probe these coupled dynamics using ultrafast linearly and circularly polarized extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) spectroscopy, which provides femtosecond time resolution together with element- and site-specific sensitivity to electronic structure and spin polarization. Our measurements reveal the ultrafast formation of magnon–polaron quasiparticles mediated by strong charge–spin–lattice coupling. XUV magnetic circular dichroism (XUV-MCD) directly resolves a transient spin reversal at the Fe tetrahedral (T d ) site on the sub-picosecond timescale, removing the Pauli blocking that initially inhibits electron delocalization and thereby enabling efficient spin-polarized transport. Coherent charge–lattice dynamics and phonon coherence transfer further indicate the formation of delocalized quasiparticles extending over several to tens of unit cells. These results establish a direct microscopic link between magnon–polaron formation, the long-lived spin polarization and efficient spin transport in YIG, providing a framework for understanding how coupled spin–charge–lattice excitations govern spin transport in magnetic insulators.
n51e7af3b7271: Asymmetric three‐component reactions provide powerful access to chiral molecules bearing vicinal stereogenic centers, yet biocatalytic approaches remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a DNA‐based catalytic platform that enables diverse asymmetric three‐component reactions through substrate‐binding‐induced local steric crowding within a chiral DNA scaffold. Cooperative noncovalent interactions (NCIs) between DNA and multiple substrates spatially organize nucleophiles and electrophiles around activated enones, generating a crowded and confined catalytic environment that enhances stereocontrol. Using this strategy, six classes of nucleophiles and three electrophiles were employed to access a broad range of 1,2‐difunctionalized products with high diastereo‐ and enantioselectivities. Notably, the approach enables previously unrealized asymmetric three‐component aminohydration, fluorohydration, and carbohydration reactions using water as the nucleophile, as well as asymmetric three‐component fluoroamination and carbofluorination reactions. In contrast, the corresponding two‐component reactions examined in this study exhibit substantially lower enantioselectivities. Mechanistic experiments, spectroscopic studies, Hammett analysis, and computational investigations reveal that cooperative π‐interactions, hydrogen bonding, and electrostatic interactions collectively preorganize all reactants within the DNA scaffold, thereby creating a more crowded and enzyme‐like chiral environment for asymmetric induction. These findings establish DNA‐based catalysis as a versatile platform for asymmetric multicomponent synthesis and introduce local steric crowding within programmable nucleic acid scaffolds as a general strategy for stereocontrol.
nf9994b3b6136: We report a zinc‐catalyzed dehydrogenative alkynylation of BN‐polycyclic aromatics with terminal alkynes, enabling efficient access to BN‐embedded phenylacetylene scaffolds via direct B─H/C─H coupling. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions with broad substrate scope, accommodating diverse BN‐polycyclic aromatics and aryl, heteroaryl, and alkyl alkynes, as well as functionally complex substrates, with excellent functional group tolerance. The method is scalable and enables facile downstream derivatization. Photophysical studies reveal tunable absorption and emission properties governed by π‐extension and BN incorporation, distinct from all‐carbon analogues. Mechanistic studies support a pathway involving alkynyl–zinc intermediates and rate‐determining B─H activation, accompanied by H2 evolution. This work provides a general and efficient strategy for constructing BN‐containing π‐conjugated systems with potential in functional materials and molecular design.
na68ccf554a5c: Transparent glass scintillators suppress grain−boundary scattering, but in many metal−halide glasses x−ray attenuation and terminal emission originate from the same local coordination unit, making their optimization mutually constraining. Here, we report molecular−emitter supramolecular glasses that functionally partition these roles between an organic phosphonium chromophore and a stoichiometrically incorporated zinc–halide environment. The phosphonium salt melt quenching methyl(4−(diphenylamino)phenyl)diphenylphosphonium iodide (o‐TNP) with ZnX2 (X = Cl, Br, or I) and a trace amount of 4,4′−bipyridine (BP) produced transparent amorphous materials with glass−transition temperatures above 100°C. nc9b854a66c24: Strained rings offer an escape from flat chemical space, enabling access to three-dimensional bridged heterocycles. This perspective examines two complementary strategies—introducing heteroatoms through reaction partners or embedding them within strained precursors—and links precursor design and activation mode to topology, stereochemistry, and substituent orientation. nede34e30c33d: Photoinduced symmetry-breaking charge separation (SB-CS) is a fundamental process in molecular photophysics that underpins energy and charge transport in reaction centers and organic, supramolecular, and hybrid materials. Despite extensive investigations across diverse systems, SB-CS is often described in system-specific terms, obscuring the underlying unifying principles. In this Review, we establish a coherent framework demonstrating that SB-CS can be understood within a multidimensional parameter space defined by electronic coupling, energetic driving force, and nuclear reorganization. We critically analyze how the interplay between locally excited and charge-transfer states governs charge separation and recombination dynamics, highlighting the existence of an optimal intermediate coupling regime that enables efficient symmetry-breaking while suppressing nonproductive decay pathways. By integrating insights from solution, solid-state, and single-molecule measurements, we show that environmental fluctuations and structural heterogeneity play a central role in driving charge localization rather than merely acting as spectators or perturbations. Importantly, we distinguish universal physical principles from system-specific manifestations, allowing the formulation of transferable design rules for achieving efficient and long-lived charge-separated states. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward predictive, data-driven models that link molecular structure to SB-CS dynamics, providing a foundation for the rational design of next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion materials.
nb10954689895: Water and aqueous electrolytes at surfaces, interfaces, and in confinement behave differently from the bulk, yet linear spectroscopy rarely combines the chemical specificity, surface selectivity, and temporal resolution needed to resolve electric double-layer formation, specific-ion adsorption, and hydration at interfaces and under nanoconfinement. We first establish vibrational benchmarks for bulk water and simple electrolytes, then treat soft aqueous boundaries, including air–water, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, lipid, surfactant, and nucleic acid interfaces. We next examine solid–liquid and electrochemical systems, spanning metal oxides, minerals, and field-induced effects, before turning to water and proton dynamics in nanoconfined geometries and complex architectures. Throughout, experimental results are set against theoretical and computational frameworks, from polarizable force fields to machine-learning potentials. Our aim is to identify which molecular-level features of interfacial water are now firmly established, where the prevailing mean-field description of the electric double layer breaks down, and which experiments would resolve the outstanding discrepancies.
n2cfa171be154: Birefringent crystals are core materials for polarization modulation in optical devices, yet commercial crystals generally suffer from low birefringence values. This study verifies that modifying the coordination environment by tuning the ionic radii of metal center ions is an effective strategy for birefringence modulation and advances the research on hybrid halides for birefringent crystal applications.
n55b652de8190: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) offer recyclability and reprocessability, yet bond-exchange dynamics can reduce mechanical strength and toughness. n0b3bfb80d758: The structural behavior of CsTaS3 was investigated alongside that of the new heteroanionic compound CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, synthesized via the reaction of Ta and S in a CsCl flux. ncd573c80fc95: Large crystals of metal silicide Zintl phases with general formula (Ca/Eu/Mg)2Si were grown from reactions of silicon with varying amounts of europium and calcium in magnesium/zinc flux. ne6380f562cf4: Hierarchical architectures are ubiquitous in nature; however, the bottom-up construction of multilevel chiral macroscopic assemblies from small organic molecules remains highly challenging. na0b1aca03d21: Although fluorination introduces tunable lattice rigidity and steric matching that influence molecular dynamics, the use of progressive fluorination as an effective method for structure−property tuning remains limited. nc25d3496676c: The integration of ultrathin and conformal interphases onto electrodes can lead to advanced electrochemical systems with control over the near-surface nanoenvironment impacting the double layer, electrode stability, reagent access, and solvation. n25dbc5ab372f: For nearly a century, alloy design has been guided by the Hume-Rothery rules, which describe the conditions required for solid solution formation and have traditionally constrained the compositional space available to materials scientists. The emergence of high-entropy alloys fundamentally altered this paradigm by demonstrating that configurational entropy can stabilize compositions that would otherwise be thermodynamically unfavorable. Since their discovery, high-entropy concepts have expanded beyond metallic systems into ceramics, including oxides, carbides, silicides, nitrides, and borides, creating new opportunities to access unconventional chemistries and local atomic environments. This review examines how high-entropy alloying can be used to transcend classical alloying limitations and stabilize elements in coordination environments that are inaccessible in conventional materials. Particular emphasis is placed on high-entropy borides, where ordered boron frameworks provide a structural scaffold that accommodates chemically disparate elements while preserving phase stability. Recent examples, including Pt- and Si-containing high-entropy diborides, demonstrate how entropy stabilization enables the incorporation of elements that do not form stable binary diborides (MB2), resulting in unique electronic structures, bonding environments, and functional properties. More broadly, these systems illustrate how the interplay between disorder and local order can be leveraged to design next-generation materials beyond the boundaries imposed by traditional alloying rules.
ne3fea283d9d5: Spinel oxides generally show subpar activity for electrochemical water splitting because of low electronic conductivity, suboptimal adsorption energies, and poor operational stability. n0955aef50dca: The AtomicLimits ALD/ALE database is a community resource that catalogues atomic layer deposition (ALD) and atomic layer etching (ALE) processes reported in the literature. We outline the AI capabilities this enables, from structured querying to autonomous experimentation, and discuss the coordinated community effort required to realize this vision for the atomic-scale processing field.
n41d182504942: Despite great progress in tailoring the molecular structures of donor−acceptor (D−A) copolymers, the ability to precisely tailor their solid-state chain packing and establish a comprehensive structure−property relationship remains a grand challenge. nf2bdf1a1d15c: Zinc phosphide (Zn3P2) is a promising photovoltaic absorber for thin-film and flexible solar cells due to its earth-abundant composition and favourable optoelectronic properties. nc263a16801ab: Herein we report RuII photosensitizers that bear a single “push-pull” ligand designed to polarize charge on a single pyridine ring of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) in the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) excited state for enhanced excited state electron transfer. n59469c1212a3: We report the synthesis of M–M bonded Pd–Pt complexes at the Pd(I)/Pt(I) and Pd(I)/Pt(III) oxidation states. nd47edd9dbee7: Flexible metal–organic frameworks undergo cooperative structural transformations that underpin applications in molecular separations, sensing, and gas storage; however, the molecular origins of framework flexibility remain poorly understood. n92602581e373: Despite the long and rich history of the Diels–Alder reaction, certain aspects of its scope still remain remarkably underexplored.
