The synthetic utility of the method is further highlighted by concise asymmetric total syntheses of (−)-camphene, (−)-β-santalene, and (−)-(Z)-β-santalol from inexpensive starting materials.
n432c6af8f247: Selective drug activation in living systems remains a central challenge in targeted cancer therapy. Bioorthogonal catalysis addresses this by using abiotic transition-metal catalysts to unmask prodrugs at the tumor site, but the repertoire of suitable reactions remains limited. Here, we exploit the Buchner ring-expansion as a new uncaging strategy, in which a metal-carbene catalyzes a regioselective intramolecular ring-expansion followed by spontaneous 1,6-elimination to release a caged payload─a cascade with no biological equivalent. The iridium porphyrin complex [Ir(mPIX)Me] catalyzes this reaction at nanomolar concentrations, and the platform can accommodate structurally diverse payloads. As a proof of concept, functionalization with a bivalent human carbonic anhydrase IX (hCA IX) inhibitor enabled tumor-selective release of epirubicin (Epi) in a cancer cell model. This work thus delineates a new reaction class to the growing toolkit of transition-metal-mediated bioorthogonal chemistry.
n6b4519d1fff8: Converting methane to methanol (MTM) holds far-reaching practical implications, yet achieving both high productivity and high selectivity remains a longstanding challenge owing to the inertness of methane and the susceptibility of methanol to overoxidation. Here, we propose a continuous-flow irradiation system (CIS) by coupling radiation technology and flow chemistry for efficient MTM under ambient conditions. High-energy radiation promises direct methane activation in an oxidant-independent and catalyst-free manner with high efficiency, which enables its integration with continuous-flow synthesis that decouples CH4 activation from methanol formation in time and space, thereby preventing overoxidation and undesirable cascade side reactions. The CIS–MTM achieves a superior methanol production rate (68.3 μmol·h–1, at a dose rate of 7.2 kGy·min–1, 83.2 RH%, CH4 flow rate 60 mL·min–1) than most existing indirect activation routes, with economic scalability comparable to industrial methods. This work introduces radiation technology as a potential direct activation method for methane conversion.
n5b03b5f81fb2: Organic single-crystal heterostructures (OSCHs) constitute a promising platform for advanced flexible optoelectronics, yet imparting mechanical flexibility to these multiblock systems, especially given the susceptibility to failure at the interfaces between individual crystal segments, remains challenging. This obstacle is particularly aggravated at cryogenic temperatures, where the freezing of vibrational motion may cause brittleness and lead to mechanical failure. Herein, we describe an epitaxial growth strategy using molecular alloys for the fabrication of crystals of cryogenically flexible two-color (blue–cyan–blue) triblock heterostructures, prepared by growing triphenylene (TP) segments onto perylene (PER)-doped alloy seed crystals via crystallization under controlled cooling. The compatibility between the host and guest molecules provides interfaces with low defect densities. Analysis of the crystal structure reveals an abundance of weak intermolecular interactions that are thought to enable the reversible elastic deformation observed at both 298 and 77 K, thereby preventing cracking. Simultaneously, efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) between TP and PER enables continuous emission tuning and doping-ratio-controlled programmability of the optoelectronic properties. The resulting heterostructures not only support low-loss active optical waveguiding and programmable multichannel optical logic and information encoding but also remain fully operational for optical transduction during bending under cryogenic conditions. This work establishes a general molecular alloying approach to structures that integrate low-temperature mechanical compliance with sophisticated photonic functionalities, providing a pathway to deformable, multiemissive optoelectronics elements that remain operational in extreme environments.
nd8e74b73afe1: Sodium-ion batteries are attractive candidates for low-cost and scalable energy storage in which hard carbon (HC) anodes are used. However, sodium (Na) metal plating in HC anodes at voltages above the plating potential remains a critical problem. The location and spatial distribution of crystalline sodium (c-Na) metal nanoparticles, the clusters associated with Na storage in HCs, are important for understanding this underpotential plating behavior but remain unclear. Here, we implement a cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and electron tomography (cryo-ET) workflow that directly localizes c-Na metal clusters in sodiated HC samples: cryo-ET maps nanoscale three-dimensional (3D) distributions, while cryo-EM resolves local structure and chemistry. Our workflow reveals that c-Na metal clusters reside predominantly on the surfaces or near surfaces of individual HC particles. This finding challenges existing interpretations in the literature that locate the c-Na metal clusters within closed nanopores in the bulk of the HC, presumably because prior characterization using nonimaging techniques and two-dimensional (2D) projection images associated with traditional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) lacks the spatial 3D information necessary to resolve the full spatial distribution. Our discovery is an important step toward explaining the underpotential plating phenomenon of Na metal in HC anodes, suggesting that particle-level surface and near-surface interfaces are relevant targets to mitigate plating alongside bulk-pore, electrode, and electrolyte/interphase design.
n4a9e6597477b: Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination. Using l-glutamate (l-Glu) as a model, we demonstrate that with Cu nanowires as the bifunctional electrocatalyst, the system generates NH4+ and biologically active NADH in situ, driving the production of l-Glu under mild conditions. The coupled cascade not only shifts the reaction equilibrium forward but also provides a favorable orientation and a proton-rich environment for the bioactive cofactor, boosting overall selectivity of bioactive NADH. The modular design allows straightforward adaptation to diverse substrates and electrodes, demonstrating the broad generality of this platform. This work establishes a sustainable and versatile strategy for amino acid synthesis and opens new directions for electroenzymatic production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.
na6fb955bb3bb: Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a nonintuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.
n616ad993cb29: Light-driven CO2-to-chemical conversion presents a sustainable route for biomanufacturing, yet the performance of photosynthetic biohybrid systems remains fundamentally constrained by disorganized biotic–abiotic interfaces, which result in inefficient photoelectron transfer, low carbon production, and substantial cellular toxicity. Here, we report a spatially organized intracellular biohybrid system that enables the light-powered conversion of CO2 to 2,3-butanediol inEscherichia coli. Inspired by the algal pyrenoid, we constructed a TiO2/RuBisCO hybrid condensate (TRHC) by integrating protein liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) with in situ biomimetic mineralization. This spatially defined condensate physically clusters light-harvesting and carbon-fixing modules, thereby facilitating direct photoelectron transfer and contributing to improved long-term cellular robustness under continuous illumination. The TRHC achieved an apparent quantum yield of 12.4% and reduced the light-induced cellular mortality by 64%. By providing a robust photoelectron supply for CO2 assimilation, the integrated system attains a 2,3-butanediol yield of 1.38 mol/mol from the consumed glucose. Moreover, under illuminated fed-batch fermentation, the platform maintains sustained biosynthetic activity over 5 days, producing 62.11 g/L of 2,3-butanediol. This LLPS-guided strategy offers a generalizable framework for engineering efficient biotic-abiotic interfaces in solar-driven biomanufacturing.
nca7ba85a90b3: Selective removal of functional groups offers a powerful route to streamline molecular design and generate structural diversity. The use of such deletion strategies has surged in organic synthesis, yet achieving these transformations with high selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present a photoenzymatic platform for stereocontrolled C–CN bond cleavage of malononitriles, enabling access to diverse chiral nitriles. Directed evolution of the flavin-dependent enzyme OYE1 yielded a variant that efficiently converted a wide range of geminal dinitriles, affording products in high yields (up to >99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 3:97 e.r.). The platform was further extended to a one-pot cascade combining Michael addition with enzymatic decyanation. Mechanistic studies revealed a pathway involving a benzyl radical intermediate (Int1), followed by a carbanion species (Int2). This work establishes the first photobiocatalytic cyano group deletion strategy and provides a modular approach for sustainable synthesis of valuable chiral nitrile scaffolds.
na4f7103bb090: External pressure is a powerful tool for tuning hybrid metal halides (HMHs), yet the resulting structural and optical changes are usually reversible upon decompression. Locking pressure-accessed states through covalent bond formation, particularly while preserving single-crystallinity and optical functionality, remains challenging. Here, we report a pressure-induced single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SC-SC) [2 + 2] dimerization in a two-dimensional lead halide, (S-MAMBA)2PbBr4, which contains acrylate-functionalized S-MAMBA+ cations. This process yields a stable dimerized single-crystal phase upon decompression. The topochemically preorganized arrangement of S-MAMBA+ enables irreversible cyclobutane formation while preserving the crystallinity. High-pressure vibrational and diffraction measurements, together with recovered single-crystal structure determination, establish the pressure-induced bond-forming transformation. During compression, the emission evolves from self-trapped exciton (STE)-dominated to free-exciton (FE)-dominated recombination near the dimerization threshold, indicating a reconstructed excitonic pathway. After decompression, the dimerized phase shows irreversible optical reconstruction, characterized by opposite absorption and emission shifts. Density functional theory (DFT) reveals that this chemical transformation perturbs the inorganic-framework band-edge electronic structure through changes in organic–inorganic interactions and interlayer coupling. This work demonstrates that pressure can be used as a novel and powerful trigger for permanent bond and electronic structure reconstruction in hybrid materials.
n484b66814545: Mesoporous anisotropic nanohybrids (m-ANHs) have attracted growing interest because their structural asymmetry enables unique advantages in applications such as multidrug co-delivery and cascade catalysis. However, anisotropic growth in mesoporous systems has thus far been largely confined to an amorphous framework. Achieving regioselective growth of crystalline functional units integrated with mesoporous frameworks remains highly challenging, primarily because of the intrinsic competition at the heterointerface between crystal nucleation/deposition and micelle-directed mesostructural coassembly. Herein, we report an acidity-gated interfacial crystallization-coassembly switching strategy to construct single-crystalline mesoporous MOF (meso-MOF)-based ANHs. This strategy enables the site-selective growth of a new single-crystalline meso-MOF compartment at predefined heterointerfaces, yielding a diverse family of well-defined frame-like, dumbbell-like, and ternary spiny nanohybrids. Mechanistically, precise regulation of the HCl/CH3COOH ratio modulates the nucleation kinetics of MOF precursors, generating localized supersaturation that is sufficient to trigger site-selective heterogeneous nucleation. Concurrently, synchronization of MOF nucleation/growth with interfacial micelle-directed coassembly allows crystallization and mesopore organization to proceed cooperatively. The applicability of this interfacial regulation is demonstrated in several lattice-compatible and chemically stable MOF systems with different compositions and hybrid configurations. As a proof of concept, the hierarchical spiny topology significantly enhances physical bacteria–material interactions, endowing the ternary ANHs with superior antibacterial performance. Remarkably, even in the absence of any drug loading, the ANHs achieve an approximately 90% inhibition efficiency against drug-resistant bacteria. This work establishes a versatile route to regioselectively integrate single-crystalline mesoporous domains into complex anisotropic nanohybrids and highlights the functional potential of structurally programmed crystalline mesoporous interfaces.
n1e3051fecd2b: Nitrogen-centered radicals possessing substantial anionic character have remained highly challenging to isolate because of their intrinsic electronic instability in the absence of metal coordination. Herein, we report a family of stable N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-derived α-diimine radical cations that constitute a rare class of persistent organic radicals featuring pronounced anionic nitrogen-centered radical character. Combined crystallographic, EPR, electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal an unusual electronic structure in which the molecular framework is formally cationic whereas both the unpaired electron and substantial negative charge are predominantly localized on the α-diimine nitrogen atoms. These radicals exhibit remarkable stability, undergo selective proton- and hydrogen-atom-transfer reactions, and participate in fully reversible, stepwise interconversion among dicationic, radical cationic, and neutral redox states without degradation of the molecular framework. Two-electron reduction induces reversible C–N bond formation to generate either an azetidinimine or a zwitterionic structure, with their relative stability governed by remote electronic substituents. Variable-temperature spectroscopy, UV–Vis analysis, and DFT calculations reveal dynamic solution-state equilibria that can be thermodynamically tuned through peripheral electronic modulation. These findings establish a new design principle for persistent nitrogen-centered radicals and reveal how redox state, charge distribution, spin localization, and reversible covalent bond reorganization can be coupled within a metal-free molecular framework.
nc3b35eff382c: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), or “forever chemicals,” are emerging environmental contaminants often used as coatings. To provide a sustainable replacement, here we engineer the superhydrophobic lignin-integrated particle (SLIP), a bioinspired coating material based on natural plant water vasculature. SLIP coatings achieve superhydrophobic performance matching that of PFAS materials. Additionally, the SLIPs are demonstrated to be biodegradable and tolerant to abrasion and UV light exposure. SLIPs show significant environmental benefit over PFAS use through quantified social and environmental cost analysis.
n2536967af3f8: The 2026 Chemistry Nobel Prize celebrates how molecular handedness can be created and amplified. From a materials perspective, the award invites a wider question: can chiral crystal faces, pores, and minerals provide the asymmetric stage on which chemistry first learns to choose left from right?
n7585374a1700: Controlling interfacial energy transfer is central to hybrid optoelectronic and light-harvesting systems but is often limited by the short lifetime of donor excitations. Here, we show that dopant-induced exciton reservoirs regulate energy transfer. In Mn2+-doped CsPbX3 (X = Br, Cl) nanocrystals, vibrationally assisted delayed fluorescence (VADF) enables exciton capture, storage, and repopulation. This exciton recycling sustains energy transfer to molecular acceptors through Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET). Ultrafast transient absorption and time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of FRET efficiency on Mn concentration, consistent with an optimal regime of Mn-mediated exciton recycling. By tuning halide composition and temperature, we establish a correlation between VADF strength and energy-transfer efficiency, achieving up to a 4-fold enhancement in FRET. These findings identify exciton availability as a key control parameter for interfacial energy transfer and highlight exciton-reservoir engineering as a strategy for controlling energy flow in semiconductor nanostructures.
nd7621b3081db: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) materials that simultaneously exhibit large luminescence dissymmetry factors (glum), high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), and dynamic optical addressability remain highly sought after yet challenging to realize. Here, we establish a CQDs-CLCs photonic coupling platform via helical photonic confinement of narrowband-emissive carbon quantum dots (CQDs) in a chiral liquid crystal (CLC) host, enabling controlled emitter-photonic bandgap (PBG) spectral engineering. This yields amplified chiroptical signals with a glum of up to 1.12 and a figure of merit (FM = glum × PLQY) of 0.67. Beyond static performance, the helical photonic architecture allows dynamic CPL modulation by multiple stimuli, including temperature, light, electric field, mechanical pressure, viewing angle, and polarization. This work establishes helical photonic confinement as a material-photonic coupling strategy for decoupling dissymmetry amplification from emission efficiency while enabling multimodal stimulus-responsive modulation, offering potential applications in optical encryption, smart textiles, and photonic devices.
n4608e4aed51b: Magnetic particle hyperthermia relies on the efficient conversion of magnetic field energy into heat, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing this process within individual particles remain poorly understood. Here, we combine AC magnetometry experiments with dynamic micromagnetic simulations to connect microstructural features, magnetization dynamics, and macroscopic heat dissipation. We resolve heat generation at the intraparticle level, uncovering heterogeneous nanoscale heat-generation bursts with nanometer and nanosecond resolution. At a given particle size, grain size acts as an experimentally tunable parameter, balancing anisotropy disorder and pinning strength, thereby controlling both the magnitude and spatiotemporal distribution of heat release. Experiments show that flux-closure-dominated nanoflower architectures composed by larger grains generate more heat than their smaller-grain counterparts, whose deeper intraparticle pinning landscape redistributes heat generation over extended time windows. Together, our results provide a mechanistic framework linking nanoparticle microstructure to magnetic heating and establish design principles for optimizing nanoflowers as magnetic hyperthermia transducers.
nb69140aa4c9d: Two-dimensional (2D) spiral growth is crucial for scalable moiré superlattices, yet controlled large-area synthesis remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we report a rational epitaxial strategy for synthesizing oriented spiral WS2 films on a-plane sapphire, where unidirectionally aligned R-stacked domains serve as templates and substrate tilting acts as the key trigger for spiral growth. Comprehensive characterization confirms high density, identical crystallographic orientation, zero interlayer twist, well-defined R-stacking, and excellent crystalline quality across these structures. We propose a two-stage growth model: dual-coupling-guided formation of aligned R-stacked domains transitions into a dual-mode process for simultaneous lateral coalescence and vertical screw-dislocation-driven growth. The unique configuration of these oriented-spiral films endows photodetectors with superior performance and an extended spectral response. Our work represents a significant advance in 2D spiral materials, establishing a key step toward robust and scalable twistronics.
nd2187e3238da: Diamond synthesis from a graphite precursor is primarily constrained by the requirement for the simultaneous application of extreme pressures and temperatures. We explore the microstructural changes in highly oriented pyrolytic graphite subject to shear during room temperature compression. Using a diamond anvil cell, nonhydrostatic pressures of up to 160 GPa were applied, resulting in an optically transparent, diamond-like material above 80 GPa that reverted to an opaque, largely graphite-like material upon decompression. Detailed microstructural analysis of the recovered sample revealed nanoscale diamond-like domains embedded within a graphitic matrix containing shear bands and localized basal slip features consistent with a high shear environment. Employing a rotational diamond anvil cell greatly enhanced these shear-induced features, producing significant amounts of diamond in samples recovered from applied pressures as low as 15 GPa. These findings demonstrate that shear can facilitate the graphite-to-diamond transformation, enabling sp3 bond formation under conditions where extreme temperatures are not required.
n0e1d8a99ab72: Ratchets provide directed transport without global biased forces via parity-breaking combinations of nonequilibrium driving with dissipation or nonlinear dynamics. They play a central role down to the quantum level in molecular motors, colloidal particles, microbiological processes, semiconductor devices, optical lattices, and photonic structures, where nonequilibrium is usually achieved by dynamic potentials or couplings. Here, we address the question of whether transport can be achieved by only using time-dependent dissipation while keeping all potentials and couplings static. In this experiment-theory collaboration, we construct such non-Hermitian ratchets that solely rely on time- and space-periodic dissipation. Notably, the rectified transport increases with larger local dissipation. Floquet theory uncovers low-loss directional transport at suitable driving frequencies, which is linked to linear quasienergy bands. These regions are separated from nonresonant behavior by sharp transitions with characteristic exceptional points in the spectrum. A plasmonic Floquet-dissipative ratchet is studied experimentally by using real- and Fourier-space leakage radiation microscopy.
n97add992c8e9: The para-C–H activation of free aromatic carboxylic acids without directing groups remains a challenging task. Now, the authors report on an iridium-based catalytic system that leverages the synergistic effect of multi-noncovalent interactions to overcome this issue, enabling direct access to para-functionalized carboxylic acids and their derivatives.
n39728f0d6aac: The isolation of oxoboranes (RB≡O) featuring a genuine B–O triple bond has remained an outstanding challenge owing to the electron deficiency of boron and the intrinsic instability of the B≡O linkage. So far, direct evidence for such species has been largely limited to gas-phase and matrix-isolation studies and only recently inferred in solution. Here we report the isolation of a stable, free oxoborane generated via a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation of a heterocumulene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes a terminal B≡O unit, while electronic structure analyses reveal two orthogonal π bonds consistent with a highly polarized triple bond. Mechanistic studies support a carbon monoxide coordination–insertion–isomerization pathway. The resulting oxoborane exhibits ambiphilic reactivity, enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives. These findings establish free oxoboranes as isolable species under condensed-phase conditions and provide a platform for exploring low-coordinate boron–oxygen multiple bonds. The isolation of oxoboranes featuring a genuine B–O triple bond is challenging owing to the instability of the B≡O linkage. Now stable crystalline oxoboranes have been prepared through a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation, revealing a highly polarized B–O triple bond and enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives through ambiphilic reactivity.
n02d3dfe40622: Oxoboranes, molecules bearing a triple bond between a dicoordinate boron atom and a monocoordinate oxygen atom, are some of the longest-sought reactive main-group species. Their syntheses have been the subject of a series of documented attempts dating back to at least the early 1960s, leading to gas-phase/matrix isolation and evidence of chemical trapping, as well as isolation of oxoborane derivatives with reduced B–O bond orders. However, their detection or isolation of base-/acid-free oxoboranes in the condensed phase remains challenging. Here we present a remarkably simple synthesis of three oxoboranes that are stable as crystalline solids at room temperature. These species feature exceptionally short (1.208(4)–1.217(4) Å) and strong B–O bonds. Their properties are elucidated by both experimental and computational methods, and an explanation for their unusual stability is provided. Oxoboranes are among the longest-sought species in main-group chemistry. Now, stable crystalline oxoboranes with exceptionally short and strong B–O bonds have been prepared through the reaction of a diboracumulene with carbonyl-bearing compounds.
n4c9e68be9b0c: Energy poverty is a growing concern, but we still know little about which measures actually improve people’s health and living conditions. Here the authors find that structural measures and consistent financial support deliver the clearest benefits.
ncba5523cca40: The microscopic origin of ionic memory in two-dimensional (2D) nanofluidic memristors remains debated. Voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of 2D nanofluidic channels is identified to trigger memristive hysteresis leading to nonlinear ion transport in the channels.
n4c660f8c68f6: Intrinsic electric polarization in III-nitride semiconductors is an advantage for large-scale optoelectronic devices but remains largely unexplored in sensory-memristive devices. Polarization-induced spatial separation of photogenerated carriers at the interfaces of III-nitride heterostructures enables efficient and scalable in-sensor computing at room temperature.
n910f94bd03f6: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognised the status of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) at the forefront of materials chemistry. The increased visibility brought by such recognition, however, also calls for renewed attention to the fundamentals, reminding us that being on everyone’s lips should not lead us to overlook the basics. Here, we wish to turn the spotlight on what is possibly the most fundamental aspect of all, that is, the determination of the chemical composition of MOFs. We provide a brief overview of routine analytical methods and a series of suggestions for deriving the chemical formula.
na4f04bdd8985: Efficient interfacial electron transfer from light-harvesting semiconductors to molecular catalysts remains a major challenge in molecular–semiconductor hybrid photocatalytic CO2 reduction, particularly for narrow-bandgap semiconductors, whose reduced thermodynamic driving force often requires assistance from metallic electron-transfer mediators such as Ag. Here, we show that, despite its narrow bandgap of 2.1 eV, the layered perovskite oxynitride K2LaTa2O6N (KLTON) functions as an effective semiconductor support for a supramolecular RuRu′ CO2-reduction catalyst without relying on Ag nanoparticles. The RuRu′/KLTON hybrid selectively converted CO2 to formate under visible-light irradiation with >99% selectivity, a turnover number of 691, and an apparent quantum yield of 6.1 ± 0.6% at 420 nm. Loading a small amount of Ag further increased the turnover number to 1077, but this 1.5-fold enhancement was modest compared with the larger Ag-induced activity enhancements reported for several conventional oxynitride-based hybrids, highlighting the weak Ag dependence of the KLTON-based system. Spatial photodeposition of Ag and MnOx revealed spatially differentiated surface redox reactivity on the terraced layered structure of KLTON, while time-resolved microwave conductivity and transient infrared absorption measurements showed favorable photogenerated-carrier dynamics and demonstrated that Ag loading modifies the electron dynamics of KLTON. Time-resolved emission measurements further revealed an additional nonradiative decay pathway at the Ru(II) photosensitizer/KLTON interface, consistent with interfacial electronic interaction without uniquely assigning its microscopic origin. These results identify favorable carrier dynamics and weak Ag dependence as key features of the KLTON-based molecular hybrid and highlight layered narrow-bandgap mixed-anion semiconductors as promising support materials for visible-light-driven molecular photocatalysis.
nc9503e1589c4: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have attracted considerable interest, displaying impressive performance for a wide plethora of electrocatalytic reactions. However, the important question whether isolated sites are always beneficial remains unresolved. Here, by using the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) as a model reaction, we examine how isolated single-atom metal sites restrict the adsorption mode of intermediates to the monodentate configuration, which leads to weak intermediate stabilization and poor reaction kinetics. This contrasts with bulk metal sites where availability of the bidentate adsorption configuration offers better intermediate stabilization and dehydrogenation kinetics. As a result, Ir, Pt, and Pd SACs were found to require high HzOR overpotentials of 0.90, 1.21, and 1.19 V at 3 mA cm–2, respectively. Comparatively, their Ir, Pt, Pd nanoparticle counterparts with similar metal loading exhibit considerably lower overpotentials of only 0.35, 0.83, and 0.64 V at 3 mA cm–2, respectively. Taken together, our work contributes towards a more complete understanding of SACs, emphasizing the importance of considering site structure and the mechanistic demands of the reaction.
n30461fef956f: Nonoxidative butane dehydrogenation offers a direct route to C4 olefins, yet it remains challenged by the need to promote C–H activation while ensuring olefin desorption and suppressing C–C cracking. Here, we report a mechanism-guided study that combines density functional theory calculations with experimental validation to rationally design Rh-based catalysts for butane dehydrogenation. A series of Rh models with distinct geometric configurations on a graphene surface, including isolated Rh atom, fully exposed Rh2 and Rh3 clusters, and extended Rh surfaces, were constructed to elucidate the structure–activity relationship. The calculations reveal a volcano-type dependence of dehydrogenation activity on the Rh geometric configuration. Fully exposed Rh3 clusters exhibit optimal energetics for sequential C–H activation, whereas isolated Rh atoms and Rh nanoparticles show inferior activity. Experimental studies on Rh/nanodiamond@graphene catalysts confirm the prediction, demonstrating that fully exposed Rh clusters with an average Rh–Rh coordination number of approximately 1.9 achieve the best balance between C–H activation, olefin desorption, and C–C bond cleavage suppression. This study highlights highly efficient Rh active sites by regulating the geometric configuration and electronic property and provides a general strategy for designing dehydrogenation catalysts.
nf665f23a53b9: Directed evolution of enzymes is generally performed toward a specific substrate, which predictably improves enzyme activity toward the probe substrate. However, it is difficult to predict whether evolved enzymes will be selective or promiscuous toward other substrates. Multiplexed directed evolution can identify enzyme variants with selectivity/promiscuity across multiple substrates, but is typically performed using plate-based screening assays that are limited to testing a few hundred mutants. Combining substrate multiplexing with ultrahigh-throughput evolution technologies is a promising avenue for deeper exploration of the mutational landscape, but it has not been investigated whether enzymes evolved using multiplexed ultrahigh-throughput methods exhibit selectivity/promiscuity toward a broader scope of small-molecule substrates beyond the probes used during evolution. Here, we performed multiplexed ultrahigh-throughput evolution of Bacillus subtilis (BS2) esterase, merging yeast surface display with masked acid chloride probes, to identify a panel of mutants with improved selectivity toward the phenylcyclopropyl (pCP) ester protecting group relative to not only the probe substrate, but also a broad panel of 90 additional esters. Additionally, we applied the platform to identify a promiscuous mutant with improved activity across a broad substrate scope. Finally, we applied the highly pCP-selective BS2 variant, together with a selective variant for the methylcyclopropyl (mCP) ester protecting group, to demonstrate proximity labeling in mammalian cells with two orthogonal enzyme/probe systems, opening new opportunities in multiplexed proximity labeling. Overall, this study presents an efficacious method to identify enzyme variants with desired selectivity profiles that may be extended to multiple applications in chemical biology and synthesis.
n6a9ec78b6cd0: Given the thermodynamic stability of the C(sp2)–O bond, the development of simple and efficient strategies for its functionalization holds significant practical value. In this study, we report an electroreductive, one-pot nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) of aryl/alkenyl triflates with diverse (1°, 2°, and 3°) alkyl bromides. Rapid in situ generation of Ni0 species enables efficient activation of the C(sp2)–O bond, yielding a broad range of C(sp2)–C(sp3) coupling products. Notably, the ligand functions as an organo-mediator to assist alkyl halide activation and prevent the over-reduction of substrates. This protocol is distinguished by its broad substrate scope, scalability, and mild reaction conditions.
n2c136e03ac1b: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) are generally considered C1-selective in CO2/CO electroreduction, as spatially isolated sites cannot efficiently sustain adjacent CO-derived intermediates required for C─C coupling. Here we show that this selectivity bias is not intrinsic to atomically dispersed Cu, but depends on single-atom site density. Across a series of Cu–N3O catalysts with different Cu site densities, increasing site density drives a clear selectivity crossover from H2 and CH4 formation to C2+ products. The total C2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) rises from 9.6% on the low-density to 78.1% on the high-density at 1 bar CO, and further reaches 87.7% at 7 bar CO, whereas the low-density remains C1-selective. In situ attenuated-total-reflection surface enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that dense Cu single atoms sustain a larger *COatop population and simultaneously shift interfacial water from strongly hydrogen-bonded species towards free-water-rich configurations. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that higher site density stabilizes CO-containing surface states and lowers the barrier of the acetate-forming pathway. These findings identify a CO-rich and proton-accessible interfacial state that favors C─C coupling over C1 hydrogenation, establishing site density as a structural descriptor for multicarbon electrosynthesis on single-atom catalysts.
n5037ea9f1f9d: Sluggish charge dynamics and poor *NO polarization at active sites hinder the efficiency of photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (PcNRA). To address these issues, an atomic-level regulation strategy synergizing facet engineering with axial coordination was developed. Specifically, isolated Cu sites were anchored onto an electron-rich, ultrathin BiVO4 substrate exposing (040) facets. Functionalized ligands featuring distinct donor heteroatoms (S, N, O) were then systematically introduced, yielding a series of single-atom catalysts (S/N/O-Cu/BVO) with tailored axial microenvironments. A comprehensive methodology combining multidimensional spectroscopy and computational chemistry was established to verify this single-atom axial coordination. Detailed analyses of characteristic binding energies and absorption edge shifts via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and synchrotron X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) identified localized coordination field effects. Crucially, these effects are distinct from conventional electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI), providing spectroscopic confirmation of successful axial ligand incorporation and guiding the prediction of their configurations. Building upon these spectral findings, density functional theory (DFT) models were constructed and optimized, conclusively validating the asymmetric axial coordination configurations within the system, specifically Cu-S2O1, Cu-N2O1, and Cu-O4. Catalytic evaluations demonstrated that S-Cu/BVO achieves the highest ammonia yield at 435 μmol·h–1·g–1. In-situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations elucidated the multidimensional synergistic mechanism driving this enhanced activity: (1) The prominently exposed (040) facets act as an interfacial electron sink, efficiently directing photogenerated electrons toward the Cu sites; (2) The axial S ligands reconstruct the electronic structure of the Cu centers via strong orbital coupling, thereby improving effective orbital overlap with nitrate; (3) The resulting asymmetric Cu-NO-S bridging configuration polarizes the critical *NO intermediate, substantially lowering the kinetic barrier for the rate-determining step.
nb4ac1e412542: The article explores the catalytic potential of the emerging class of Janus-type di-N-heterocyclic carbenes that have attracted attention in recent times. The article details different aspects of these Janus-type di-N-heterocyclic carbenes particularly from their classifications, expansion in synthesis approaches, to finally their utility in different homogeneous transformations.
n2515ce2b234a: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.
n80c758399425: Management of disparate chronic epithelial diseases relies on fragmented site-specific protocols yet remains hindered by common pathological barriers and sustained inflammation. Herein, we developed a top-down strategy to exfoliate short nanofibrils from Antheraea pernyi silk fibers featuring inherent Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) motifs, followed by in situ growth of Au nanoparticles. The resulting platform (Au@ASFs) achieved superior spatial adaptability via catalytic oxygen propulsion, navigating across barriers to reach deep-seated lesions. Once localized, Au@ASFs provided phase-spanning multifunctional therapy through near-infrared (NIR)-triggered photothermal sterilization. Through RGD–integrin interactions, they also promoted hemostasis and M2 macrophage polarization to resolve persistent inflammation while enhancing fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and neuronal differentiation. In vivo, Au@ASFs (+NIR) significantly improved closure of infected diabetic oral ulcers from 43.1 to 95.5% by day 7 and restored colon length in ulcerative colitis from 66.3 to 97.7% of healthy controls. In infected diabetic wounds, Au@ASFs (+NIR) increased closure from 63.8 to 89.1% by day 14. Transcriptomic analysis of wound tissues revealed reprogramming through suppressed NF-κB inflammatory signaling, activated Wnt5a/GSK-3β signaling for neuronal differentiation, and modulated PI3K-Akt signaling for tissue regeneration. Collectively, Au@ASF (+NIR) consistently resolves chronic epithelial diseases across disparate anatomical sites, establishing a unified drug-free paradigm that transcends site-specific constraints.
n6bfe06cebdf4: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is driven by amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation and a cascade of interconnected neurotoxic events, including oxidative stress, glutamate excitotoxicity, calcium dysregulation, and impaired neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling. To address the multifactorial nature of AD pathology, chiral d- or l-cysteine-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) nanoparticles are developed as a multitarget nanotherapeutic platform. Both enantiomers effectively inhibit Aβ aggregation, scavenge reactive oxygen species, reduce extracellular glutamate levels, and attenuate calcium dysregulation. In parallel, d/l-Cys-COFs rescue compromised neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling, as evidenced by normalized expression of neuropeptide Y and brain-derived neurotrophic factor. In transgenic AD mice, d/l-Cys-COF treatment significantly improves memory and cognitive performance. Notably, the d-enantiomer affords superior neuroprotection through enhanced suppression of pathological intracellular calcium overload, whereas restoration of neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling remains chirality-independent. These findings identify chirality as a key design element for multitarget nanotherapeutics against AD, with enantioselective efficacy arising primarily from differential regulation of calcium dysregulation and shared restoration of neuroactive signaling contributing to the overall therapeutic benefit.
nc14d1c48363d: Giant optical nonlinearities enable advanced materials control and bridge exotic light-matter phenomena to next-generation photonics. However, materials exhibiting strong higher-order optical nonlinearity beyond the second order are typically rare. Here, we report the discovery of a giant and ultrafast second-harmonic generation (SHG) in self-assembled polar skyrmions under mid-infrared excitations. The transient SHG intensity exhibits a distinctive power dependence originating from higher-order nonlinearity. More generally, we show that large higher-order nonlinearity emerges across diverse domain structures in polar superlattices. Phase-field simulations demonstrate a strong and periodic local permittivity variation within each polar texture at equilibrium, and further confirm the fast polarization oscillation in polar skyrmions with mid-infrared excitations. This intense local permittivity modulation can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions, unlocking dramatically enhanced nonlinear optical responses without photonic engineering. Consequently, the self-assembled polar topologies with strong inherent optical nonlinearity could establish a platform for quantum information processing and high-speed optical communications.
n9cadf3617cd8: Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. However, a predictive understanding of how dynamic charge regulation at the nanoscopic scale influences ionic mobility in these polymer networks remains elusive. Here, using large-scale molecular simulations, we dissect the coupled mechanisms governing small-ion transport in weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels, and reveal how charge density, competitive binding, and dynamic charge regulation jointly control ion mobility. By systematically isolating these effects, we uncover a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence of ion self-diffusion on hydrogel pKa and salt concentration for multivalent ions. Strikingly, allowing the hydrogel backbone to dynamically regulate its charge eliminates this nonmonotonicity and leads to dramatic enhancements in ion mobility, with diffusion coefficients increasing by more than a factor of 2 for trivalent ions. We attribute this effect to a protonation-assisted hopping mechanism that continuously remodels the local electrostatic landscape, providing an additional molecular-scale pathway for ion unbinding beyond translational escape and accelerating ion-pair kinetics without affecting the fraction of free ions. Our results demonstrate that dynamic nanoscale charge regulation can decouple ion mobility from equilibrium binding strength, offering a powerful design lever unavailable in fixed-charge materials. Building upon these insights, we propose simple molecular design principles for next-generation ion-conducting hydrogels and suggest alternative strategies for nanostructured membranes, energy materials, and biologically inspired charge-adaptive soft matter.
ncf528759a6ea: The deterministic realization of quantum light sources operating at telecom wavelengths is essential for long-distance fiber-based quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate that telecom O-band emission can be achieved from site-controlled InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots (QDs). Our concept utilizes a buried AlAs/AlOx stressor layer with the unique feature of inducing a well-defined and controllable tensile strain field at the growth surface, enabling both site-selective nucleation at the mesa’s centers and a redshift of QD emission to the ∼1.3 μm wavelength range. This concept not only eliminates the need for strain-reducing layers (SRLs), which are known to degrade optical coherence, but also provides spatial control and spectral tunability. The grown telecom QDs show single-photon emission with g(2)(0) = (5.0 ± 1.0) × 10–2 at 4 K and (2.8 ± 0.3) × 10–1 at 77 K, demonstrating the quantum nature and thermal stability of the emitters. The emission characteristics of complex excitonic states are analyzed using 8-band k·p and configuration-interaction modeling, which quantitatively reproduces the experimental observations. Finally, we present a theory-supported strategy to further redshift the emission toward the center of the O-band and beyond by employing a multiburied stressor approach. This combined framework of experiment and theory establishes the buried stressor concept as a scalable route toward highly coherent, position-controlled O-band quantum emitters compatible with scalable photonic integration.
n2d3fc4f248f9: Enantioselective chiroptical sensing is gaining traction across various applications. However, intrinsic molecular chiroptical responses are weak, and existing amplification approaches add synthesis, manufacturing, or operational complexity that limits sensitivity and scalability. Here, we present an enantioselective sensing paradigm merging adsorption-driven chirality induction with large-scale optical transduction in twisted stacks of aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) films. Chiral molecules adsorb onto CNTs to form chiroptically active composites that are macroscopically assembled by alignment and rotational stacking, yielding large ultraviolet circular dichroism (CD). We resolve enantiomer handedness and quantify concentration in single-enantiomer aqueous solutions using a single sensor without lithography, hotspot delivery, or a paired opposite-handed reference. We achieve high sensitivity with estimated sub-μM minimum detectable concentrations for glucose and provide a proof-of-concept demonstration with alanine. Neither analyte-only solution shows detectable CD under the present measurement conditions. We demonstrate Langmuir-type adsorption behavior using molecular dynamics simulations and reproduce experimental results using optical simulations. This platform provides a foundation for future development toward cost-effective in situ enantiomer monitoring in aqueous environments.
n07d59c17c264: Defect‐mediated nonradiative recombination remains a major barrier to efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Although considerable advances have been made with molecular additives, how the spatial arrangement of functional groups affects device performance remains largely unexplored. Here, we present a regioisomerism‐guided molecular design strategy using fluorinated aniline as a well‐defined model system to incorporate into the lead iodide (PbI2) precursor solution during two‐step sequential perovskite deposition. By systematically comparing ortho‐, meta‐, and para‐fluoroaniline, we demonstrate that the ortho isomer, 2‐fluoroaniline (2‐FA), affords the most effective regulation of defect states and device performance. This superiority arises from the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen bond, which redistributes the molecular electrostatic potential and confers stable bidentate coordination with the perovskite lattice. Additionally, 2‐FA facilitates high‐quality α‐FAPbI3 films and aligns the energy level favorably with the hole transport layer, yielding a champion efficiency of 26.05% for the n‐i‐p PSCs. Moreover, the 2‐FA‐containing device exhibits superior operational stability. This regioisomerism‐guided design works universally across n‐i‐p and p‐i‐n architectures, irrespective of one‐step or two‐step fabrication. Our work establishes regioisomerism as a simple yet powerful molecular design principle for molecular engineering and provides new insight into the rational development of efficient and stable PSCs.
nd5212608b6f2: Gas evolution from lattice oxygen release is a major obstacle to deployment of high‐energy‐density cathodes, yet its structural origin within dense electrodes remains challenging to resolve across multiple length scales. This difficulty arises because gas evolution is the collective outcome of oxygen release from numerous grains and particles, whose environments can vary across electrode, secondary‐particle, and grain scales. Here, by integrating online electrochemical mass spectrometry with synchrotron X‐ray and electron microscopy, this study resolves the spatial origin of O2 evolution through mapping Mn reduction, a chemical fingerprint of oxygen release, across four orders of magnitude in length scale. Two lithium‐manganese‐rich layered oxide (LMR) electrodes that vary only in secondary‐particle size are employed as a model system, and their O2 evolution differs twofold. Spatially resolving Mn oxidation state distribution reveals no detectable Mn‐reduction gradient across the electrode thickness or within particles, indicating that the difference does not originate from electrode‐ or particle‐scale heterogeneity. Instead, frontal facets (lithium‐intercalation planes) of grains exhibit deeper Mn reduction and surface reconstruction than lateral facets, consistent with favorable oxygen vacancy formation and migration. O2 evolution matches after frontal‐facet area normalization, identifying frontal‐facet exposure as a key structural descriptor for O2 evolution in these practical LMR electrodes.
nea6d807547a9: Aryl boronate esters are ubiquitous in synthesis and are efficiently produced by C–H borylation. However, there are no reported methods to date that convert arenes into vicinal bis‐boronate ester derivatives by double C–H borylation. Instead, all current routes require pre‐functionalized arene precursors. Vicinal bis‐boronate esters are highly desirable, as arenes with this substitution pattern are pervasive in biologically active compounds and organic materials. Herein we show that boron electrophiles derived from tetrahalo‐pyrazaboles (X2B(μ‐pyrazole)2BX2) and AlX3 (X = Cl or Br) affect the regioselective vicinal double C–H borylation of arenes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). This afforded diborylated products that were notable in their own right, representing novel cationic PAHs containing an unusual cyclic C2B2N2 unit. A subsequent pinacol installation step then affords the vicinal bis‐boronate ester‐substituted arene/PAH. A wide range of arenes and PAHs were shown to undergo highly regioselective one‐pot conversion to the vicinal bis‐boronate ester‐substituted products, of which multiple were unprecedented before this work. Overall, this work is the first, to our knowledge, double C–H borylation methodology to form vicinal bis‐boronate ester‐substituted arenes/PAHs and therefore is a useful addition to the synthetic chemist's toolbox given the considerable utility of organoboranes.
nb3c1666159c3: A novel and convenient set of conditions is reported for the generation of alkenylcopper reagents via 1,3‐Brook rearrangement of alkenylsilane derivatives formed by ruthenium catalyzed trans‐hydrosilylation of propargyl alcohol derivatives. The reactive intermediates can evolve in a stereospecific manner into allenes; this new approach is catalytic in copper and proceeds with faithful chirality transfer from the stereocenter of the substrate to the axially chiral product. The overall stereochemical course resulting from trans‐hydrosilylation followed by an anti‐elimination step is complementary to that of most protocols for allene synthesis starting from propargylic alcohols known in the literature. Alternatively, the transient organocopper species can be intercepted with a variety of electrophiles to give a wide range of substituted alkene derivatives. In this latter embodiment, the sequence of hydrosilylation/Brook rearrangement presents an opportunity for regioselective net trans‐hydrofunctionalization of alkynes, a field that has so far been dominated by less benign organotin chemistry.
n20d17a3af376: When [Cp*Ru(MeCN)3]PF6 is used as the catalyst for the trans‐hydrosilylation of propargyl alcohol derivatives, the silyl group is transferred with appreciable levels of regioselectivity to the alkyne C‐atom distal to the protic substituent. A copper‐mediated 1,4‐Brook rearrangement converts the resulting alkenylsilanes into alkenylcopper species, which can be intercepted with a multitude of carbon‐ or heteroatom‐based electrophiles; this formal ipso‐substitution of the R3Si‐group allows a variety of trisubstituted olefins to be formed in stereodefined format, including fluoroalkenes and olefins bearing trifluoromethyl substituents. Best results are obtained with copper amides such as [Cu(NEt2)]4 as the promoter in THF/DMPU; they are sufficiently basic to deprotonate the ─OH group in the first place, thereby triggering the critically important C‐to‐O silyl migration, yet mild enough to ensure compatibility with a variety of functional groups, including even C─H acidic sites adjacent to an ester or ketone. In cases where the trapping of the organocopper intermediates primarily formed is unduly slow or inefficient, the addition of either 2‐thienyllithium or tetra‐n‐butylammonium cyanide is recommended; these additives lead to more highly nucleophilic cuprate species that show the right reactivity profile for efficient coupling of otherwise noncompliant electrophilic partners.
nd6b5cea12d49: CO dehydrogenases (CODH) are metalloenzymes that reversibly oxidize CO to CO2 at a buried NiFe4S4 active site. The substrates, CO and CO2, need therefore to be transported through the protein matrix to reach the active site. The most likely pathway for intra‐protein diffusion is the hydrophobic channel identified in the crystal structures. We used site‐directed mutagenesis in an extensive manner to study the role of the highly conserved isoleucine 563 of Thermococcus sp. AM4 CODH2. Certain substitutions significantly change the biochemical properties of the enzyme (KM for CO, catalytic efficiency, product inhibition constant, catalytic bias, …), and increase its resistance to the inhibitor O2, showing that isoleucine 563 plays a key role in determining access to the active site. The mutations have the same effects on the rates of binding of CO and O2, showing that the two molecules follow the same pathway and are not discriminated by the protein matrix. The I563F mutation decreases the bimolecular rate constant of inhibition by O2 15‐fold and increases the IC50 20‐fold. This is the strongest improvement in O2 resistance reported so far, but it comes at the cost of reduced substrate affinity.
nede8bcb79f17: The dissolution/deposition energy storage path of MnO2 cathodes involves two‐electron transfer and provides doubled theoretical capacity of the typical one‐electron transfer reaction. However, its reaction activity and contribution in aqueous Zn batteries are seriously limited. Herein, we present a dual redox mediator (RM) concept to catalyze both of the reduction/oxidation reaction directions of this two‐electron transfer path. Uniquely, the 2,2,6,6‐tetramethylpiperidine‐1‐oxyl (TEMPO) compound features two pairs of redox couples with potentials below and above that of the MnO2 cathode. TEMPO also exhibits facile conversion kinetics during both electrochemical processes and chemical reactions with Mn‐active materials via two‐electron transfer. These properties allow TEMPO to catalyze the dissolution/deposition between MnO2/Mn2+ using either redox couple, respectively. The substituent group on the TEMPO molecule further determines its functioning stabilities. As a result, the optimal TEMPO dual RM enables the MnO2 cathode to achieve a high capacity of 517 mAh g−1 at 0.3 A g−1 and 80.4% capacity retention after 20 000 cycles at 10 A g−1 in typical Swagelok‐type Zn batteries. The electrolytic‐type battery also realizes a high areal capacity up to 80 mAh cm−2 with 105 mWh cm−2 energy density. This work provides an effective dual RM concept toward high‐performance Zn–Mn batteries.
nc718e5ceda49: Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries are promising energy storage systems. However, the voltage is limited in mild acidic electrolytes, while alkaline electrolytes lead to severe passivation at both electrodes. Herein, we optimize zinc–iodine battery systems by tailoring the redox couples of both electrodes based on the Pourbaix diagrams. The I–I2/I3 − cathode couple, which stays stable up to the pH of 9.5, is applied due to its facile kinetics over I−–IO3 −. Meanwhile, considering the decreasing redox potential of Zn anode in the alkaline region, the Zn–Zn(NH3)4 2+ couple is selected with pH adjusted toward the cathode boundary of 9.3 by ammonium. This reaction pathway also fundamentally avoids ZnO passivation. The resulting optimal mild alkaline system achieves 1.6 V average voltage, exceeding both mild acidic and strong alkaline electrolytes. A quaternary ammonium cation is further employed to inhibit polyiodide dissolution from the cathode and suppress hydrogen evolution reaction at the anode. Consequently, the zinc–iodine battery realizes 2.13 mAh cm−2 capacity at 3 mA cm−2 and retains 1.08 mAh cm−2 capacity at 20 mA cm−2, together with low overpotentials of 0.06 and 0.21 V, respectively. It also achieves 93.6% capacity retention for 2000 cycles with 99.2% coulombic efficiency and 88.3% energy efficiency.
n27e2f0def1b4: Being an iconic spherical molecule exclusively composed of sp 2 carbon atoms, the development of increasingly efficient synthetic receptors for C60 fullerene remains a pressing challenge in supramolecular chemistry. However, as tighter hosts that employ most of their cavity volumes to complementarily encapsulate C60 are developed, steric constraints may emerge that mechanically trap this ball-shaped guest within their lumen. Here we explore this unprecedented scenario with a rigid bisporphyrin sp2 -receptor that acts as a “mechanical jail” for C60. This exceptional host presents the tightest 3D cavity reported for this spherical guest, occupying 77% of the internal volume and enabling strong π–π and CH⋯π interactions, which result in exceptionally high binding affinities (Ka > 109 M− 1). Unlike related cage and basket analogues, encapsulation in this perfectly fitted host is kinetically hindered, leading to guest release dynamics that are extremely slow above 400 K and essentially suppressed at room temperature.
n2d9e3215a61f: We report a portal‐preorganized cucurbit[7]uril (CB7)‐ruthenium conjugate that reprograms CB7 recognition without modifying the host cavity itself. Covalent integration of a tris(2,2′‐bipyridine)ruthenium(II) chromophore at the CB7 portal yields the unimolecular receptor CB7‐Rubpy, in which guest binding is directly coupled to emission. The proximal Ru chromophore attenuates binding of classical polycationic CB7 guests while enhancing recognition of aromatic peptide and protein motifs, producing a selectivity shift of nearly two orders of magnitude relative to native CB7. CB7‐Rubpy thereby converts CB7 from a charge‐selective host into a motif‐selective receptor for aromatic protein epitopes, displaying high affinity for insulin (Ka = 1.5 × 107 M−1) and submicromolar detection capability. The same motif‐selective recognition enables monitoring of aromatic motif accessibility during protein refolding. These findings establish portal‐preorganized chromophore integration as a design strategy for coupling selectivity tuning and signal transduction in CB‐based receptors.
nd81ccc0af4a8: Acyl anion‐based umpolung is a foundational strategy in synthetic chemistry that enables reversal of the intrinsic electrophilic polarity of carbonyl compounds. Although acyl anion chemistry has been well developed, translating this polarity‐inversion concept to heavier main‐group congeners has remained elusive. Here we report the synthesis of a silicon/sulfur analogu of an acyl anion through a distinctive four‐electron reductive rearrangement of an arylthiotribromosilane precursor. Structural and computational analyses reveal a polarized Si═S interaction and lone pair at the silicon center, endowing it with acyl‐anion‐type electronic character. The resulting anion exhibits ambident nucleophilic reactivity of the silicon and sulfur centers. Reactions with Fe2(CO)9 and organic azides demonstrate chemically accessible lone‐pair reactivity at silicon, whereas sulfur‐centered functionalization with chlorophosphine and chlorosilane electrophiles affords neutral acyclic silylenes. These findings establish a strategy for translating classical carbonyl umpolung concepts into low‐valent silicon chemistry and provide access to electronically cooperative main‐group frameworks featuring dual reactive sites.
nca7b93d9163a: Anode free lithium sulfur batteries (AFLSBs) can fully exploit the ultra−high energy density of Li−S systems. However, issues such as irreversible lithium loss caused by uneven solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on anode during the charging/discharging process, along with severe volume changes leading to structural instability, are key factors limiting their lifespan far below practical application. Herein, a sphere−sheet hetero−interlayer (2DLP−PASF) is designed, which adapts to volume changes and exhibits Li+ selectivity. The interlayer is fabricated by electrophoretic deposition of −SO3Li rich elastic ionomer emulsion (PASF) particles and laponite nanosheets (2DLP) onto a copper current collector. The elastic PASF particles support 2DLP to form a dispersed stress−buffering structure, which can accommodate volume changes during the charging/discharging process and suppress dendrite growth. Furthermore, rich −SO3Li in densely packed PASF shells between 2DLP repel anions electrostatically through the Donnan effect, which facilitates efficient Li+ transport and flux homogenization, thereby inhibiting the polysulfide shuttle. Additionally, −C≡N and −CF3 in PASF cores transform into a stable, Li3N/LiF−rich secondary SEI on anode, which in turn synergizes with the tough 2DLP−PASF to further stabilize lithium deposition. As a result, the AFLSB assembled with 2DLP−PASF modified copper current collector and Li2S cathode demonstrated significantly improved comprehensive electrochemical performance.
nc97df46ac947: Anode‐free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) remove the excess metal anode and increase projected cell‐level energy density, but they place reversibility on a transient negative‐electrode interface. In each cycle, Na is deposited on a foreign current collector and removed to a highly depleted state. Cell failure is governed by whether continuity can be preserved across a sequence of short‐lived interfacial states, including bulk coordination, interfacial desolvation, heterogeneous nucleation, metallic coalescence, Na isolation, and recurrent solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) renewal. AFSMBs are therefore better understood as dynamically reconstructed interfacial systems, where non‐uniformity introduced during interfacial entry can propagate through later plating and stripping. This review examines AFSMBs through three coupled stages: solvation‐controlled interfacial entry, current collector regulated Na reconstruction, and SEI renewal controlled by reaction–pathway selectivity and mechanical coherence. Current density, stripping depth, pressure, temperature, sodium inventory, and cell architecture are treated as boundary conditions that determine whether local interfacial gains persist under practical operation. By linking coordination chemistry, metallic continuity, interphase renewal, and device‐level constraints, this review provides a mechanistic framework for predictive AFSMB design.
ncfef82017e52: Iron parent imides serve as key intermediates for iron-promoted nitrogen fixation and ammonia oxidation. However, these active species are difficult to be isolated, and their reactivities are underexplored. So far, only a few multinuclear iron parent imides were reported, but none plays a key intersection during the bidirectional transformation. Herein, we adopt the bulky 1,2,4-tri(tert-butyl)cyclopentadienyl (Cp′) and bidentate 1,3-propanedithiolate (pdt) ligand to provide the steric protection for the reactive [Fe2S2] scaffold. As predicted, the highly active imido species can be captured by this [Fe2S2] platform to generate a novel thiolate-bridged diiron parent μ-imide complex 3. Mössbauer spectroscopy and DFT calculation reveal that 3 features a bent {FeIII−NH2−−FeIII} framework with two anti-ferromagnetic coupled, low-spin Fe(III) centers. Importantly, imide 3 can not only undergo protonation to generate amide and finally release ammonia, but also go through hydrogen atom transfer to regenerate nitride. This reactivity indicates that 3 is a key junction that associates the late stage (N3− → NH2− → NH2 − → NH3) of nitrogen fixation and the initial period (NH2 − → NH2− → N3−) of ammonia oxidation. Overall, this work provides one available strategy that can stabilize a high-activity imide and investigate its reactivity of bidirectional interconversion.
nab652182988c: Understanding charge transfer across donor‐acceptor interfaces is essential for designing high‐performance optoelectronic materials. Herein, we construct host‐guest metal‐organic framework (MOF) cocrystals employing a calcium‐based naphthalenediimide (NDI) host and electron‐rich aromatic guests to investigate photoinduced charge transfer at well‐defined crystalline donor‐acceptor interfaces. Challenging the conventional view that a high concentration of radical anions is typically associated with high photothermal conversion efficiency, our study uses electron paramagnetic resonance, surface photovoltage spectroscopy, and femtosecond transient absorption microscopy to show that a more extended conjugated plane in the guest accelerates charge recombination (charge‐transfer state lifetime: 201 vs. 348 ps). This leads to a MOF cocrystal with a photothermal conversion efficiency twice that of its counterpart, despite the latter exhibiting significantly higher NDI radical concentration. Moreover, this MOF cocrystal displays good aqueous stability and retains a photothermal conversion efficiency of 65.6% in aqueous media, enabling efficient near‐infrared light‐driven photothermal polymerization in both organic and aqueous phases. Notably, this photopolymerization proceeds even under natural sunlight irradiation and across biological tissue barriers. This work provides a novel design principle for donor‐acceptor materials, in which promoting charge recombination can be strategically exploited to develop high‐performance photothermal materials for solar energy utilization.
nd51d3b5660cb: In this work, we report the synthesis of highly active non-noble metal catalysts with controlled nanoparticle size and dispersion through a new catalyst preparation strategy combining the continuous-flow synthesis of...
n7b345d81f501: The results demonstrate that aqueous NH 3 can be thermocatalytically decomposed to H 2 and N 2 at these comparatively mild temperatures.
n8a4a4ea5188b: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) emerges as a versatile bio-based platform chemical, combining renewable accessibility, rich multifunctional reactivity, asymmetric synthesis potential, and routes to high-value chemicals and sustainable materials alike.
ne7d878d963e8: Icosahedral carboranes have extensive applications owing to their unique properties. This review summarizes advances in the mechanistic study of transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization.
n7b2d3ede544f: Vanadium-based thiophosphates in the MPQ3/M2P2Q6 family provide an unusual platform for coupling mixed-metal valence, metal vacancies, and 2D magnetism, but access to phase-pure multimetal solid solutions with verified chemical homogeneity remains limited. Here, we show that multication alloying provides a route to incorporating V into layered thiophosphates while retaining the mixed-valent, vacancy-containing character of V2−xP2S6. This approach yields Fe1.25V0.6P2S6, Ni1.25V0.6P2S6, Co1.25V0.6P2S6, and high-entropy V-containing compositions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (scXRD) and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping confirm formation of layered single-phase alloys and chemical uniformity both across the surface and through the flake thickness. Optical measurements show semiconducting band gaps spanning ∼1.33−1.66 eV, while temperature-dependent transport reveals markedly enhanced conductivity and low activation energies (∼0.2−0.3 eV) relative to conventional divalent TM2P2S6 analogs. Oxidation-state mapping indicates robust mixed-valent V2+/V3+ character consistent with defect-assisted hopping and self-doping linked to vanadium vacancies, likely causing enhanced conductivity. Magnetic measurements further show composition-dependent behavior, consistent with magnetic frustration and glassy components in Fe1.25V0.6P2S6 and (VMnFeCoNi)2P2S6, highlighting the role of multimetal disorder in shaping exchange interactions. Together, these results establish a route to phase-pure, conductive V-containing thiophosphate alloys and expand the tunable design space for coupled transport and magnetism in layered chalcophosphates.
n110c822b7b03: Two Zn(II)-based mixed-ligand metal−organic frameworks (MOFs) were synthesised using solvothermal methods and fully characterized (SCXRD, PXRD, TGA, DSC, FTIR, HSM). The MOFs are formulated as [Zn2(NDC)2(AzPy)2]n˙n(DMF)3 (ZNA150-DMF) and [Zn(NDC)(AzPy)0.5]n˙n(DMF)0.5 (ZNA90-DMF), where NDC2− = 2,6-naphthalene dicarboxylate, AzPy = 4,4′-azopyridine and DMF = N,N′-dimethylformamide, and are synthesized at 150 °C and 90 °C, respectively. Single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed that ZNA150-DMF and ZNA90-DMF are non-interpenetrated and triply interpenetrated, respectively. Both MOFs are highly flexible, displaying large changes in their unit cell parameters and void space features upon desolvation with the void space of both desolvated forms (ZNA150-act and ZNA90-act) consisting of isolated voids, thus leading to transient porosity, where these isolated pockets temporarily connect into channels to facilitate sorption. ZNA90-act carbon dioxide sorption isotherms have inflection points indicating a pressure-sustained structural change, as proven by variable-pressure single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction studies on ZNA90-act immersed in a CO2 gas environment. Variable-temperature single crystal X-ray diffraction studies on both activated MOFs, in the absence of gas, show that these are highly flexible, displaying colossal thermal expansion properties with changes in void space features. These changes tend towards what was observed for ZNA90-act under CO2 pressure, thus possibly linking flexible MOF behavior under the two sets of conditions.
na063f64bb8cf: Copper nanoparticles (Cu NPs) have a broad applicability, yet their synthesis is sensitive to subtle changes in reaction parameters. This sensitivity, combined with the time- and resource-intensive nature of experimental optimization, poses a major challenge in achieving reproducible and size-controlled synthesis. While machine learning (ML) shows promise in materials research, its application is often limited by scarcity of large high-quality experimental data sets. This study explores ML to predict the DLS-derived hydrodynamic diameter of Cu NPs from microwave-assisted polyol synthesis using a small data set of 25 in-house performed syntheses. Latin hypercube sampling is used to efficiently cover the parameter space while creating the experimental data set. Ensemble regression models successfully predict hydrodynamic diameters with good predictive performance given the limited data set. Since quantitative regression requires a unique DLS-derived hydrodynamic diameter, the regression model is restricted to monomodal DLS distributions, while a complementary classification model identifies synthesis conditions for which quantitative prediction is applicable. Using equivalent out-of-sample validation (OOB and LOOCV), the ML and DoE models showed comparable generalization (MAE = 40.92 and 40.46 nm, respectively). The final ensemble model achieved an R2 of 0.74, an MAE of 23.81 nm, compared to an R2 of 0.60, an MAE of 33.54 nm for the DoE model, while retaining the complete synthesis parameter space, making it better suited for synthesis guidance. Additionally, classification models using both random forests and large language models (LLMs) are evaluated to distinguish between large and small particles. These classification models exhibited only modest predictive performance, indicating that this small data set is insufficient to fully exploit the capabilities of complex LLMs. Overall, this study demonstrates that carefully curated small data sets, paired with robust classical ML, can effectively support the synthesis of Cu NPs and highlights that for lab-scale studies, complex models like LLMs may offer limited benefits. The validation experiments further indicate the potential of ML guided synthesis to improve the efficiency of experimental optimization and reduce resource consumption.
neb882bc2452f: Transition metal (TM) dissolution from the cathode and deposition on the anode in lithium−ion batteries is a key degradation mechanism, yet its spatial distribution in commercial cylindrical automotive-grade cells remains insufficiently understood. In this study on lithium−ion cells 18650 with a NMC811/graphite technology, we reveal a pronounced radial inhomogeneity in cathode metal deposition on the anode, with significantly higher accumulation in the inner windings of the jelly roll compared to the outer regions, identifying a critical vulnerability in the cell design while operating in overvoltage conditions. Spatially resolved near-edge edge X-ray absorption fine structure measurements further highlight this geometry dependence, revealing a higher fraction of Ni4+ in the inner windings, whereas the outer regions are dominated by Ni2+. This radial gradient correlates with intrinsic geometric characteristics of cylindrical cells, where the smaller bending radius in the inner windings may plausibly contribute to elevated mechanical stress, higher compressive pressure, and reduced heat dissipation in the cell core. The findings directly link cell geometry to both the extent and chemical state of TM deposition, proving its central role in degradation processes.

n57eeb16565c6: SnS 2 @NiS 2 /CNF was fabricated via interface engineering by simple electrospinning and sulfidation, achieving synergistically enhanced reversible capacity, initial coulombic efficiency, rate capability and long-cycle stability.
n62bbdb30b1d6: This study develops an NIR-responsive photocatalyst for pollutant degradation based on rare-earth nonlinear optical effects. The optimized CN–Yb–Tm system achieved a tetracycline degradation efficiency approaching 100% under NIR light.

nb15812125e75: Cells generate pico-to-nanonewton forces through metabolic circuits and diffusion for downstream processes, including stress fiber assembly and cellular growth. The inherent complexities of the system’s processing, reactivity, and adaptability make it difficult to recapitulate in a synthetic setting. Herein, we compartmentalized the urease-urea feedback-controlled reaction network (FCRN), demonstrating global vs local function adaptability by coupling with peptide self-assembly. Compartmentalized FCRN (c-FCRN) facilitates chemical energy-to-mechanical energy conversion, creating forces on the piconewton scale, allowing nanofiber alignment, akin to what a cell does.
