The rational integration of dual-active sites induces oriented charge flow, significantly enhancing photogenerated carrier separation and utilization, as evidenced by ultrafast spectroscopy showing extended electron lifetimes. This synergistic architecture delivers markedly higher production rates of 1.2 mmol g–1 h–1 for CO and 2.5 mmol g–1 h–1 for benzaldehyde, representing approximately 8-fold and 5-fold enhancements over pristine CdS, respectively. Comprehensive in situ spectroscopic studies combined with density functional theory calculations elucidate the distinct roles: Au sites strengthen CO2 adsorption and stabilize intermediates for reduction, while Ag2S promotes alcohol dehydrogenation. This synergistic dual-site architecture maximizes redox efficiency by matching reaction potentials and minimizing carrier recombination. This work provides mechanistic insights into catalyst design for integrated CO2 valorization and biomass upgrading, providing a basis for efficient chemical production.
n334c79cb8698: The selective oxyfunctionalization of C(sp3)–H bonds remains a central challenge in chemical synthesis. Although oxygenases and peroxygenases provide biocatalytic alternatives to metal-based chemical methods, their practical use is constrained by costly cofactor regeneration, toxic co-substrates, or limited selectivity. Molybdenum (Mo)-dependent alkyl dehydrogenases circumvent these limitations by employing water, rather than O2 or H2O2, as the oxygen source for hydroxylation in conjunction with an electron acceptor. Here, we combine enzymatic, structural, and computational analyses to characterize a Mo-dependent p-cymene dehydrogenase (pCDH) from an anaerobic hydrocarbon-degrading bacterium. Isolated pCDH selectively hydroxylates a variety of benzylic and allylic C(sp3)–H bonds. A 2.0 Å cryo-EM structure of the heterotrimeric enzyme in complex with p-cymene captures key states of the catalytic cycle. Structure-guided QM/MM modelling and docking rationalize the substrate scope and radical mechanism. These results identify water-dependent Mo-dehydrogenases as promising catalysts for selective C(sp3)–H oxyfunctionalization.
n80df4c9d9ab6: Efficient H2 dissociation and subsequent spillover of active hydrogen species are critical factors for achieving high activity in CO2 hydrogenation reactions. Herein, we constructed a well-designed and highly dispersed Cu–In bimetallic catalyst supported on CeO2. This catalyst enables the spatial separation of plasmonic enhancement, H2 activation, and CO2 conversion sites, thereby significantly improving H2 dissociation capability and H-spillover efficiency. Comprehensive investigations using multiple transient characterizations, together with in situ/operando spectroscopy, reveal that the three components are tightly coupled through H-spillover, electron transfer, and interfacial interactions. Specifically, the Ce sites on the CeO2 surface serve as the active centers for CO2 conversion via a redox mechanism, while the available indirect but consistent evidence suggests that In species likely act as the primary H2 dissociation sites, promoting the reduction of Cu species and the regeneration of oxygen vacancies on the CeO2 surface through H-spillover. Meanwhile, the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect of Cu significantly enhances the light absorption and photothermal conversion efficiency of the catalyst. The photoexcited LSPR electrons generated by Cu are further transferred to the In species and CeO2 surface, thereby facilitating H2 dissociation and the redox cycling of Ce sites. Such a “functional separation–synergistic enhancement” strategy effectively improves the catalytic activity, and the optimal catalyst achieves a CO yield of 230.1 mmol gcat–1 h–1 W–1 cm2 under 1.5 W cm–2 light irradiation at the surface temperature of 300 °C, significantly outperforming both the corresponding dark reaction and the monometallic Cu/CeO2 and In/CeO2 counterparts. This work provides important design principles and mechanistic insights for constructing highly active CO2 hydrogenation catalytic systems by enhancing H2 dissociation and H-spillover processes.
nb868a2c8a215: LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.
n615084cc7254: Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.
n472b3f592c93: Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.
n352917b010cd: Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.
n001f71cde773: The efficacy of peptide-based tumor vaccines is often constrained by the size-exclusion barrier of the subcapsular sinus (SCS), which restricts infiltration of macromolecules into the lymph node (LN) parenchyma essential for T-cell priming. Here, inspired by the clinical contrast agent Sonazoid, we developed an ultrasound-assisted vaccine platform with tunable phase-transition behavior for the active modulation of the LN microenvironment. The system integrates phosphoserine-decorated lipid chemistry to promote cell-mediated LN trafficking, a covalently conjugated adjuvant–antigen construct for synchronized immunostimulation, and liquid-state perfluorocarbon nanodomains programmed for ultrasound-triggered liquid–gas transition. Upon localized ultrasound irradiation, the chemically programmed phase transition triggers cargo release, while the resultant acoustic cavitation generates transient openings in the SCS endothelium. This process enables deep parenchymal infiltration of vaccine components that would otherwise be excluded. Beyond the physical barrier disruption, RNA sequencing reveals that acoustic stimulation drives both structural and immunological reprogramming of LN into an immune-permissive niche. By synergizing mechanical stimulation with biological modulation, this strategy induces benign and persistent LN expansion, amplifies antitumor T-cell responses, and establishes durable immunological memory, resulting in both prophylactic and therapeutic outcomes. This approach is versatile across both model antigens and neoantigens, offering a bioinspired, two-stage LN-targeted delivery strategy that serves as a framework for designing more effective therapeutic vaccines.
n04986efcd5d2: In stark contrast with traditional refraction phenomenon in isotropic media, refraction of hyperbolic polaritons enables extreme confinement and nanofocusing of mid-infrared light. However, the tuning of hyperbolic refraction typically relies on plasmonic systems (e.g., gating graphene and phase-change materials), and therefore, the electron–electron scattering introduces inevitable propagation losses of polaritons. Herein, we demonstrate that refraction of highly confined hyperbolic polaritons in α-phase molybdenum trioxide (α-MoO3) crystal strongly depends on the dielectric superstrate. We theoretically and experimentally indicate that both the wavevector (its direction and magnitude) and the propagation direction of refracted hyperbolic polaritons can be controlled by varying the twist angle between the vdW dielectric layers of tungsten diselenide (WSe2) and α-MoO3 crystals. Moreover, we observe the total internal reflection and zero-phase propagation of nanoscale-confined polaritons in hyperbolic media. Our study of the propagation of hyperbolic polaritons not only deepens the understanding of polariton refraction at the nanoscale and in strongly anisotropic media but also promises the development of functional nanophotonic elements and devices.
nf084b8590f19: Silicon-based solid-state batteries (Si-SSBs) offer enhanced safety and higher energy density over conventional liquid-electrolyte systems, yet their practical realization is critically hindered by severe volume expansion of silicon anodes and poor interfacial compatibility with solid-state electrolytes. This review provides a comprehensive evaluation of recent advances from a coupled design perspective, integrating silicon anode engineering, electrolyte compatibility optimization, and interfacial stabilization. We systematically examine emerging strategies for silicon anodes alongside compatibility approaches tailored to each electrolyte type, with a particular focus on the coupled chemo-mechanical degradation at the silicon/electrolyte interface. A systematic compatibility mapping linking different Si architectures with specific electrolyte families reveals the most promising material combinations and their underlying design principles. Beyond materials design, we address critical manufacturing challenges including stack pressure management, scalable processing, and prelithiation techniques essential for industrial translation. Finally, we propose a forward-looking roadmap integrating multiscale characterization, AI-assisted design, and scalable fabrication, providing both theoretical guidance and practical strategies for developing high-performance, commercially viable Si-SSBs.
n20c2405e443b: Dynamic DNA nanomachines are programmable devices capable of executing certain controlled movements, structural reconfigurations, and functional tasks. Over the past few decades, extensive advancements have been made in designing DNA-based molecular systems driven by strand displacement, catalytic reactions, enzymatic processes, chemical or physical stimuli. The development of DNA nanotechnology has further enabled the construction of highly precise and complex DNA nanomachines. Herein, we review dynamic DNA nanomachines from a motion-to-function perspective, emphasizing how programmable movement, structural reconfiguration, or autonomous operation can be converted into biomedical output. Structural platforms, driving mechanisms, biomedical functions, and translational barriers are discussed. Particularly, we focus on the systems in which DNA dynamics directly contribute to biosensing, bioimaging, therapeutic activation, cell regulation, and molecular decision-making. This framework distinguishes dynamic DNA nanomachines from static DNA nanostructures, which also highlights the design requirements needed to move these systems toward practical biomedical applications.
n9345afcbbafa: Conductive hydrogel electrodes are vital components for achieving human-machine interfaces. However, the inherent trade-off between high conductivity and favorable mechanical/adhesive properties remains a significant challenge for hydrogel-based epidermal electrodes. Here, we developed a multifunctional MXene/WPU/PAA (MWA) hydrogel electrode that combines robust mechanical properties, strong adhesion, and excellent conductivity. The introduced MXene nanosheets can induce free-radical polymerization, resulting in fast gelation (<5 min) at room temperature. Theoretical analyses reveal that MXene nanosheets form abundant hydrogen bonds with polymer chains, thus enhancing the cross-linking density and mechanical strength of the hydrogel electrode. The MWA hydrogel can form a stable skin-electrode interface, enabling high-fidelity multimodal physiological signal monitoring. Specifically, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for sEMG reached 36.0 dB, while the SNR for ECG was 30.1 dB, outperforming the Ag/AgCl electrodes. The MWA hydrogel exhibits outstanding adhesion under repeated cycles and simulated sweat conditions, reaching 94.2 and 55.5 kPa, respectively. Furthermore, the MWA hydrogel electrode demonstrates precise scalp EEG monitoring, enabling wireless drone flight control via real-time brainwave decoding. This work provides insight into MXene-polymer interactions and demonstrates the applicability of the developed electrode to brain-computer interface applications.
n231920bd57fc: Atomically thin materials can strongly confine light into quanta of lattice vibrations, leading to strong light–matter interactions. Some of these materials can exhibit topology, which protects the edge states embedded inside the bulk from backscattering, while some host magnetism, providing another degree of freedom to control topological properties. The simultaneous observation of all of these phenomena in a single material can lead to various applications by enabling light-controlled topological electronic and nanophotonic devices. Here we demonstrate via first-principles density functional perturbation theory calculations that atomically thin MnBi2Te4 is a promising platform for hosting three highly confined, tunable, and long-propagating magnetophononic polaritons. These polaritons strongly modulate exchange interactions, especially the second polariton in 2 SL MnBi2Te4, inducing strong light–matter coupling in the presence of light. Intriguingly, this coupling not only induces an antiferromagnetic-to-ferromagnetic phase transition but also drives an electronic phase transition from trivial to topologically nontrivial states in 2 SL MnBi2Te4. We also show that these polaritonic modes have relatively weak electron–phonon scattering rates and that these scattering rates change with layer thickness and magnetic ordering due to spin–phonon coupling. Overall, our results suggest that MnBi2Te4 is a promising material for topological electronics, nanophotonics, and nanophonics capable of providing greater control of data signals via light.
nd55a381048d4: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are versatile precursors for nanostructured, heteroatom-doped carbons. However, understanding the spatiotemporally resolved mechanisms that govern crystalline-to-amorphous framework collapse, diffusion-mediated reorganization of transient intermediates, and the subsequent formation of graphitic carbon remains challenging. Here, we elucidate the transformation of the 2D leaf-shaped zeolitic imidazolate framework ZIF-L into Zn-dispersed N-doped carbon using a combination of in situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). These measurements directly capture the sequential collapse of the layered MOF framework and the associated morphological evolution under controlled heating, decoupled from beam-induced effects during electron microscopy. Complementary ex-situ pyrolysis (700–1100 °C), together with high-resolution TEM, synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (X-PDF) analysis, and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), reveals the diffusion of Zn-containing species, ligand decomposition, and progressive graphitization within the amorphous matrix. We identify temperature-dependent stages involving ligand breakdown, migration of Zn–Nx species, followed by Zn loss, and ultimately forming porous N-doped carbon at 1000 °C that exhibits the strongest electrochemical response within this series. These findings establish temperature-dependent structure–property relationships that enable the thermal engineering of MOF-derived ORR catalysts.
n900c122acae3: Acute lung injury (ALI) is characterized by an uncontrolled cycle of inflammation and oxidative stress. However, conventional therapeutics are limited by physiological pulmonary barriers and poor targeted bioavailability. In this study, an inhalable multifunctional liposomal system (designated as R&I/Lip@PEG-M) was elaborately engineered to codeliver Resveratrol and IMD-0354 to disrupt the inflammation-oxidative stress cycle for ALI therapy. Upon nebulized inhalation, the negatively charged R&I/Lip@PEG-M liposomes would efficiently penetrate the mucus barrier, extensively accumulate in the pulmonary alveoli, and be specifically taken up by alveolar macrophages via mannose-mediated targeting recognition. Particularly, the internalized liposomes could exert combined therapeutic effects by scavenging intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and blocking the NF-κB signaling pathway to inhibit inflammation. In the LPS-induced ALI mouse model, the designed R&I/Lip@PEG-M significantly reduced the population of inflammatory macrophages, reprogrammed the redox microenvironment, and successfully mitigated lung damage and pulmonary edema.
n18e48ff0f97f: Two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offer tunable interlayer spacing and accessible surfaces that can overcome key limitations of conventional sodium-ion battery (SIBs) anodes. Here, we investigate Na+ storage mechanisms in three-layer 2D heterostructures composed of horizontally stacked graphene (G), nitrogen-doped graphene (NG), and MoS2 (M) by combining cyclic voltammetry with operando spectroelectrochemical Raman spectroscopy. Restricting the active thickness to three atomic layers enables direct spectroscopic access to interfacial charge transfer and strain during cycling. Electrochemical analysis reveals that Na+ storage is governed by two coupled factors: the permeability of the electrolyte-facing outer layer, and the electronic–mechanical interactions within the interlayer space. NG outer layers facilitate ion access and deliver up to 40-fold higher capacities than pristine graphene stacks, whereas MoS2 top layers suppress ion infiltration. Operando Raman correlates faradaic features with reversible structural changes, allowing separation of charge-doping and strain effects during cycling. The results demonstrate that Na+ storage proceeds predominantly via reversible accumulation in confined interlayer and blister-like reservoirs formed during solvent cointercalation. Incorporating MoS2 as a middle layer redistributes charge and buffers mechanical strain, enhancing cycling stability. These findings provide insights into charge storage mechanisms in 2D materials.
n344f6e871368: Optogenetics enables highly specific regulation of neuronal activity with exceptional spatiotemporal precision, providing powerful tools for neural circuit interrogation and the treatment of neurological disorders. However, the limited tissue penetration of visible light restricts its application to deep neural tissues. Near-infrared (NIR) neuromodulation has emerged as a promising alternative by leveraging the superior tissue penetration and minimal invasiveness of NIR light. Recent advances in NIR-responsive nanomaterials, optical engineering, and neurotechnology have rapidly transformed the field from nonspecific photobiomodulation to cell-specific nanotransducer-mediated neuromodulation and integrated neuromodulation systems. In this review, we summarize the optical principles governing NIR propagation in biological tissues and the mechanisms underlying NIR-mediated neural stimulation. We then discuss recent advances in representative NIR nanotransducers, including photothermal, optoelectric, photoacoustic, and NIR-to-visible upconversion platforms together with integrated neuromodulation systems that combine NIR stimulation with multimodal neural recording and closed-loop feedback. We further highlight emerging applications in the central nervous system, optic nerve, and peripheral nerve disorders. Finally, we discuss the key challenges toward clinical translation, including improving tissue penetration, cell specificity, biosafety, and translation, developing intelligent multidisciplinary neuromodulation platforms, and integrating artificial intelligence with closed-loop neural interfaces to achieve adaptive, precise, and personalized neuromodulation.
n81f9458e755a: Lanthanide-doped luminescent nanocrystals (NCs) hold significant promise for bioimaging, theranostics, catalysis, sensing, lighting, and displays, motivating an in-depth understanding of their optical properties. This work reveals the profound, yet widely disregarded, impact of surface structure changes on the luminescence of growing NCs through a model study of Eu3+ surface-exchanged Sr2YF7 NCs. Contrary to expectation, a stark drop in luminescence intensity exceeding several orders of magnitude was observed as the particle size increased. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy imaging shows that the NCs evolve from spheroidal to cuboidal morphologies during growth, with a shift in preferentially exposed crystal facets from {111} to {200} that renders lattice distortion less favorable. High-resolution optical spectroscopy probing surface Eu3+, together with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and reaction kinetics study, reveals a high extent of Eu3+ exchange in the small spheroidal NCs with lattice distortion extending far from the surface into the interior. This starkly contrasts the situation in the large cuboidal NCs, where the extent of Eu3+ residing in the surface region is severely limited, thereby causing the dramatic drop in luminescence. These findings demonstrate surface structure control as a powerful strategy for tailoring the luminescence properties of Ln3+-doped NCs and other nanomaterials for advanced applications.
nfbc81d758378: Intertwined electronic orders in low-dimensional quantum materials often evolve in a strongly thickness-dependent manner, yet direct spectroscopic access to their mutual evolution remains a key challenge. NbSe2 is a prototypical layered superconductor in which charge-density-wave order coexists with superconductivity, but spectroscopic signatures of the charge-density-wave state are frequently obscured, limiting direct comparison with superconducting order. Here, we demonstrate all-van der Waals planar tunnel junctions as a spectroscopic platform for simultaneously probing charge-density-wave and superconducting states in NbSe2 from the bulk to the bilayer limit. Temperature-dependent tunneling spectra reveal distinct anomalies associated with charge-density-wave formation and superconducting gap opening, allowing both quantum phase transitions to be tracked within the same device architecture. We find that the charge-density-wave transition temperature increases from ∼34 to ∼56 K as the NbSe2 thickness is reduced from 11L to the bilayer, while the superconducting transition temperature decreases from ∼7.2 to ∼5.4 K. These results reveal a clear anticorrelation between the two ordered states as dimensionality is reduced. Moreover, our spectroscopic studies reveal that the emergence of charge-density-wave order modifies the electronic states of NbSe2 over a broad energy window extending up to ±300 meV, a widely anticipated but previously experimentally inaccessible characteristic. Our results provide comprehensive spectroscopic evidence for the thickness-dependent competition between charge-density-wave order and superconductivity in ultrathin NbSe2 and position planar van der Waals tunnel junctions as a powerful platform for investigating emergent quantum phases in layered materials.
n035457817aae: Staphylococcus epidermidis is the leading cause of medical-implant-related infections. This pathogen attaches to medical implants coated in host fibrinogen via adhesin proteins. To resist high shear forces, adhesin-ligand rupture forces can exceed 2000 pN, a force that is much higher than streptavidin–biotin (150–300 pN). Yet, these adhesin-ligand complexes have a quite moderate KD (∼380 nM). This nanomechanics is explained, in part, by catch-bond behavior where adhesin-ligand lifetimes increase with force. Notably, prior reports of adhesin catch-bond mechanics at both low (3–30 pN) and high (1100–1400 pN) forces have lifetimes that are difficult to reconcile. Here, we combined constant-velocity and constant-force assays and thereby showed slip-bond behavior over six decades of lifetimes first for SdrG:Fgβ (1000–2400 pN) and then for SdrE:CFH (800–2200 pN) from Staphylococcus aureus. Individual lifetimes for SdrE:CFH exceeded 15 min at 800 pN. To investigate the thermodynamics of SdrG:Fgβ stability, we measured its lifetime using the constant-force assay as a function of both force (1000–1800 pN) and temperature (10–37 °C). Analysis yielded the enthalpic-dissociation barrier (ΔH‡ = 40 ± 4 kBT) and, assuming an enthalpy-dominated barrier, the dissociation attempt frequency (∼6 × 1010 s–1). Our results unambiguously demonstrate high-force slip-bond behavior for two different adhesin-ligand pairs and provide biophysical parameters governing the stability of key virulence factors.
ne01172f5198e: MRSA mastitis is clinically refractory and characterized by progressive inflammation driven by intracellular bacteria that form persistent niches in mammary epithelial cells and macrophages to evade antimicrobial clearance. Conventional antibiotics, particularly β-lactams, are widely used but suffer from poor intracellular accumulation, failing to reach these reservoirs. Even nanocarrier-based strategies struggle to achieve efficient endosomal escape and precise intracellular targeting. Herein, we report a fibronectin-functionalized, fluorinated PLGA nanoparticle encapsulating amoxicillin and sulbactam (Fn-F-PLGA@A/S) engineered with a 2.5% (w/w) fluorinated core for efficient endosomal escape. The fibronectin decoration enables sequential targeting of both host integrins and bacterial fibronectin-binding proteins (FnBPs). Fn-F-PLGA@A/S achieved efficient intracellular delivery, clearing 90% of intracellular MRSA in macrophages and epithelial cells within 4 h in vitro. To prolong mammary retention, Fn-F-PLGA@A/S was loaded into a thermosensitive hydrogel. In a murine MRSA mastitis model, a single intramammary dose of the gel formulation achieved >90% bacterial reduction, attenuated TNF-α and IL-6, and preserved alveolar architecture and tight junctions. Proteomic analysis revealed upregulation of AMPK-mediated autophagy, suggesting that beyond direct antibiotic action, the potent intracellular clearance achieved by Fn-F-PLGA may involve the engagement of host autophagic machinery, potentially facilitating the sequestration of MRSA within degradative compartments. Collectively, by integrating sequential targeting, sustained local retention, and autophagic engagement, this platform provides a robust strategy to address the key limitations of conventional antibiotics against intracellular pathogens in refractory infections.
ne1702d896a41: Lithium‐carbon dioxide (Li–CO2) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high‐energy storage with CO2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two‐electron conversion toward Li2C2O4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual‐atom Fe–N–Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N‐doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe1‐Mo1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe1‐Mo1/ICPs) to promote a reversible two‐electron Li2C2O4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N‐doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter‐site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe–N–Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor‐acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li2C2O4. Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li2C2O4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual‐atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.
n3855271dde3e: For wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskites, quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) surface reconstruction using bulky-cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium-based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low-dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N-methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge-neutralized ammonium–sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden–Popper-like quasi-2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap-mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide-ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO-treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO-treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS-L-1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge-neutralized organic spacer for quasi-2D surface reconstruction in wide-bandgap mixed-halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.
n8bc1da4da222: Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self‐assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene‐block‐poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time‐resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport‐mechanical‐morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self‐assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.
n626efefab170: NMR chemical shifts are plainly transformed into machine learning features that have rational and intuitive chemical meaning. A small number of these features are used to predict molecular reactivity (via the HOMO-LUMO energy gap), resulting in a model that is not reliant on a priori knowledge of chemical structure or charge.
n6e245f30a071: This review discusses transferrable lessons and parameters from solution-based COF syntheses and small molecule mechanochemistry for the mechanochemical syntheses of imine and imine-derived COFs.
n81ff3f33c787: The development of ferroelectric materials relies on cation engineering of pure oxide systems. However, the discovery of new polar frameworks in pure oxides has become increasingly difficult because of their chemical and structural limitations. We report an approach to realize ferroelectricity in the n = 1 Ruddlesden−Popper (RP) family (A2BX4), a structure that is typically nonpolar in the oxide form because of its high crystalline symmetry. To stabilize the polar order in this rigid framework, we utilized anion engineering, specifically the partial substitution of O2− with F−. Although traditional topochemical fluorination requires a stable crystalline parent oxide, the parent n = 1 oxide Pb2MO4 (M = Fe, Co, Ni) is thermodynamically unstable and cannot be synthesized as a crystalline template. A low-temperature fluorination method using amorphous oxide film precursors was used to overcome this challenge. c-Axis-oriented epitaxial thin films of metastable Pb2M(O,F)4 were obtained, because a stable parent crystal was not required. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and electrical measurements (P−E) hysteresis and positive-up-negative-down (PUND) measurements confirmed that these layered oxyfluorides exhibited clear and switchable ferroelectricity. This behavior probably originates from the strong O/F anisotropy, which forces significant off-center cation displacements within the single perovskite layers. Thus, amorphous-based low-temperature fluorination provides a universal route for exploring novel functional materials across various mixed-anion systems.
n4d11072d1704: Lithium-conducting fluoride garnets exhibit ionic conductivities of ∼10–10 S cm–1, far below those of their oxide counterparts. Here, we investigate the origin of this poor transport in Na3Ga2Li3F12 and Na3Al2Li3F12 through a combination of structural characterization and first-principles calculations. Both compounds are highly ordered, with no significant antisite disorder, and exhibit intrinsic ionic conductivities of ∼2 × 10–11 S cm–1 at 100 °C. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal low Li-ion migration barriers (0.16 to 0.29 eV), indicating that the fluoride garnet framework does not inherently restrict Li-ion diffusion. However, the formation energies for lithium Frenkel and Schottky defect pairs are high (1.9 to 2.4 eV), indicating that the intrinsic concentrations of mobile Li-ion defects are negligibly small. These results establish that the low conductivity of stoichiometric fluoride garnets arises from high defect-formation energies, rather than high migration barriers.
nafc6148501c9: Reversible-deactivation radical photopolymerization (photoRDRP) enables precise spatiotemporal control of polymer architectures. Because of embedded active chain ends, photoRDRP offers straightforward reactivation and chain extension, providing unmatched flexibility for fine-tuning structural, mechanical, and physicochemical properties for targeted applications. Nevertheless, its application to 3D printing remains limited by the cost and synthetic effort of the control agent, as well as by a limited reactivity under common near-UV and blue light sources, which requires printers working in the visible range and results in usually low printing rates. Herein, we show the unexpected ability of 2-isopropylthioxanthone (ITX) to promote both a direct acrylate photopolymerization, (with no need for any conventional co-initiator and a printing rate close to those of conventional photoinitiators) and a subsequent surface-initiated (SI) photopolymerization via reactivable surface-bound species, yielding postfunctionalization results that are equivalent to, or surpass, those of RAFT systems. Compared to benzyldithiocarbamate (BDC) and N-(tert-butyl)-N-(2-methyl-1-(4-benzoylphenyl)propyl)-O-(1-phenylethyl) hydroxylamine (MBA), two model photoinitiators for photoRDRP in the near-UV range, ITX enabled controlled SI photopolymerization of neat acrylate monomers over thicknesses of several hundred micrometers, with higher molar reactivity and a broader spectral response. This allowed for direct photopolymerization and photostructuring using wavelengths from 365 to 405 nm. This straightforward and scalable approach opens promising avenues for the on-demand functionalization and assembly of complex 3D-printed architectures and is expected to bridge the gap between academic precision and industrial accessibility.
n2969b07b530f: The complex interactions between Zn2+ and water molecules in aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) lead to the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which is difficult to regulate. However, most reported studies either...
n74ccc94c1753: Conventional molecular strategies for stabilizing wide-bandgap perovskites rely on rigid additives that provide static chemical anchoring, yet their capacity to accommodate dynamic thermo-mechanical stress induced by thermal expansion mismatch remains...
nbc5b0d843282: Direct seawater electrolysis (DSE) enables in-situ hydrogen production using natural seawater without pretreatment, emerging as a key technology to overcome resource bottlenecks and support offshore low-carbon hydrogen economies. Nevertheless, seawater's...
n4c8470583766: The ORR and OER activity of α-K x MnO 2 simultaneously improve with increasing electrolyte pH. Electrochemistry, operando spectro-microscopy & grand-canonical DFT link this behavior to pH-dependent electrode charging and bulk cation (de)insertion.
n564b237ad3b0: Public battery datasets are growing rapidly, but fragmented hosting and inconsistent descriptions make them difficult to find, compare, and reuse. Battery Data Commons presently indexes 349 datasets in a living, searchable metadata registry, using human- and machine-readable descriptions linked to the original sources. This exposes experimental context without relocating raw data to give datasets wider visibility and a second life to legacy ones. Together, these capabilities provide infrastructure for reproducible battery science, engineering, and AI-enabled innovation.
nd0f1813bd0ea: AI-guided DIW and directional freezing create hierarchical LFP cathodes with low-tortuosity ion pathways. This design enables rapid Li + transport, yielding ∼10 mAh cm −2 at 71.16 mg cm −2 to overcome the thick-electrode energy–power trade-off.
n3c978d3b0d98: Closing battery-material loops requires recovery media that not only dissolve degraded cathodes but also direct dissolved metals into reusable material streams. Here, hydration-regulated coordination chemistry in a tetramethylammonium chloride-oxalic acid...
nd8233baf45ef: This editorial introduces the cross-journal themed collection Frontiers in materials discovery: innovations and challenges in machine learning and artificial intelligence, highlighting progress and open challenges in materials prediction, synthesis, and characterisation.
n98f1126b8042: Protein conformational dynamics govern how proteins assemble across distinct pathways. This review unifies native crystallization, amyloid fibrillization, and reduction-induced phase transitions, revealing how dynamic assembly routes can be harnessed to design adaptive, hierarchical protein materials with programmable functions.
nadecefe71ce0: Electrocatalytic nitrite reduction coupled with plasma nitrogen oxidation offers a promising route for ambient ammonia synthesis, yet simultaneously achieving high activity and stability remains challenging owing to high kinetic barriers and catalyst deactivation. Here, we develop a robust hybrid electrocatalyst for active and durable nitrite reduction to ammonia by leveraging Fe3C nanoparticles supported on nitrogen-doped carbon nanosheets (Fe3C/CN). As a benefit from strong interactions between Fe3C and CN, this hybrid catalyst delivers a high faradaic efficiency of 89.6% at −0.7 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode (vs RHE) and a record ammonia yield rate of 16 956.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.9 V vs RHE, along with no apparent performance decay over 1000 h of continuous electrolysis, underscoring its potential for sustainable electrochemical ammonia production. Mechanistic studies reveal that the synergistic effect between Fe3C nanoparticles and a nitrogen-doped carbon matrix enhances catalytic performance by optimizing reactant adsorption, water dissociation, and promoting reaction kinetics.
n6da192ecfdf0: The microscopic origin of supercurrent nonreciprocity in van der Waals Josephson junctions remains under debate, particularly regarding the role of twist-angle engineering. Here, we investigate twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 vertical Josephson junctions with controlled crystallographic alignment and clean interfaces. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy directly determines the twist angle and interface quality. While Josephson coupling exhibits a pronounced twist-angle dependence, the supercurrent diode efficiency remains small and shows no systematic angular dependence. In contrast, enhanced diode responses emerge in weakly coupled junctions with reduced transparency and interfacial disorder. Deliberate interface degradation further enhances the diode efficiency to nearly 30% and produces irregular magnetic-field dependence. These results demonstrate a clear decoupling between Josephson coupling and supercurrent nonreciprocity, indicating that interfacial disorder rather than twist-angle-controlled momentum matching plays a dominant role in the observed diode response. Our findings establish an important benchmark for understanding nonreciprocal superconducting transport in van der Waals Josephson devices in the future.
n3a568ea8be74: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) hold great promise for next-generation high-energy-density energy storage systems, but suffer from uneven Li nucleation and unstable interfaces. Here, a scalable coplacement gas-phase reaction strategy is developed to construct an adaptive alloy–fluoride interface on nickel mesh current collectors, enabling one-step in-situ formation of a uniform Ni3Sb/NiF2 layer. The lithiophilic Ni3Sb alloy effectively lowers the lithium nucleation barrier and guides uniform lithium deposition. Upon cycling, NiF2 is transformed into a LiF-rich interphase, which stabilizes the electrode/electrolyte interface and homogenizes Li+ flux. The combined interface enables durable and uniform Li plating/stripping under long-term cycling. Consequently, the Ni3Sb/NiF2-modified anode achieves stable cycling for over 2600 h in symmetric cells and delivers 83.1% capacity retention after 240 cycles in LiFePO4 full cells with a high areal capacity of 10 mAh cm–2. This work provides a facile and scalable strategy for engineering multifunctional interfaces toward practical LMBs.
nbb73d85d18cb: Quantum magnets with competing interactions often emerge from delicate balances among microscopic parameters, making it essential to disentangle the intrinsic spin dynamics from extrinsic disorder effects. Here we introduce a multimodal optical approach combining infrared and domain-resolved micro-Raman spectroscopies at high magnetic fields to reconstruct the intrinsic magnetic excitation spectrum of twinned crystals of the Kitaev–Heisenberg antiferromagnet Na3Co2SbO6. Far-infrared spectroscopy reveals multiple field-tunable magnetic excitations, but the intrinsic response is obscured by replica features arising from twin domains. By correlating magneto-infrared and domain-resolved Raman spectra, we isolate the single-domain magnon response and uncover a pronounced 2-fold in-plane magnon anisotropy. This anisotropy far exceeds that expected from the measured in-plane g factor anisotropy and is instead dominated by anisotropic bond-dependent exchange interactions. By unifying high-field, high-resolution, and spatially selective optical probes, our work establishes a broadly applicable framework for revealing intrinsic spin dynamics and constraining the spin Hamiltonian in multidomain quantum magnets.
nd32b1b713fca: Protein nanopores are valuable platforms for single-molecule sensing; however, expanding the range of structurally defined nanopores remains challenging. We describe a minimal, structure-guided redesign strategy that converts BtuB, a TonB-dependent vitamin B12 transporter, into a functional β-barrel nanopore. Using protein structure prediction and molecular dynamics, we eliminated the internal plug domain, selected extracellular loops, and preserved the 22-stranded β-barrel scaffold. BtuBΔ1–136_Δloops formed single channels in planar lipid bilayers, exhibiting an approximately linear current–voltage relationship and a single-channel conductance of ∼1.2 nS. Polymer exclusion analysis revealed an apparent PEG-accessible diameter of approximately 4 nm, indicating a highly accessible pore entrance. Noise analysis showed that extracellular loop architecture influences the stability of ion transport. These findings highlight the distinction between geometric pore accessibility and functional ion-conducting pathways in redesigned β-barrel nanopores, suggesting that TonB-dependent transporters may serve as useful scaffolds for β-barrel nanopore engineering.
nee6fc826001e: Radiotherapy efficacy is limited by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Current immunometabolic strategies using nonselective inhibitors or exogenous stimulus-activated nanomedicines suffer from off-target toxicity, insufficient antitumor responses, and procedural complexity. Herein, we developed PLG@OMVs-VP, an X-ray-activatable nanoadjuvant, to remodel the immunosuppressive TME and amplify the radiotherapy efficacy. PLG@OMVs-VP comprises outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) modified with verteporfin (VP) and an indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase inhibitor (NLG-919) via a PEGylated singlet oxygen (1O2)-cleavable linker. Upon X-ray radiation, VP absorbs X-rays and generates 1O2, which not only induces immunogenic tumor cell death via radiodynamic therapy but also triggers the selective release of NLG-919 for immunometabolic regulation. Moreover, the intrinsic lipopolysaccharide on OMVs activates pyroptosis, further enhancing the tumor immunogenicity. This strategy integrates pyroptosis-induced immunogenicity, radiodynamic therapy, and spatially controlled immunometabolic regulation, synergistically alleviating TME immunosuppression and eliciting antitumor immunity in both primary and distant tumors. This X-ray-activatable nanoplatform enables TME remodeling and an enhanced radiotherapy.
n5bd7d775a315: Paramagnetic molecules can serve as electron spin qubits for quantum information processing, provided that they preserve their spin coherence for a sufficient time to allow for computation and error correction. Here we report the rare isolation of stable Zr(III) aryloxide complexes, where Zr is an earth-abundant metal ion with a coherently manipulable electron spin. Density functional theory calculations reveal the trigonal planar d 1 geometry stabilizes a 4 d z 2 –5 s hybrid singly occupied molecular orbital with little ligand contribution and significant s character (25–27%), yielding large isotropic hyperfine coupling constants of 803–809 MHz. We observed long spin–lattice relaxation times ( T 1 ) up to 87 ms and dephasing times ( T m , T m CPMG ) up to 123 μs using isotope-selective pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. Nutation experiments further showed coherent manipulation of several electronic and electronuclear transitions. This study introduces Zr(III) aryloxides as competitive molecular qudits and expands the scope of metal ions to more earth-abundant metals.
nd5fe017b305b: The lack of standardized reporting and annotation of nucleic acid nanostructures limits reproducibility, interoperability and the efficient reuse of published designs. NanostarDB is a community-driven knowledgebase that standardizes nucleic acid nanostar designs through persistent identifiers, structural annotations, and integrated computational tools for design exploration, analysis and reuse, and is compliant with principles of findability, accessibility, interoprability and reusability (FAIR).
n594ee9b84f39: Margarida Costa Gomes, CNRS Research Professor at École Normale Supérieure de Lyon, talks to Nature Synthesis about understanding the molecular behaviour of porous liquids and the challenges of translating that understanding into functional materials.
n755546c87c55: Becky Greenaway, Associate Professor (Reader) and Royal Society University Research Fellow at Imperial College London, talks to Nature Synthesis about developing automated high-throughput experimentation to design porous liquids as well as persistent challenges in the field.
nd5e3ddd6d674: The design of metal–support interfaces is critical for overcoming the persistent trade-off between CO2 conversion and methanol selectivity in CO2 hydrogenation. Though an inverse catalyst with an oxide-on-metal configuration provides a platform for tuning interfacial properties, the distinct roles of multi-interfaces with different electronic properties and how they collectively govern reaction pathways remain largely unexplored. Herein, we constructed an inverse Ga2O3-ZnO/Cu catalyst to engineer dual pathways for efficient CO2-to-methanol conversion. Comprehensive characterization reveals that Ga2O3 induces charge redistribution in the catalyst for more oxygen vacancies, which enhance CO2 adsorption. The Cu-ZnO interface facilitates the formation of key intermediates along the formate pathway. Meanwhile, Ga also introduces a RWGS + CO* hydrogenation pathway to preferentially convert CO2 to methanol. In addition, Ga2O3 loading-enabled smaller Cu nanoparticles further enhanced H2 dissociation and spillover on the surface. Consequently, the optimized Ga2O3-ZnO/Cu catalyst achieves a high space time yield of methanol (728.73 gCH3OH kgcat–1 h–1) with a high methanol selectivity of 82.37% at 220 °C and 3 MPa. This work provides insights into engineering reaction pathways for methanol synthesis via the rational design of synergistic active sites.
n205bf2a0f460: Oxygen storage and release on oxygen storage materials such as CeO2–ZrO2 solid solution (CZ) are key phenomena for high-performance automotive three-way catalyst (TWC). In order to clarify the microscopic oxygen dynamics on TWC, oxygen storage distribution in a model catalyst comprising dense CZ substrate with Pd is visualized by combining oxygen isotope labeling and reaction quenching. The effects of temperature, oxygen storage duration, and hydrogen reduction (oxygen release) duration on 18O concentration distribution in the bulk and surface of the model catalysts are systematically investigated. In the temperature range of ≤400 °C, oxygen release and storage originated primarily from the Pd-CZ-gas triple phase boundary (TPB) and Pd surface, while the contribution from the bare CZ surface is limited. Oxygen incorporated from around the TPB diffuses in three directions: toward the CZ depth, CZ surface, and Pd surface. Furthermore, during the oxygen release process, the disappearance of the oxide layer (PdO) on the Pd and the subsequent exposure of metallic Pd accelerate oxygen release from the TPB, expanding the oxygen vacancy region deeper into the CZ directly beneath the Pd. Conversely, in the temperature range of ≥500 °C, in addition to the TPB-mediated process, the oxygen exchange on the entire CZ surface and bulk diffusion are activated, significantly expanding the storage and release regions. This study demonstrates that the OSC (oxygen storage capacity) mechanism in Pd/CZ catalyst is not static; rather, the dominant oxygen release/storage sites and transport pathways dynamically change depending on the temperature and the presence of a PdO layer.
nb4d62c55fe73: A gold-catalyzed dearomative cyclization of indoles with ynone-nitriles assisted by a Lewis or a Brønsted acid has been developed, which provides an efficient route to 4-azafluorenones via an unexpected indole ring-opening process. The key strategy involves the attack of an iminyl intermediate to the indoleninium species at its highly electrophilic C2 position, with both intermediates being generated spontaneously during the dearomatization process. By varying the gold catalyst and acid additives, the 1+1 and 2+1 component reactions can be achieved selectively.
n559bcbb12446: The local electric field generated at organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can profoundly influence electrocatalytic reactions, yet how molecular interfaces regulate local field distributions and reaction pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we combine grand-canonical density functional theory with in situ surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy to investigate CO2 reduction at cobalt phthalocyanine-copper (CoPc-Cu) interfaces. Density functional theory calculations show that CoPc creates a confined interfacial microenvironment and modifies the charge distribution at the Cu surface, producing non-uniform local electric fields that are experimentally probed using the vibrational Stark effect of adsorbed CO. Theory and experiment reveal that this field heterogeneity modifies CO adsorption across neighboring Cu sites and increases the adsorption-energy difference between adjacent CO intermediates, thereby lowering the barrier for C–C coupling. Consistent with this mechanism, CoPc-Cu exhibits an enhanced C2+/C1 product ratio, particularly at modest cathodic potentials where the confined hybrid interface is preserved. This work provides direct in situ evidence that organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can regulate electrocatalytic selectivity through local electric-field engineering, offering design principles for field-enhanced CO2 electroreduction.
na2ae666e2be8: Herein, we report a metal-free, cooperative oxidized graphitic carbon nitride/l-proline catalysis for enantioselective dearomative oxyalkylation of 2-arylindoles. The developed method leverages the band structure of g-C3N4 to efficiently generate singlet oxygen (1O2) under visible light and aerobic conditions, driving an oxidative dearomatization cascade. The resulting intermediates are intercepted via an l-proline-mediated Mannich addition, providing direct access to C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones in high yields (up to 88%) and with enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). By integrating heterogeneous carbon nitride photocatalysis with asymmetric organocatalysis, this protocol offers a robust, recyclable alternative to traditional noble-metal catalysis for enantioselective synthesis of C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones.
na4b680435232: Sulfur assimilation fuels bacterial growth by supplying the reduced sulfur required for the biosynthesis of sulfur-containing biomolecules. Adenosine 5′-phosphosulfate reductase (APSR) catalyzes the reductive step of this pathway, converting adenosine 5′-phosphosulfate (APS) to adenosine monophosphate. This reaction proceeds through nucleophilic attack by catalytic C256, located in the flexible C-terminal tail, on the sulfur atom of APS, forming a thiosulfonate enzyme intermediate. Here, we investigate this reaction in APSR from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, an opportunistic pathogen associated with severe infections, particularly in patients with cystic fibrosis. APSR contains an iron–sulfur [4Fe–4S] cluster, which participates in redox steps of the reaction. Here, we show that the redox state of the iron–sulfur cluster also controls the catalytic step. Multiscale molecular simulations investigate how oxidized and reduced cluster states affect APS binding, active site organization, and the nucleophilic attack step. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show that the oxidized [4Fe–4S]2+ cluster stabilizes substrate interactions and the conformation of the C-terminus, facilitating a catalytically productive orientation of C256. The activation barrier of 17.7 ± 1.7 kcal mol–1 from quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) umbrella sampling MD simulations at the B3LYP-D3(BJ)/6-31G(d) level is consistent with kinetics experiments performed on an ortholog enzyme. The redox state of the iron–sulfur cluster shows its role in modulating the conformation of conserved K144, which is important for transition state stabilization in the nucleophilic attack. These findings illuminate the mechanism of this P. aeruginosa target and provide broader insight into the roles of iron–sulfur clusters in controlling enzyme reactivity.
nf54c9c3a4e37: Sn–Pb perovskites are promising low-bandgap absorbers for photovoltaics, but their efficiency is limited by the low open-circuit voltage, VOC. The VOC deficit, WOC, is related to energetic disorder, characterized by the Urbach energy, EU, comprising static and dynamic contributions. For Cs0.25FA0.75SnxPb1–xI3, these contributions were determined using time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) and photoluminescence (PL) measurements between 180–350 K. For Pb-based films, both techniques provided similar EU values. However, for Sn-containing compositions (x = 0.2 and 0.5), TRMC-derived EU were twice higher than those found by PL. These differences arise from compositional heterogeneity: TRMC integrates absorption over the entire thickness while the PL-derived absorption originates from low-bandgap domains, likely from the Sn-rich top surface as revealed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The PL-derived EU trend corresponds to the bandgap-normalized WOC, which is smallest for x = 0.5 (∼9.2 meV), attributed to the low dynamic contribution originating from the lower mass of Sn.
n30b94de8dfc0: Catalyst layers are widely used to accelerate water dissociation in bipolar membranes (BPMs), yet their role in defining junction electrostatics and reversible reaction kinetics remains unclear. Here, we probe the electrochemical response of catalyst-containing BPM junctions using open-circuit voltage measurements, polarization analysis, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We show that catalyst nanoparticles influence both the recovery of the membrane potential and the voltage losses associated with water dissociation and formation at the catalyst layer. These changes reflect coupled effects of catalyst surface chemistry, junction electrostatics, and proton-transfer kinetics. Notably, catalysts that recover the membrane potential do not necessarily reduce overvoltage under applied bias, highlighting that membrane-potential recovery alone is insufficient to predict BPM performance. By combining improvements in membrane-potential recovery and reaction kinetics, catalyst–ionomer interface engineering reduces water-formation losses by up to 65% and increases peak power density for energy storage by more than an order of magnitude.
ncaa528f19de4: Organic electrodes for secondary batteries are hindered by molecular dissolution and low operating voltages. Herein, we report a coordination-driven strategy to construct insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules (BTD-M, M = Cu, Ni, or Zn) featuring high-voltage p-type triphenylamine-derived ligands (N4′,N4′-diphenyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-3,4,4′-triamine, BTD). By precisely tuning metal–ligand coordination, we thermodynamically lock discrete molecules against electrolyte dissolution while preserving unhindered access to active sites. The optimal BTD-Cu exhibits a narrow bandgap of 0.7 eV, enabling extensive electron delocalization for electronic conductivity. This electrode delivers a near-theoretical capacity of 134 mAh g–1 at 1C and still delivers 83 mAh g–1 at 10C. Leveraging bipolar redox chemistry of p-type ligands and metal centers, the symmetric all-organic dual-ion battery achieves an average voltage of 2.4 V and a cycle life exceeding 1000 cycles. This work establishes insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules as an accessible platform for organic battery design.
n7239f24e26b8: Sustainable Na-ion batteries (NIBs) have attracted widespread attention in transportation vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems due to abundant sodium sources, high safety records, and favorable all-climate performance. However, their overall performance and cost are largely governed by cathode materials, which determine practical application and commercial market prospects. Iron- and/or manganese-based polyanionic cathodes not only reduce cost but also provide high working voltage and desirable cycling stability, benefiting from strong inductive effects and robust structural covalency of polyanionic groups, making them attractive for sustainable batteries. This review summarizes material design concepts, research progress, technological bottlenecks, and development directions for various types of phosphate, pyrophosphate, and sulfate cathodes. Besides, we focus on clarifying the structure–function relationships by comprehensively comparing synthesis methods, crystal structures, electrochemical behavior, and reaction mechanisms of Fe/Mn-based polyanionic cathodes for NIBs. This review provides critical guidance for the future advancement of practical NIBs.
ncffc9d7d09d2: Hydroxide-induced degradation and swelling of organic anion exchange membranes (AEMs) fundamentally limit the advancement and industrialization of alkaline hydrogen production. Here, we present a free-standing inorganic AEM comprising 90 wt % layered double hydroxides within a three-dimensionally fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene scaffold. The membrane achieves zero swelling, suppressed hydrogen crossover, and a low area-specific resistance of 0.089 Ω cm2 while remaining stable for 1344 h in 1 M and 30 wt % KOH at 80 °C, under which commercial polymeric membranes fail rapidly. The confined hydrogen-bond network within layer double hydroxide galleries promotes Grotthuss-dominated OH– transport as supported by ab initio molecular dynamics. The membrane sustains 1 A cm–2 operation for 550 h in AEM water electrolyzers and 425 h in alkaline water electrolyzers, establishing a durable inorganic AEM platform for alkaline hydrogen production and related electrochemical energy technologies.
n8bef34ebf68d: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS− readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li+, constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H2O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm−2)/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF6‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.
n89e5b5bca6e5: Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N4. To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.
nffe48c158979: Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g−1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mgIr cm−2, it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm−2. Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.
ncf71a8efe79d: High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li+ transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li+ transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide‐enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb‐O‐Cl framework on LiNi0.83Co0.07Mn0.10O2 cathodes (denoted as C‐NCM). Derived from a mixed‐anion LiNbOCl4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb‐O‐Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb‐containing near‐surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li+ transport. Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li+ migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C‐NCM exhibits reduced sulfide‐derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface design from passive oxide‐barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed‐anion interfacial chemistry.
ne30e3fb6ac4e: Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi0.65Co0.05Mn0.30O2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO2. Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.

nc2b183cdb892: Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction reaction to high-value multicarbon products represents a highly promising strategy for achieving carbon neutrality goals. Among various electrocatalysts, copper-based materials occupy a central position due to their unique capability for *CO adsorption and dimerization; however, they still face severe challenges, including high overpotentials and limited product selectivity. Orbital engineering, particularly the construction of p-d bimetallic systems through the introduction of p-block metals, has emerged as a pivotal approach to surmounting the performance bottlenecks of Cu-based catalysts. This review systematically summarizes the recent research progress in copper-based p-d bimetallic catalysts designed via orbital engineering for efficient CO2 reduction reaction. We provide an in-depth discussion on the modulation mechanisms of p-block metals on the performance of Cu active centers from three key dimensions: electronic effects, geometric effects, and microenvironment regulation. Furthermore, we summarize the primary challenges currently facing the field of p-d orbital matching and offer perspectives on the rational design of future CO2 reduction catalytic systems that possess high activity, stability, and energy efficiency, aiming to provide theoretical guidance and practical insights for the large-scale application of green energy conversion technologies.
ne4de33ef25b8: Conventional elastomer networks can provide mechanical stability but offer limited capacity for network rearrangement and reprocessing. In this work, a sulfur-rich oligomeric crosslinker (S-VBGE) was introduced into epoxidized natural rubber (ENR) to construct a filler-free dual-dynamic network containing reversible hydrogen-bonding associations and sulfur-containing dynamic structures. The optimized ENR-SV15 formulation reached a tensile strength of 14.84 MPa and a toughness of 85.07 MJ·m−3. Based on three independent fatigue crack growth measurements, its apparent fatigue threshold was 310 ± 14 J·m−2, compared with 41 ± 1 J·m−2 for ENR-0. Temperature-dependent stress relaxation and reprocessing experiments indicate thermally activated network rearrangement, while variable-temperature FTIR supports the thermal responsiveness of the hydrogen-bonding associations. Together, these results show that balancing reversible associations, sulfur-containing dynamic structures, and network constraints can improve crack growth resistance while retaining solid-state reprocessability in dry ENR elastomers.
n7ce8d9e34583: Interfacial reactions at the electrolyte/Zn anode critically influence the reversibility and cycling stability of aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, we employ an in operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (E-QCMD) to investigate the dynamics of Zn deposition/dissolution in three representative ZnSO4, Zn(OTf)2, and Zn(ClO4)2 electrolytes at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 M. Using a three-electrode configuration under a constant overpotential of ± 100 mV, current density, mass change, and dissipation were simultaneously monitored in real time. A comparison between the measured mass change (ΔMf) and the theoretical Faradaic mass (ΔMq) reveals that both electrolyte anion identity and concentration strongly affect Zn redox behavior. Zn(ClO4)2 promotes the formation of rigid, highly reversible Zn deposits, although accompanied by hydrogen evolution, whereas concentrated Zn(OTf)2 forms viscoelastic interfacial layers, consistent with the accumulation of alkaline byproducts and the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). ZnSO4 exhibits intermediate behavior with improved reversibility at higher concentrations. Complementary analyses of Coulombic efficiency and mass-per-electron (MPE) further show that concentrated Zn(ClO4)2 and ZnSO4 electrolytes provide more reversible Zn deposition/dissolution than Zn(OTf)2. Ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations corroborate this picture by resolving the anion-dependent interphase chemistry and the underlying solvation and hydrogen-bond structures, respectively. These findings provide mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent Zn interfacial chemistry and demonstrate the capability of in operando E-QCMD for elucidating Zn redox processes in AZIBs.
n903958ec794a: The development of near-infrared (NIR) organic lasers has long been constrained by inefficient excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) and limited electronic delocalization, which restrict both performance and scalability. In this study, we demonstrate that subtle molecular modifications can improve laser properties. By introducing a π-bridge-enhanced donor-π-acceptor (D-π-A) architecture in the molecule MDS-DHAQ, we improve molecular planarity and extend π-conjugation. This strategic adjustment is associated with predominantly K*-type emission, consistent with an ESIPT-based four-level lasing scheme. Through self-assembly, MDS-DHAQ molecules spontaneously form well-ordered micro/nanocrystals that serve as the gain medium and resonant cavity for lasing. These self-assembled crystals exhibit single-mode lasing at 940 nm, with a low threshold of 3.8 μJ cm−2 and a linewidth of approximately 0.37 nm. Furthermore, they show a 10% reduction in lasing intensity after 10,000 pump pulses. This work highlights how molecular alterations can tune the physical properties of materials, offering an approach that integrates molecular engineering and self-assembly. The resulting NIR organic lasers have potential applications in integrated photonics and optoelectronics.
