nbacb4ba04329: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. Here, electron-donating ligands spatially separate the frontier orbitals of Au22 nanoclusters, extending hot-carrier lifetime to nanoseconds and enabling high-performance, stable photodetectors. This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.
n89e8ac68b1d8: Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.
nbb3af51a923a: This review focuses on recent advances of asymmetric hydrogenation in the strategic total synthesis of natural products and drug molecules, and outlines future perspectives for this field.
ne7b758fb2af0: This Tutorial Review establishes a unified framework connecting the fundamentals of solar vapor generation with materials and structural design, providing guiding principles for efficient, scalable, and sustainable water production.
n61f901993ff1: Dual-atom alloys (DAAs) embedded in metallic surfaces constitute an emerging catalytic platform fundamentally distinct from the widely studied carbon-supported dual-atom sites, as they enable intrinsic metal–metal cooperation within an active metallic environment. However, a systematic understanding of their structure–stability relationships remains elusive, mainly due to the prohibitive cost of exploring the vast space of compositions, crystal surfaces, and atomic configurations. Here, using Cu-based DAAs as a prototypical platform, we construct a library of 6804 candidate structures spanning nine crystal planes and two representative dual-atom configurations. Density functional theory (DFT)-calculated formation energies for 930 representative structures (13.7% of the library) are employed to train a physics-informed residual multilayer perceptron model combined with 5-fold ensemble learning. The model achieves high predictive accuracy with cross-validation R2 > 0.906 and demonstrates robust transferability across different crystal planes and structural motifs, outperforming conventional machine-learning baselines. Interpretable SHAP analysis indicates that electronic structure descriptors predominantly govern stability, with geometric compatibility contributing as a secondary factor. Systematic stability trends are identified, including a thermodynamic preference for diagonal configurations on the (100), (311), and (411) surfaces, linear-close configurations on the (110), (111), and (211) surfaces, and enhanced stability for noble-metal dopants, such as Au, Pt, and Pd. Electronic structure analysis further establishes a clear correlation between formation energy and the dopant d-band center, with greater stability achieved when the d-band center is located farther from the Fermi level. With the training on a limited number of DFT-calculated samples, this physics-aware and transferable machine-learning framework enables rapid and data-efficient prediction of dual-atom alloy stability. The approach is readily extensible to diverse crystal surfaces and alloy systems, providing a generalizable theoretical foundation for the thermodynamic screening and rational design of DAAs with high synthetic feasibility in energy catalysis.
n1e296c89bac2: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.
ne57c01b2a31f: A contact-electrification-induced dielectric polarization mechanism enables unidirectional charge transfer for stable, low-crest-factor direct-current generation, thereby supporting robust self-powered operation of a multi-sensor IoT system.
n03dd40dd7715: The unstable ITO-SAM interface limits organic solar cell efficiency and stability. We introduce a molecular locking strategy using a vacuum-deposited InClx interlayer that triggers ligand exchange to form a robust multidentate In–O–P coordination network. This enhances SAM anchoring and coverage, delivering 20.4% efficiency in small-area cells and 18.8% active-area efficiency in modules, while enhancing device stability. This approach provides a generalizable interfacial platform that overcomes the efficiency-stability-scalability trilemma, paving a new pathway for advancing organic photovoltaics and beyond.
n89ccf33f7b56: Singlet fission in tetracene generates triplet excitons that are harvested by a metal halide perovskite through a ZnPc-mediated interface with energetics consistent with an interfacial hybrid charge-transfer (IHCT) pathway, enabling triplet sensitization and their contribution to photocurrent generation in perovskite photovoltaic devices.
n227b519af3e2: A monolayer photonic crystal integrated with a transparent manganese halide gel scintillator enhances the extraction of X-ray-excited light while preserving high spatial resolution. By combining X-ray computed tomography with structured-light scanning, the system enables a unified, spatially registered three-dimensional visualization of internal structures and external geometry.
n7e91b73ebf65: Lanthanide-doped nanoparticles with near-infrared-II (NIR-II, 1000–1700 nm) emission hold great promise for deep-tissue bioimaging, yet their luminescence efficiency is often limited by conventional sensitization pathways. Herein, we go beyond this conventional paradigm by introducing a Ca2+-formed band structure modulation in the host lattice to dramatically boost the NIR-II emission of lanthanide-doped nanoparticles. Rational doping of Ca2+ ions restructures the energy levels, enabling the probe to efficiently capture excitation energy and channel it toward NIR-II-emitting lanthanide activators. This Ca2+-induced band structure modulation mechanism not only enhances the absorption cross section but also accelerates energy transfer to the NIR-II-emitting states. As a result, the designed nanoprobes exhibit excellent photostability and a high quantum yield. In vivo bioimaging demonstrates that the resulting nanoprobes enable deep-tissue visualization with an improved signal-to-background ratio. This work establishes a sensitization strategy that goes beyond conventional approaches, positioning lanthanide-based NIR-II probes as promising candidates for advanced biological imaging.
ne7b79c7b67eb: Free-electron-based nanoscopy enables the study of optical excitations in materials with deep-subwavelength spatial resolution, with cathodoluminescence (CL) being one of the most useful signals. When combined with an optical collection system, CL measurements can access multidimensional information on light; yet the phase of the emitted optical fields has remained largely elusive. Here, we demonstrate a reference-free phase retrieval approach for far-field CL wavefronts using the Gerchberg–Saxton algorithm implemented with real-space and angular-space CL intensity data. Applying this approach to representative nanostructures, including a planar surface, nanosphere, plasmonic crystal, and nanowire, we reconstructed distinct phase distributions that revealed their underlying radiation mechanisms. This reference-free framework offers a robust and flexible route for retrieving the phase of electron beam-excited optical fields without relying on a reference wave, making it readily extendable to a wide range of nanostructures.
n47a7c3e613f4: Accessing crystal phases under nonequilibrium conditions is a central challenge for expanding the landscape of materials. Simple-cubic (sc) structures are considered energetically unfavorable in elemental solids and have previously been confirmed only in polonium. Here, we report the direct observation of a previously unrecognized sc-Ag formed under far-from-equilibrium conditions. Using electron beam irradiation inside a high-resolution transmission electron microscope as a trigger, we induced the radiolytic decomposition of silver iodide (AgI) and tracked the in situ formation of silver crystals in real time. Continuous imaging revealed that sc-Ag formation strongly depends on the polymorph of the precursor and occurs selectively from metastable γ-AgI. The sc-Ag exhibited unusually high chemical reactivity, undergoing gradual oxidation into silver oxide under high-vacuum conditions where conventional fcc-Ag remains stable. These findings demonstrate that irreversible crystal formation pathways can kinetically stabilize crystal structures inaccessible under near-equilibrium conditions and extend a previously inaccessible structural limit of metallic bonding.
neb234c21ae13: Dense TiO2 thin-film electrodes suffer from limited electrolyte penetration and restricted Li-ion transport, making the electrode architecture a critical parameter for efficient charge storage. Herein, glancing-angle deposition (GLAD) combined with reactive magnetron sputtering is used to engineer ion-accessible TiO2 nanocolumnar architectures without compositional modification or postprocessing. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations guided the selection of substrate tilt and azimuthal rotation conditions to control the column orientation, intercolumnar spacing, and open porosity. The predicted morphologies were subsequently validated by electron microscopy for the experimentally deposited thin films. Electrochemical measurements show that GLAD-engineered electrodes deliver up to approximately 4-fold higher areal capacitance than dense TiO2 films. ToF-SIMS depth profiling further reveals that Li species remain largely concentrated near the surface of dense films. In contrast, the GLAD-engineered nanocolumnar architecture allows for a more uniform Li distribution throughout the electrode depth. These results establish morphology-controlled ion accessibility as the primary origin of the enhanced electrochemical response.
n4d80e6efe44e: Two-dimensional halide perovskites host strongly bound excitons whose fine structure governs polarization selection rules and radiative recombination, yet spectral features in phenethylammonium lead iodide ((PEA)2PbI4) remain controversially assigned. Here, polarization-resolved low-temperature photoluminescence (PL) combined with first-principles G0W0+BSE calculations probes the intralayer and interlayer excitonic fine structure of this Ruddlesden–Popper perovskite. The low-energy multiplet is consistent with the intralayer excitonic fine structure governed by electron–hole exchange, crystal symmetry, and layer inequivalence in the two-layer unit cell, without requiring Rashba effects or exciton–polaron mechanisms as its primary origin. The weak doublet about 40 meV higher is best accounted for by interlayer excitons based on its energetics, splitting, and real-space character. Distortion-induced mixing of interlayer excitons with bright intralayer excitons provides a plausible explanation for the observed interlayer PL intensities and nearly orthogonal polarizations. These results support a layer-resolved excitonic picture encompassing both intralayer and interlayer states in (PEA)2PbI4.
n1bc9f897b04e: Silver bismuth sulfide (AgBiS2) quantum dots (QDs) are promising candidates for eco-friendly solution-based solar cells. However, structural defects in QDs hinder high efficiency. Controllable synthesis of AgBiS2 QDs remains challenging, often yielding crystals with surface and lattice defects that promote nonradiative recombination. Improving AgBiS2 QD quality before film formation is crucial, as synthesis-related imperfections often persist in devices and inherently limit effective passivation later on. This study presents a photoinduced surface reconstruction method for AgBiS2 QDs that achieves nearly perfect ionic ordering with lower lattice strain, leading to denser films and better band alignment with charge layers than the initial AgBiS2 QDs. Corresponding solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 9.71%, exceeding 8.16% for untreated solar cells. By enhancing AgBiS2 QD quality at the source rather than relying solely on downstream passivation, this approach offers a complementary pathway to high-performance QD solar cells.
na56287cc88e2: Anticounterfeiting technologies capable of enabling both visual authentication and machine-readable encryption are critically demanded. Here we present a wafer-scale and flexible tellurium nanowire (TeNW) platform with programmable localized orientation, enabling dual-mode anticounterfeiting based on polarization-encoded information. By employing a lock–shear and lift-off strategy, pixelated and highly aligned TeNW arrays with feature sizes down to 5 μm are realized on arbitrary rigid and flexible substrates, exhibiting dichroic ratios of up to 4.6 and stretchability exceeding 100%. Beyond passive optical security, the semiconducting nature of TeNWs allows these oriented arrays to function as active channels in asymmetric Schottky photodetectors, delivering broadband photoresponse (405–1064 nm), an anisotropic photocurrent ratio of 2.35, and an ultrafast response time of 430 μs under self-powered operation. Leveraging this capability, polarization-encoded information can be transduced into polarization-sensitive electrical signals, establishing a hardware-level security paradigm that physically encodes information in the material rather than in algorithms.
n6138ed783720: Stereochemistry underlies structure–function relationships across biology and materials science. Here, we investigate electron transport in oligopeptide stereoisomers using single-molecule experiments and computational modeling. Our results show that stereochemical modifications in tyrosine-based peptides lead to significant variations in molecular conductance and transport distance along the peptide backbone, associated with changes in aromatic side-chain interactions and electronic coupling. In alanine-based peptides, stereochemical modifications alter molecular conductance through secondary-structure interactions associated with β-turn conformations. Molecular dynamics simulations and quantum mechanical calculations reveal the molecular origins of these stereochemistry-dependent structural and electronic properties. Overall, this work shows that stereochemical modification of nonterminal amino acids provides a means to control electron transport through distinct mechanisms involving aromatic side-chain interactions and secondary structure. These results establish stereochemistry as a molecular design parameter for controlling electron transport in peptide-based electronic materials.
n075d9b648d12: Magnetoresistive effects are typically symmetric under magnetization reversal. However, nonlinear spin transport can give rise to unidirectional magnetoresistance in systems with strong spin–orbit interaction and broken inversion symmetry. Here, we report a large magnonic unidirectional spin Hall magnetoresistance (USMR) in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrPS4 in contact with Pt, driven by the nonequilibrium magnon accumulation with a finite magnon chemical potential. In contrast to conventional magnonic USMR driven by magnetization fluctuations, this effect persists under strong magnetic fields and low temperatures. The magnitude of magnonic USMR in CrPS4/Pt exceeds that of YIG/Pt by more than 2 orders of magnitude and surpasses the electrical USMR in metallic Ta/Co bilayers by a factor of 2. Our results highlight magnon chemical potential gradients for nonlinear magnetoresistance in antiferromagnetic van der Waals heterostructures and open a route to magnon-based antiferromagnetic spintronic functionalities in two-terminal device geometries.
nd95c37a4ec19: Polymer thin films in wearable electronics undergo creep recovery during operation as on-body devices, resulting in unrecoverable strain that subsequently induces mechanical instability in the films. However, the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films has not been investigated due to their intrinsic fragility and the difficulty in controlling ultralow loads for the films. We evaluate the creep recovery behavior of pseudo-free-standing polymer thin films as a function of creep stress, developing direct creep recovery testing with a feedback-based ultralow-load control system. Polystyrene (PS) thin films exhibit a sharp increase in unrecoverable strain with the onset of crazing. While poly(3-butylthiophene) (P3BT) thin films show a linear increase in the relative ratio of unrecoverable strain with increasing creep stress, poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) thin films exhibit a viscoelastic strain larger than unrecoverable strain. This work reveals the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films and proposes a direct creep recovery testing method.
nb55bfa734a4d: Temperature can influence competing catalytic pathways differently, but its role in balancing electrocatalytic activity and stability remains underexplored. Now it has been shown that cooling water to near freezing selectively suppresses manganese dioxide dissolution, extending water oxidation lifetime and revealing anomalous subzero kinetics.
n191280d1777b: Defect engineering is promising to solve the photocarrier dynamics mismatch between rapid bulk recombination and sluggish surface oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in PEC water splitting but is limited by forming random or bulk defects. Herein, we adopt a phase and facet modulation strategy to construct a 2D defective spinel β-In2S3 photoanode with highly exposed, well-ordered indium vacancies (VIn). These VIn introduce a shallow acceptor level near the valence band (VB), which induces selective photohole capture to VIn shallow traps. The efficient and fast (∼0.13 ps) photohole transfer from the VB to the VIn state and the sharply elongated lifetime for photoholes accumulated at VIn, by facilitating band-edge exciton dissociation, induce separation efficiency nearly 100% even at low bias. Meanwhile, surface VIn lowers the OER barrier by boosting the conversion of *OH to *O and promotes surface reaction kinetics, enabling the photohole transfer efficiency to reach 95%. Thus, VIn simultaneously acts as photohole-capture centers and surface-active sites to optimize photohole separation and interfacial transfer dynamics. Through introducing and exposing ordered VIn to reaction interfaces, the β-In2S3-2D photoanode achieves a record-high photocurrent density of 9.7 mA cm–2 at 1.23 VRHE and an IPCE reaching 80% without hole scavengers. Such a regulation mechanism can guide reverse design of defective semiconductor photoanodes for efficient PEC conversion.
n09a1cbc0aeea: Adsorbate site hopping, defined here as surface-confined migration of adsorbed species or adsorbate equivalents between distinct sites, is a widespread phenomenon in heterogeneous catalysis and includes spillover between different surface phases. Because it enables communication between spatially separated functionalities, site hopping has often been viewed as a route to bifunctional catalytic synergy and, in some cases, to performance beyond constraints imposed by Brønsted–Evans–Polanyi relationships. However, its catalytic value is conditional rather than universal. Downhill migration to a stronger binding site may increase local barriers for subsequent transformation or introduce site-regeneration penalties, while kinetically accessible hopping may remain irrelevant if it does not reduce the energetic span of the catalytic cycle. In addition, apparent rate enhancements assigned to site hopping can arise from other modes of intersite communication, including desorption–readsorption, subsurface or bulk diffusion, ion–electron intersite coupling, catalyst restructuring, or changes in active-site identity. This Perspective develops a thermodynamic and kinetic framework for distinguishing these processes and assessing when site hopping becomes catalytically consequential. We discuss driving forces, hopping barriers, coverage and dynamic surface effects, kinetic signatures, and diagnostic pitfalls, with the aim of clarifying when site hopping can be used as a catalyst design principle.
nd471b55536b6: 8,12-Guaianolides are a class of sesquiterpene lactones that exhibit diverse biological activities, which are often strongly influenced by structural variations, including the stereochemistry of the C8 oxygen substituent. Here, we report a concise, diastereodivergent approach to both 8α,12- and 8β,12-guaianolide scaffolds from santonin-derived triene 5 by combining engineered cytochrome P450 BM3-catalyzed allylic C–H hydroxylation with a photochemical rearrangement. The P450 BM3 mutant LG-23 selectively hydroxylates the C8α position of 5, whereas a single additional mutation, L437I, inverts the facial selectivity to favor C8β hydroxylation. Structure-guided mutagenesis and docking studies suggest that the β-methyl group of Ile437 remodels the active site and enforces a flipped substrate binding mode that directs the opposite C8 C–H bond toward the heme iron. The utility of this enzymatic stereochemical switch was demonstrated by the synthesis of the 8α,12-guaianolides xerantholide (1) and mikanokryptin (2) and the 8β,12-guaianolide 11,13-dehydroachalensolide (4). This study demonstrates that a single active-site mutation in P450 BM3 can switch the facial selectivity of C–H hydroxylation at one carbon center, providing a strategy for stereodivergent enzymatic oxidation in complex-molecule synthesis.
n7bd1ca9de2cc: Highly active water oxidation catalysts based on earth-abundant elements are strongly demanded for practical application of artificial photosynthesis. An iron complex with a chlorin ligand derived from chlorophyll-a demonstrated the highest turnover frequency (= 21.3 ± 0.3 s–1) and turnover number (= 6920 ± 110) among homogeneous catalysts reported for photocatalytic water oxidation utilizing [RuII(bpy)3]2+ (bpy: 2,2′-bipyridine) and S2O82– as a photosensitizer and a sacrificial electron acceptor, respectively. The molecular nature of the Fe chlorin complex during the photocatalytic water oxidation was confirmed by dynamic light scattering analysis and electrospray ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. Also, kinetic studies suggested that the rate-determining step is O–O bond formation via coupling of two high-valent iron–oxo species formed by three-electron oxidation of the mononuclear Fe chlorin unit with water. The high planarity of the chlorin ligand enables the high-valent iron–oxo species to approach another iron–oxo unit closely, thereby facilitating O–O bond formation.
nd1125c45a8c2: Buried-interface engineering is critical for inverted perovskite solar cells, yet integrating anchoring, charge transport, electrostatic regulation, and defect passivation within single molecular systems often creates intrinsic trade-offs. Here, we use cavity-selective host–guest recognition to construct a modular, recognition-directed interface. The cavity of dipolar 4-tert-butylsulfonylcalix[4]arene (tBSCA) selectively accommodates the terminal phenyl group of substrate-anchored Ph-4PACz. Comparisons with a structurally related calixarene analogue and competing inclusion orientations identify a thermodynamically preferred Ph-4PACz-tBSCA configuration, distinguishing cavity-selective association from nonspecific interactions. This preferred configuration underpins a preferentially organized dipolar interface that retains Ph-4PACz-mediated anchoring and charge transport while enabling tBSCA to regulate interfacial electrostatics, reduce interfacial defect sites, and suppress defect-assisted halide migration and interfacial accumulation. The resulting devices achieve a PCE of 27.36% (certified at 26.74%), and a 110 cm2 module delivers a certified efficiency of 22.61%. These results demonstrate configuration-selective molecular recognition as a strategy for the modular organization of complementary functions at buried perovskite interfaces.
n053a91296ef7: Pure-water membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) represent a promising strategy to eliminate (bi)carbonate salt precipitation for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2R). However, the absence of alkali metal cations fundamentally restricts CO2 activation and intermediate stabilization, thereby reducing catalytic performance. Here, we overcome this limitation by identifying the ionomer charge density as a key molecular-level parameter associated with pure-water CO2R. By comparing anion-exchange ionomers with varying charge characteristics, we reveal that high-charge-density ionomer (HCDI) introduces a favorable catalyst–membrane interfacial environment, enabling superior macroscopic CO2R performance. HCDI-enabled MEAs achieve >99% CO Faradaic efficiency at 100 mA cm–2 and sustain ∼92% at 1000 mA cm–2. In situ diagnosis and electrochemical characterization reveal that the HCDI-functionalized interface produces a substantial *CO signal, while concurrently suppressing hydrogen evolution. By decoupling cation effects from liquid electrolytes, these findings support interfacial ionomer charge density as a useful comparative parameter for pure-water CO2 MEA electrolyzers.
n6bade4f80897: Integrating alternative oxidation reactions (AORs) into photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is promising for unassisted hydrogen production and value-added chemical synthesis, yet organic semiconductor (OS) photoanodes suffer from poor charge extraction and short carrier lifetimes. Here, we address this bottleneck by stabilizing long-lived hole polarons through macroporous tin oxide (mcSnO2) interlayers. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that accelerated electron extraction through mcSnO2 stabilizes hole polaron states, substantially prolonging carrier lifetimes. Consequently, the optimized organic photoanodes outperform bare counterparts by more than 5.5-fold, retaining 74% of their initial photocurrent over 15 h for iodide oxidation and 61% over 35 h for ascorbic acid oxidation. Furthermore, integrating this robust organic photoanode with an OS-based photocathode enables the first bias-free organic PEC tandem cell coupling hydrogen evolution with AORs, delivering a remarkable solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 1.4%. These findings establish interfacial carrier lifetime engineering as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance and durable organic PEC systems.
n40622435b3df: A triazine–heptazine homojunction in porous carbon nitride nanotubes enables efficient charge separation and oxygen activation, enhancing visible-light-driven H 2 O 2 production and selective benzyl alcohol oxidation to benzaldehyde.
n4e3f0fc1db08: Tandem catalytic conversion of syngas to methyl acetate and acetic acid was studied using a Cu-based mixed oxide for methanol synthesis and an Ag-exchanged MOR zeolite for DME carbonylation.
n7346fcd5e078: Interface engineering has emerged as a critical strategy for advancing perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs), enabling remarkable improvements in the device efficiency, stability, and spectral purity. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of interface engineering in PeLEDs, beginning with the fundamental principles that govern carrier injection, transport, and recombination at heterojunctions between perovskite emitters and charge-transport layers. We then survey advanced characterization techniques, including photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and time-resolved optical methods, that elucidate interfacial energy-level alignment, defect states, charge dynamics, and degradation pathways. On the basis of these insights, we systematically discuss versatile engineering strategies, such as self-assembled monolayers, dipole interlayers, dimensional regulation, and passivation schemes, to mitigate non-radiative recombination, balance charge fluxes, and enhance operational stability. Finally, we highlight emerging applications spanning high-resolution displays, flexible lighting, and lasing while outlining key challenges and future directions toward commercial realization. This Review aims to offer a holistic framework linking interfacial design to device performance, guiding next-generation PeLED development.
n65cca399b7fe: The interfacial electron-transfer process acts as a pivotal kinetic determinant of electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency, governing the generation of excited-state emitters and thus dictating the intensity and stability of ECL signals. Currently, harnessing diverse nanomaterials has driven significant advances in the development of novel ECL luminophores and the activation of coreactants. However, most of these luminophores exhibit low ECL efficiency in aqueous media, and the intrinsic reaction and activation mechanisms remain ambiguous because of their complex structures and compositions. Notably, tuning electron-transfer pathways at the molecular/atomic level can not only enable efficient signal amplification but also facilitate the tracking of reaction pathways, thereby providing deeper insights into the fundamental mechanisms underlying ECL processes. This Review comprehensively summarizes advances during the past five years in tuning interfacial electron transfer to enhance ECL. Furthermore, we highlight progress in electron-transfer-mediated signal amplification strategies for highly sensitive ECL biosensing and bioimaging applications. Finally, we propose and discuss the challenges and perspectives associated with improving the ECL efficiency through the modulation of electron transfer processes. Precise regulation of interfacial electron transfer holds substantial promise for advancing ECL theories, clarifying reaction mechanisms, and expanding the scope of ECL-based bioanalytical applications.

na77c9788cf55: We first performed descriptor-based systematic screening and identified the six-carbon molecule with a moderate terminal-to-terminal distance (6.46 Å) as forming a robust bidentate anchoring configuration that suppresses shuttling.
ne736f6de4e25: Dual-anion regulation induces covalency-driven amorphization in Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes, promoting Li+ transport, oxidative stability, and mechanical compliance. This bond-covalency-mediated strategy enables long-life all-solid-state lithium batteries and provides a general design principle for high-performance halide solid-state electrolytes.
n7385a583557b: Curvature couples polarization, crystalline defects, and interfacial electrostatics in freestanding ferroelectric oxides. Here, we examine bent epitaxial Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3/SrTiO3/Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3 (PZT/STO/PZT) membranes using atomic-resolution electron microscopy, strain and polarization mapping, relative projected-potential reconstruction, and molecular dynamics simulations. The tensile-side PZT remains comparatively lattice-continuous and accommodates bending mainly through polarization rotation and domain reorganization. The compressive-side PZT exhibits dislocations, slip-related lattice offsets, surface steps, and localized strain concentration. Curvature-series observations and images across U-shaped and N-shaped regions indicate that the defect-rich region follows the local compressive stress state. Bending also breaks the approximate electrostatic symmetry of the two PZT/STO interfaces: the tensile side shows weakened negative interfacial contrast, whereas the compressive side shows a dislocation-associated increase in relative projected potential. These results identify curvature as a variable for selecting polar versus plastic relaxation pathways and modulating interfacial electrostatic landscapes in flexible ferroelectric heterostructures.
n5ec1c3f27341: Silicon anodes enable high-energy-density Li-ion batteries but face reversibility challenges when operating under extreme temperature and charge-rate conditions. Now, a liquid electrolyte design results in interface protection and reduced electrode expansion during such operation, while also having lithium plating tolerance.
nb2bc4b44a338: Cathode interlayers play a pivotal role in improving the performance of organic solar cells. Yao, Zhang, Zhang, Wang et al. show a stepwise solvent treatment to achieve a vertically aligned cathode interlayer, enabling a certified efficiency of 20.65% in binary organic solar cells.
ne155ad15dc4f: Gene expression reconstituted outside the cell controls the composition and dynamics of cytoskeletal networks, bringing the tools of synthetic biology to active matter and opening a route to genetically programmed biomaterials.
nb70f07fba36a: Stacking-controllable 2D In2Se3 grown by chemical vapour deposition reveals a strong dependence of ferroelectricity on stacking order. A 2H/3R homojunction memristor achieves an on/off ratio one order of magnitude higher than that of pure-phase devices, offering opportunities for advanced ferroelectric memory applications.
nc220489fcb25: Chemical ligation of synthetic polymers is achieved via supramolecular polymerization followed by dynamic covalent polycondensation in a process that does not require thermal activation.
na37558c52271: By creating permanent cavities of well-defined size and shape within a fluid, porous liquids bring the precise control over gases afforded by microporous solids to the realm of liquids. Here, we reflect on how the porous liquid concept, beyond simply imparting fluidity to a porous solid, provides a promising platform for overcoming long-standing challenges with manipulating dissolved gases.
n48f8def67571: A modified colloidal atomic layer deposition at room temperature grows a vacancy-ordered Cs2SnCl6 shell epitaxially on CsPbCl3 nanocrystals, avoiding the core degradation and parasitic shell nucleation that accompany high-temperature routes. The resulting core–shell nanocrystals achieve an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% and retain 65% of their emission after six months of ambient storage and 30% after 48 h of exposure to added water.
n874a803e9337: Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. Departing from the conventional host-centric view, we demonstrate that reversibility in Mg batteries can be governed by electrolyte-derived reaction chemistry. Here, we harness trace water to impart controlled electrolyte reactivity, enabling electrolyte-derived Mg/Cl-containing species to participate in cathode activation. In tunnel-type MnO2, the regulated electrolyte induces lattice expansion and improves electrochemical reversibility. In organic cathodes, improved rechargeability is consistent with a stabilizing role of Cl– in anion-coupled redox. Because polar-solvent chemistry can irreversibly passivate Mg metal, a Sn/MgCl2 artificial interface suppresses parasitic anode reactions while preserving cathode activation. This strategy enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, including α/γ-MnO2, methylphenothiazine, tetrathiafulvalene, and hybrid I2/O2 systems. These findings establish electrolyte-derived chemical activation as a guiding principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in magnesium batteries.
n7b18684a7f4e: Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Although a uniform Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is suggested to improve cycle stability, the synthesis–structure relationship governing domain formation remains underexplored. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Through a comparative investigation of the synthesis mechanism, we reveal the templating effect that more clustered transition-metal oxide precursors lead to more localized Li2MnO3-like ordering in the final cathodes, a tendency also observed with a different lithium source. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.
n8d648f4076f8: The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.
n03850d8c938a: Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. Although poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) possesses high intrinsic permittivity, stabilizing its polar structure remains thermodynamically challenging. Here, we report a scalable physical processing strategy to optimize PVDF-based films via a specialized shear-imposed coating methodology. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.

n80fcdd851a13: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. Its unique surface coordination architecture governs substrate adsorption via steric effects; this structural feature, combined with the cluster’s remarkable stability, concurrently facilitates effective alkyne activation and ensures high hydrogenation selectivity. Notably, this work overcomes the conventional dependence on noble metals such as gold and palladium in hydrogenation catalysis, revealing the significant potential of ligand-protected copper nanoclusters for this transformation.
nb91102874037: While polyester waste represents a valuable carbon resource for chemical production, its upcycling typically involves multiple steps for polymer depolymerization, intermediate separation, and subsequent conversion. This work establishes a tandem catalytic method that integrates depolymerization and selective upcycling in a single process, which selectively converts diverse commercial polyesters and mixed waste streams into valuable dicarboxylic acids.
n9a1bfe755e63: This review summarizes the bioinspired design principles, core modules, assembly strategies, unique functions, advances, and bottlenecks of artificial photosynthetic cells, and outlines future opportunities for synthetic photobiological systems.
ne129cee4338d: This review summarizes molecular design strategies for shifting molecular motors from UV to visible and near-infrared operation, with emphasis on recent advances and emerging applications.
naffa31d5ae58: Branched quaternary ammonium chlorides were explored as low-chloride aqueous electrolytes for four-electron Zn–I 2 batteries. 3-Chloro-2-hydroxypropyl trimethylammonium chloride proved optimal for Ah-level pouch cells.
n7c477b3c2b75: Facing global freshwater scarcity and energy shortages, this work designs a flower-inspired 3D solar evaporator made from modified ramie yarns that simultaneously generates clean water and electricity. Its conical structure traps sunlight to drive rapid evaporation (1.77 kg m−2 h−1) and produce thermoelectric voltage (38 mV) while resisting salt crystallization even in high-salinity brine, offering a sustainable, off-grid solution for water-electricity cogeneration.
n79a1f2802c3b: A bioresorbable, metal-free molecular magnet for wireless deep-tissue sensing is reported that enables continuous cardiac monitoring and injectable organ tracking in vivo before the material safely degrades.
n8f0b777ffd55: Strong coupling between magnons and excitons in CrSBr enables microwave-to-optical transduction, offering a route towards efficient conversion between otherwise disparate frequency regimes.
n8662555b8320: Although organosilicon compounds containing different carbon substituents are ubiquitous in synthetic chemistry, their preparation is challenging. Laboratory synthesis commonly relies on the sequential substitution of tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes, producing complex mixtures that require demanding purification. This arises from limited control over nucleophilic substitution in functionalized silanes containing three or four (identical) leaving groups. Here we introduce an experimentally straightforward and reliable procedure for the preparation of both hetero- and homoleptic silanes using an overlooked monobromination of primary and secondary hydrosilanes. An equimolar amount of elemental bromine converts a Si–H bond into an Si–Br bond without ‘overbromination’. This step also shows exceptional functional-group tolerance to existing substituents at the silicon atom. Unsaturated moieties as well as heteroatom and heteroaryl groups are compatible. When performed in an iterative fashion, multihydrosilanes can be selectively converted into secondary, tertiary and quaternary silanes with two, three or four different carbon substituents in high yields. These functionalized silicon building blocks are relevant to synthetic chemistry as well as applied chemistry materials.
n2f6e6b14dbd3: The stepwise installation of carbon substituents at silicon starting from tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes is burdened by chemoselectivity issues, typically affording product mixtures. Now, monoselective bromination of multihydrosilanes followed by nucleophilic displacement opens the door to the programmable and reliable synthesis of functionalized silicon building blocks.
n617dd9db8a0f: Advances in dynamic covalent chemistry have dramatically broadened its use in polymer research. Cyclic disulfide bonds are a widely used, versatile platform for engineering dynamic polymers. The resulting polymers leverage the dynamic character of exocyclic linkages associated with cyclic disulfide bonds, along with modular, tailorable chain-end functionalities to enable self-healing and chemical recycling. This review summarizes recent advances in dynamic polymer chemistry based on cyclic disulfide bonds that have enabled new design principles for the development and innovation in advanced polymers. We highlight living/controlled polymerization strategies for cyclic disulfide monomers, covering the principal polymerization strategies and mechanisms, and discuss the future challenges and prospective directions of the field in the context of emerging societal and technological demands.
nb67843be428e: Interlayer CO 3 2− polarizes the Ni–O–Fe motif in NiFe-LDH, inducing differentiated electronic responses at the Ni and Fe sites. This site-dependent electronics promote the early formation of Ni 3+ –O and *OOH, enabling ampere-level alkaline OER.
nc5a607337783: Rational molecular engineering of the perovskite/hole transport layer interface offers a promising route to simultaneously address inefficient charge extraction, defect-mediated recombination, and lead leakage in CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite solar cells. Herein, we introduce 2,2′-dinitro-9,9′-spirobifluorene (DN-SBF) as an interfacial molecular bridge to tackle these challenges. DN-SBF optimizes energy level alignment, establishes π–π interactions, and forms exciplexes with Spiro-OMeTAD, thereby facilitating interfacial charge transport. Meanwhile, DN-SBF passivates undercoordinated Pb2+ through multiple coordination modes, including robust bidentate chelation formed by adjacent nitro groups, effectively passivating defects and suppressing non-radiative recombination. Importantly, multipoint coordination immobilizes leachable Pb2+, substantially mitigating lead leakage and improving film biocompatibility. As a result, DN-SBF-engineered CsPbI3–xBrx devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 22.40% along with significantly enhanced operational and environmental stability. This work highlights the potential of versatile molecular bridges to concurrently enhance performance, stability, and eco-friendliness, which may contribute to the development of more sustainable perovskite photovoltaics.

ned9501745b95: Transition metal fluorides (TMFs) are promising conversion-type cathode materials for high-energy lithium–metal batteries owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, making them attractive for demanding applications such as electric aviation. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish conversion kinetics, pronounced voltage hysteresis, and poor electrochemical reversibility. Understanding the structural and chemical evolution of TMFs and the electrode–electrolyte interphase formed during cycling is essential for improving their performance. Monodisperse nanocrystalline TMFs are ideal model systems for high-resolution transmission electron microscopy because their uniform size, morphology, and electron transparency enable representative nanoscale characterization. Here, we investigate a reproducible colloidal synthesis of monodisperse, single-crystalline CoF2 nanorods and elucidate the mechanisms governing their formation to achieve precise control over particle size and aspect ratio. By independently varying reaction time, temperature, precursor composition, and ligand chemistry, we identify the key factors controlling precursor decomposition, burst nucleation, phase selection, and anisotropic crystal growth. These insights provide a transferable framework for the controlled synthesis of a broad range of transition metal fluoride nanocrystals.
n4598f3ccb9e9: In anode-free Li metal batteries, a bare current collector must be converted into a reversible Li metal anode during the first charge, making Li nucleation decisive for reversibility. However, how current collector microstructure governs Li nucleation and growth remains poorly understood, since prior studies focused on single-crystal surfaces to identify favorable crystallographic orientations, leaving grain boundaries unexplored. Here, we identify grain boundary density and character in copper current collectors as key regulators of Li deposition uniformity. Systematic annealing decouples grain size from surface chemistry, revealing that deposition uniformity improves with copper grain coarsening but saturates as disordered boundaries are eliminated during grain growth, leaving predominantly low-energy configurations. Atomistic simulations show disordered boundaries impose high barriers to Li adatom migration, whereas ordered boundaries and adjacent low-index terraces provide low-barrier pathways for redistribution. Copper foils engineered beyond this threshold sustain uniform Li plating across diverse electrolytes and improve cyclability in anode-free cells.
n9f4039694a62: Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) based on colloidal InAs quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as promising light sources for the short-wave infrared (SWIR) range. However, their development is limited by relatively low photoluminescence quantum yield as well as intrinsic device design challenges. Here, we report LEDs with electroluminescence (EL) in the SWIR based on InAs/ZnSe core/shell colloidal QDs, synthesized via a seedless one-pot approach that enables the rapid growth of relatively large InAs cores. Zirconium-doped indium oxide (InZrO) was used as the bottom transparent electrode owing to its significantly higher infrared transparency compared to the commonly employed tin-doped indium oxide (ITO). These two key innovations pushed the EL beyond 1500 nm, with external quantum efficiencies of 3.0, 1.2, and 0.6% at 1093, 1198, and 1547 nm, respectively.
n677d8e82fc56: Conventional carbonization of semi-coke induces excessive ordering of aromatic skeletons, producing dense graphitic structures that hinder Na+ intercalation and suppress low-potential plateau capacity. Here, we develop a rapid thermomechanical coupling sintering strategy using moderate pressure to drive π–π interactions and topological reconfiguration of aromatic units. This process suppresses excessive graphitization while constructing interconnected, twisted pseudo-graphitic domains with abundant closed nanopores. At 1000 mA g–1, PTR-HC reaches 80% SOC in ≈14.4 min and retains 90.1% of its plateau capacity, enabled by abundant Na+ storage sites and rapid diffusion pathways. Kinetic analyses reveal accelerated Na+ transport and a thin, NaF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase with fewer organic components. In situ XRD and Raman attribute slope capacity to surface/defect adsorption and intercalation and the plateau capacity to quasi-metallic Na clusters in closed pores. This work establishes pressure-driven topological engineering as a promising strategy for upgrading semi-coke into fast-charging hard carbon with high plateau-capacity retention.
nadb66549bf6c: Interfacial losses at the perovskite/C60 and C60/metal contacts limit inverted perovskite solar cell performance. Here, we introduce a vacuum-evaporated molecule with giant spontaneous orientation polarization, 6F-2PI, for simultaneously tailoring both interfaces. Incorporating 6F-2PI increases the work function of perovskite, reducing the conduction band offset at the perovskite/C60 interface, which facilitates electron extraction. Concurrently, its phthalimide moieties passivate defect states, suppressing nonradiative recombination, as evidenced by a 0.03 eV recovery in quasi-Fermi level splitting. At the C60/metal interface, 6F-2PI also delivers efficient charge extraction, improved interfacial contact, and thermal resilience. Moreover, its hydrophobic fluorinated units prevent moisture ingress. Consequently, this dual-interface modulation boosts PCE from 18.5% to 22.5% with exceptional device stability, retaining over 90% of its initial efficiency after 2000 h under ambient conditions. Furthermore, this framework exhibits universal compatibility across both vacuum-deposited and solution-processed devices and simplifies processing for mass production.

n37d5bb016408: The bacterial surface represents the primary interface between pathogens and hosts, yet its chemical and architectural complexity challenges conventional classification. This Review examines structural organization, molecular composition, and biogenesis of bacterial surface components across the Gracilicutes and Terrabacteria clades, linking mechanistic detail to pathogenic function. We describe lipid diversity, integral membrane protein biogenesis, and lipoprotein processing at the inner membrane and how these components support surface remodeling, secretion, and virulence. We then examine the peptidoglycan layer and its role in immune recognition and surface protein display, teichoic acids and their contributions to antimicrobial resistance and immune evasion, and S layers, whose crystalline arrays mediate adhesion and immune modulation. The outer membrane section covers lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, outer membrane protein biogenesis and folding, lipoprotein trafficking, and contributions to pathogenicity, while the mycobacterial section addresses the mycolyl-arabinogalactan-peptidoglycan complex and virulence factors. We discuss bacterial capsule diversity, biosynthesis, and use as vaccine antigens, along with adhesive surface structures such as fimbriae, pili, and curli fibers and their roles in colonization and biofilm formation, before covering secretion systems types I through XI and their contributions to virulence. This Review provides a framework for understanding how bacterial surface diversity shapes infection and identifies chemical vulnerabilities for therapeutics.
n3f072c4ef5be: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer exceptional structural resolution for investigating how local environments govern catalytic behavior and, ultimately, for controlling these effects through catalyst design. Yet, atomic dispersion does not imply a single or fully defined catalytic environment. The behavior of atomically dispersed active centers is shaped by a hierarchical local environment comprising persistent and transient contributions, while also being influenced by an extended reaction environment that intersects with the local environment in controlling reactivity and can become integrated into it. Establishing these boundaries and understanding how these contributions evolve and interact are central challenges in the interpretation and design of SACs. Here, we critically examine how local environments are generated and controlled, experimentally and theoretically resolved across spatial and temporal scales, transformed from synthesis through operation and deactivation, and linked to catalytic performance through structural, energetic, and electronic descriptors. By integrating aspects that are often considered separately and highlighting those that remain insufficiently addressed, we provide a roadmap toward the predictive, environment-driven design of SACs and a deeper understanding of catalytic phenomena.
n98cc28f955b7: Regenerated cellulose (RC), derived from natural cellulose through dissolution and regeneration processes, has emerged as a sustainable, versatile, and cost-effective material for advanced electronic devices. With unique hierarchical structures, abundant hydroxy groups, and excellent mechanical and thermal properties, RC allows extensive customization of its characteristics, offering biocompatibility, flexibility, processability, and environmental friendliness. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in RC-based electronics, focusing on its multiscale molecular configuration, dissolution and regeneration mechanisms, and functionalization and engineering strategies. It first provides a detailed molecular-level analysis of RC structures and formation mechanisms. The principles and strategies of cellulose dissolution and regeneration are then discussed, with emphasis on solvent systems and structure-regulating mechanisms essential for processing control. Functionalization strategies are categorized into direct modification and hybridization with functional materials. Notably, the hybridization approach involves the development of conductive, semiconductive, and insulating RC composites, evaluated from the perspectives of material selection, interfacial design, and processing techniques. Subsequently, engineering approaches to enhance mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and optical transparency are explored. Applications of RC in sensors, actuators, circuits, energy harvesting and storage devices, and electromagnetic shielding devices are highlighted, demonstrating its potential to drive sustainable innovation in electronics. Finally, future directions are proposed to address remaining challenges, paving the way for RC to contribute to eco-friendly, high-performance electronic devices.
n2259056ca8a7: Classification of donor–acceptor molecular components used to identify key self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) as HTLs for overcoming efficiency limitations in solar cells.
ne25eeb3fee85: This review summarizes the classification, physical and chemical synthesis, and structure–property relationships of layered superlattices, with emphasis on emerging applications, structural control, dynamic characterization, and device integration.
nca9f0c2237c8: This review proposes a mechanism-based unified framework for liquid hydrocarbon separation membranes and discusses the fabrication- and application-oriented regulation strategies in microenvironment engineering.
n8f2204474093: Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier due to its clean and versatile nature, offering opportunities for decarbonizing diverse sectors. Hydrogen utilization in many applications relies on identifying and understanding materials with exceptional hydrogen storage and transport properties. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of hydrogenation reactions in ternary ABO3 perovskites using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML) screening. We performed DFT simulations for a diverse range of perovskites featuring a variety of A-site cations (Ca, Sr, Ba) and B-site cations (Co, Fe, Mn, Ce, Ti, Zr) across various phases (cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, and hexagonal). By computing all data at the same theoretical level, we establish a consistent framework to compare how crystal phase, lattice-site chemistry, and host electronic structure govern hydrogen incorporation and diffusion. Therefore, we identify hexagonal SrMnO3, cubic SrFeO3, and hexagonal BaFeO3 as particularly promising candidates, combining favorable hydrogenation thermodynamics (ΔG < 1 eV) with low rotation and hopping barriers (<0.2 eV), while orthorhombic phases, although thermodynamically preferred, suffer from proton trapping, highlighting the importance of phase engineering toward cubic/hexagonal frameworks. Ab initio molecular dynamics further support this phase-dependent kinetic picture by showing relatively facile H diffusion in cubic SrFeO3 but much slower proton motion in orthorhombic BaCeO3 under the same conditions. By incorporating spatial and electronic descriptors with the DFT data into our ML models, we further develop a mechanistically motivated ML model based on structural and electronic descriptors to screen hydrogenation thermodynamics across 111 ternary ABO3 compositions. This model led to the identification of two additional promising candidates, hexagonal BaPdO3 and cubic BaSnO3, which were subsequently validated by DFT calculations. These findings provide a foundation for the rational design of ABO3 perovskites and demonstrate the potential of ML-driven frameworks with chemical insights to accelerate materials discovery in energetic and catalytic applications.
n84be227f2011: The propagation of both catalyst diffusion and reaction fronts in a polymeric chemically amplified resist (CAR) is evaluated by time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) depth profiling, and is compared with the propagation of catalyst diffusion fronts in inert resist analogues. We report that catalysts display accelerated and highly non-Fickian dynamics in the reactive CAR, even when located well behind the propagation front, while simple Fickian diffusion is observed for the same conditions in inert resist analogues. The complex catalyst dynamics of reactive systems is attributed to two key factors: (1) Transient free volume following deprotection events, which is a long-hypothesized acceleration mechanism acting on the diffusion front; and (2) a newly identified plasticization process induced by inert, nonvolatile byproducts of catalyst photoactivation. We propose a physics-informed model of enhanced catalyst diffusion due to the independent contributions of these two processes, and demonstrate that this model coupled to a first-order reaction provides a reasonable prediction of both the diffusion and reaction fronts. Our study presents a critical evaluation of mechanisms that control the spatial extent of reaction in CARs, and suggests that quantitative models of the patterning process should account for the impact of nonvolatile catalyst activation byproducts.
nf7c814172a5b: Although methane pyrolysis appears to be a promising technology for avoiding direct CO 2 emissions, growing dependence on natural gas and the high methane fugitive emissions associated with the process may offset its claimed benefits.
n91d94e745e84: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? This perspective reveals they actually deliver markedly enhanced thermal safety over carbonates in sodium architectures alongside uniquely higher thermal resilience toward metallic sodium than lithium equivalents. However, this protective margin is fundamentally negated by oxygen-driven chemical autoxidation rather than mere electrochemical degradation. These insights establish the anode-free ether configuration as the definitive trajectory for future sodium batteries, perfectly balancing energy density with robust safety.
ne37abb50eb58: Next-generation two-dimensional electronics require robust insulating layers that effectively control current without compromising device performance. Here, we report fluorinated diamane, a diamond-like van der Waals material, as a high-performance gate dielectric. By combining a high dielectric constant, exceptional breakdown strength, and efficient heat dissipation, fluorinated diamane integrates seamlessly with diverse two-dimensional semiconductors and memory devices. This material platform addresses long-standing dielectric bottlenecks in ultra-scaled two-dimensional electronics.
n13a8e447775c: Translating local stereochemical information into higher-order helical architectures is a central challenge in materials design. Now it has been shown that stereochemically preorganized Au4 nanoclusters assemble into homochiral triple helices through directional aurophilic interactions, providing a design strategy for chiral nanocluster materials with amplified chiroptical responses.
n1c5fe76634c2: Molecular motors typically rotate by cycling through excitation and relaxation to ground states. Now it has been shown that a molecular motor can be driven by angular-momentum transfer. Circulating positive and negative currents flowing through orbitals of opposite helicity along a carbon–carbon triple bond enable unidirectional rotation.
nc4af52b33230: When defect-mediated losses are mitigated, lithium niobate phononic crystal nanomechanical resonators can have intrinsic phonon lifetimes of up to 21 ms at gigahertz frequencies.
n78efa0d612ee: Confining water within a polymeric hydrogen-bond network creates a controlled aqueous reaction environment that stabilizes precursors and directs the growth of dense, crack-free perovskite thick films. The resulting X-ray detectors achieve an ultralow detection limit of 19.8 nGyair s−1.
n28e992a16ec2: Diffusion-limited conversion of pre-formed covalent organic framework membranes creates a continuous chemical gradient across their thickness, with linkage conversion increasing from one face to the other while preserving aligned crystalline nanochannels. This asymmetry directs selective ion transport and increases salinity-gradient energy conversion, while the formation of robust linkages improves acid stability.
n38cc2abfab13: Reversible zinc oxidation, enhanced by lactate coordination, enables a self-sustained, circuit-free pathway for high-density hydrogen storage and delivery. By overcoming solubility limits under ambient conditions, this system delivers higher volumetric capacity and safety than existing carriers, providing a robust alternative to high-pressure infrastructure for decentralized, on-demand green hydrogen delivery.
n0d952b2b1d7b: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are a class of crystalline, porous networks constructed by polymerization of organic building blocks. However, most COF syntheses developed so far rely on acid- or base-catalysed reactions that are sensitive to monomer structure, require extensive condition screening, proceed under harsh conditions over several days and often yield low-quality products. Here we report a general hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy enabled by benzimidazole and its derivatives, acting as both hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors, to produce high-quality COFs. Distinct from conventional catalysis, these catalysts interact with monomers, intermediates and transition states, thereby reducing energy barriers at each step and promoting reversibility. This approach enables control through catalyst-to-monomer ratios and allows the rapid synthesis, within hours, of imide-, imine-, hydrazone- and sp2-carbon-linked COFs with high crystallinity and porosity. The method further supports catalyst reuse and 1,000-fold scale-up, producing COFs with benchmark proton conductivity, establishing hydrogen-bonding catalysis as a versatile route for scalable COF synthesis and applications. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are typically synthesized under harsh acid- or base-catalysed conditions. Here a hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy based on reusable benzimidazole enables the rapid and scalable production of COFs with high crystallinity and porosity, offering a general route to imide, imine, hydrazone and sp2-carbon-linked COF synthesis.
nf0562d26e0df: Porosity has long been considered a property exclusive to solids, yet a new class of materials now combines permanent, well defined pores with the ability to flow. Realizing the full promise of these materials as ‘supersolvents’ will require a deeper understanding of the liquid–pore interface and continued exploration of understudied designs, alongside their translation into separation, catalysis, sensing and therapeutic applications.
nb499b9db648a: A diffusion-limited topotactic exchange strategy transforms vertically aligned imine-linked covalent organic framework membranes into gradient-encoded frameworks across multiple linkage chemistries while preserving crystallinity and channel orientation. The built-in chemical asymmetry enables directional ion transport, enhanced osmotic energy conversion and robust operation under strongly acidic conditions.
n819e845d5be8: The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. Herein, an in situ modification strategy that introduces NH4+ species in Nb2CTx MXene electrodes and integrates them with 1T phase VS2/WS2 heteronanosheets is evaluated. Operando Raman analysis revealed that the process involves cation dehydration and K+ rehydration. These results highlight the importance of NH4+ dynamics, thermodynamic stability, and interfacial interactions. A VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+//N-doped nanocube-based asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated, exhibiting a peak energy density of 54 Wh kg–1 and long-term cycling stability without significant performance degradation.
nca948f974a8a: A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. na4e19c33972d: Understanding the dynamic interplay between all components in complex electrocatalytic systems is crucial to advancing their performance. na1cf152b01fc: The electrochemical carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) is an attractive anodic alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction, offering a route to lower the energy demand of electrosynthesis while utilizing abundant industrial waste gas. The system sustains bias-free operation for >140 h. Pulsed electrolysis was introduced to alleviate such carbonate buildup and stabilized operation at 100 mA cm–2. Techno-economic analysis estimated an H2O2 minimum selling price of $0.71 kg–1. Together, these results establish COOR as a practical strategy for energy-efficient electrosynthesis using industrial waste gas.
na2ef69e2788a: Integrating dry carbon electrodes (CEs) into inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offers a solvent-free, scalable route to low-cost photovoltaics. This coordination-derived interlayer serves a dual function: it acts as a structural buffer, enabling damage-free dry CE lamination, and it establishes an energetic band alignment that bridges the ETL/CE work-function gap. Consequently, our devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.12% and maintain their initial efficiency after 1000 h of dark N2 storage, establishing metal-polymer interfacial coordination as a viable pathway for robust inverted C-PSCs.
nc8d8f7d0533e: Two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) mixed tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, but uncontrolled crystallization produces excessive low-n phases that impede charge extraction due to a quantum confinement effect. Here, we employ 1,4-benzenediammonium iodide (1,4-BDI2) as a multifunctional additive to regulate crystallization, phase distribution, and defects. The additive modulates precursor colloid assembly and retards low-dimensional crystal growth, yielding dense films dominated by highly oriented three-dimensional perovskites with suppressed n = 1 and reduced n = 2 phases. Meanwhile, 1,4-BD2+ cations and unincorporated organic ligands accumulate at grain boundaries to form a passivating complex that passivates deep-trap states and forms favorable interfacial energy-level alignment to promote charge transfer. Consequently, inverted tin perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.94% and an open-circuit voltage of 0.91 V, together with improved operational and storage stability. This work establishes an integrated molecular strategy for phase regulation and defect passivation in efficient lead-free photovoltaics.

nae349e85fe17: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures. n3f9ff6cc68a9: Two-dimensional infrared (2DIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for probing the structure and picosecond dynamics of complex, condensed-phase systems at the molecular level. In electrolytes and ionic liquids, where physicochemical properties arise from the interplay between solvation and ionic interactions, 2DIR spectroscopy provides unique insights into intermolecular interactions and dynamical processes that are often inaccessible to conventional spectroscopies. This review highlights seminal and recent advances in understanding the behavior of these systems using 2DIR spectroscopy, with particular emphasis on spectral diffusion, vibrational relaxation, and chemical exchange dynamics. The review also describes how complementary information from the vibrational modes of solvents, salts, and external probes enables detailed characterization of ion–ion interactions, hydrogen-bonding networks, and solvation environments, providing a molecular framework of the structure and time evolution of these charged systems. Moreover, particular attention is given to the dynamics of distinct molecular moieties and to the role of specific anions, cations, and solvent environments in governing behavior on femtosecond to picosecond time scales. Finally, the review describes current challenges, including the limited availability of intrinsic vibrational reporters and experimental constraints, and key open questions in electrochemical and energy-relevant systems that remain despite an extensive number of studies in the area.
ne76deac1490b: This review offers a unified view of large-scale first-principles electronic-structure algorithms through the tension between locality and global quantum constraints. It also highlights stochastic methods, AI, and advanced-computing paradigms.

n0204b953e2c2: The incorporation of noble metals into iron oxide nanomaterials represents an effective strategy to tailor their redox and structural properties through metal-oxide interactions. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) shows that Pd significantly enhances iron reducibility. Accordingly, wavelet transform analysis of the EXAFS region further provides evidence of Fe–Pd interactions, indicating nanoscale proximity between Pd and Fe atoms. These bulk-sensitive results are complemented by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), which reveals an increased fraction of reduced Fe species at the nanoparticle near surface upon Pd incorporation. In situ grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GI-XRD) during heat treatment under H2 provides insight into the evolution of these effects, showing (i) suppression of the hematite minor phase already after Pd impregnation and (ii) magnetite major phase lattice expansion during H2 treatment, both occurring exclusively in the presence of Pd. Complementary XPS analysis indicates partial migration of Pd into the iron oxide lattice under H2 treatment, contributing to the oxide lattice expansion beyond that of iron reduction alone. Magnetic measurements reveal an overall magnetization increase upon Pd incorporation, with a nonlinear dependence on Pd loading reflecting the balance between enhanced iron reducibility and lattice disorder. Finally, Ag incorporation slightly increases the fraction of reduced Fe species but strongly alters the magnetic response, consistent with an additional bimetallic perturbation arising from Pd–Ag coexistence.

nc5a177fd0583: Terrestrial electrochemical design implicitly relies on Earth-bound physics, such as gravity and natural convection. nbbc8c425d33b: Weak interlayer coupling, originating from electron interactions of adjacent layers, can provide promising prospects for two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), which can be respectively evaluated by energy criteria qualitatively and by band-gap transformation and band-shifting ratios quantitatively. nd0b03b2e60f4: Point defects govern the properties of complex oxides, yet they are hard to control precisely. nacf5a46e6957: Mechanically generated radicals are often considered detrimental in materials. ncc10780a8982: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. Here, Zn single-crystal electrodes exposing well-defined (002), (100), and (101) crystalline facets were used to isolate the role of crystallography in Zn metal cycling. Zn deposition is strongly facet-dependent, forming hexagonal, rectangular/prismatic, and corner-defined morphologies on (002), (100), and (101) facets, respectively. Time-dependent SEM further reveals that Zn growth proceeds via discrete edge- or corner-initiated crystallographic units rather than uniform terrace coverage. During stripping, Zn metal is removed via facet-preserved mesoscopic dissolution domains, leaving geometry-defined pits rather than random corrosion-like features. However, these pits are not preferentially refilled during subsequent plating. Repeated cycling redirects Zn growth to protrusions and roughened regions, causing mossy/dendritic accumulation, mixed-texture evolution, and loss of epitaxial reversibility. These findings highlight the need to control both oriented deposition and poststripping surface reconstruction.
n2e01c45604e0: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, yet its practical deployment is limited by trade-offs among activity, stability, and precursor cost of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. In PEMWE, Ir10Ru65Ni25 delivered 3.90 A cm–2 at 1.8 V and stable operation for 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2, demonstrating SDL-driven discovery of multimetallic OER catalysts.
nd3add93a99bc: Polymer coatings are widely used to stabilize silicon anodes, yet repeated volume changes can fracture the coating and accelerate continuous SEI reconstruction. Consequently, SiOx-P(HFBA+MPS)||Li cells deliver 73.5% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 800 mA g–1. A practical 1.5 Ah NCM811||Si/C/Gr-P(HFBA+MPS) pouch cell achieves 71.9% capacity retention after 300 cycles and shows improved thermal safety. This work provides a scalable strategy for durable and safe silicon-based batteries by integrating autonomous self-healing of the polymer coating with sustained fluorine-assisted interphase stabilization.

nd7bb92b5f0b0: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. n7217e9742006: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. n36c28ff1dc93: Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.
n20dda3652070: The palmierite oxides are a promising family of ion conductors, and understanding how compositional modification affects their structure and, in turn, their ionic conductivity is pivotal for unlocking high ionic conductivity in these solid electrolytes. Here, we investigate the Sr3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.4), establishing a solubility limit at x = 0.2, and demonstrating that Mo-substituted compositions exhibit bulk O2– conductivity approximately 2 orders of magnitude higher than the pristine composition at 600 °C.
